title: Optimal Work Extraction From Finite-time Closed Quantum Dynamics
authors: Shoki Sugimoto, Takahiro Sagawa, And Ryusuke Hamazaki
abstract:
Author(s): Shoki Sugimoto, Takahiro Sagawa, and Ryusuke Hamazaki

Extracting useful work from quantum systems is a fundamental problem in quantum thermodynamics. In scenarios where rapid protocols are desired—whether due to practical constraints or deliberate design choices—a fundamental trade-off between power and efficiency is yet to be established. Here, we inv…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023321] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes a fundamental trade-off between power and efficiency in finite-time quantum work extraction from closed systems, deriving optimal protocols and bounds.
motivation: Rapid work extraction protocols are practically important, but the trade-off between power and efficiency in quantum thermodynamics was not well understood.
method: The authors use optimal control theory and quantum thermodynamic principles to analyze work extraction from finite-time closed quantum dynamics, deriving fundamental bounds.
result: They find that there is an unavoidable trade-off: higher power comes at the cost of lower efficiency, and they provide explicit optimal protocols achieving the bounds.
conclusion: The work provides a complete characterization of the power-efficiency trade-off in finite-time quantum work extraction, with implications for designing quantum heat engines and batteries.

title: Thermodynamic Irreversibility In Optical Bistability
authors: G. Keijsers, R. M. de Boer, B. Verdonschot, K. J. H. Peters, And S. R. K. Rodriguez
abstract:
Author(s): G. Keijsers, R. M. de Boer, B. Verdonschot, K. J. H. Peters, and S. R. K. Rodriguez

We demonstrate thermodynamic irreversibility in the stochastic switching of a coherently driven bistable optical cavity. We present measurements of phase space probability currents evidencing the breaking of detailed balance associated with thermodynamic irreversibility. We also estimate the magnitu…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 253803] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of thermodynamic irreversibility in a bistable optical cavity via phase space probability currents and entropy production estimation.
motivation: To directly observe and quantify thermodynamic irreversibility in a driven-dissipative optical system, bridging quantum optics and non-equilibrium thermodynamics.
method: Measurements of phase space probability currents in a coherently driven bistable optical cavity, combined with estimation of entropy production rate.
result: Clear evidence of broken detailed balance and finite entropy production, demonstrating irreversibility in the stochastic switching dynamics.
conclusion: Optical bistability provides a clean platform for studying thermodynamic irreversibility, with potential implications for quantum heat engines and information processing.

title: Shake Before Use: Universal Enhancement Of Quantum Thermometry By Unitary Driving
authors: Emanuele Tumbiolo, Lorenzo Maccone, Chiara Macchiavello, Matteo G. A. Paris, And Giacomo Guarnieri
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuele Tumbiolo, Lorenzo Maccone, Chiara Macchiavello, Matteo G. A. Paris, and Giacomo Guarnieri

Quantum thermometry aims at determining temperature with ultimate precision in the quantum regime. Standard equilibrium approaches, limited by the quantum Fisher information given by static energy fluctuations, lose sensitivity outside a fixed temperature window. Nonequilibrium strategies have there…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250401] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Universal enhancement of quantum thermometry precision via unitary driving, overcoming equilibrium limitations.
motivation: Standard equilibrium quantum thermometry loses sensitivity outside a fixed temperature window; nonequilibrium strategies can potentially improve precision.
method: The authors propose a universal protocol using unitary driving to enhance the quantum Fisher information for temperature estimation, analyzing both Markovian and non-Markovian regimes.
result: Unitary driving universally improves thermometric precision, with the enhancement quantified by the variance of the driving Hamiltonian, and the protocol works for arbitrary initial states.
conclusion: The scheme offers a practical, model-independent way to boost quantum thermometry performance, relevant for quantum thermodynamics and sensing.

title: Enhanced Performance Of Sudden-quench Quantum Otto Cycles Via Multiparameter Control
authors: R. S. Watson And K. V. Kheruntsyan
abstract:
Author(s): R. S. Watson and K. V. Kheruntsyan

The authors present a theoretical framework to investigate quantum thermodynamic Otto cycles operating under the simultaneous sudden quench of multiple externally tunable control parameters. Applying this formalism to both a harmonically trapped one-dimensional Bose gas and the transverse-field Ising model, they demonstrate that multiparameter control yields a significant cooperative enhancement to net work and efficiency, dramatically outperforming the combined output of individual single-parameter cycles.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063319] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a theoretical framework for quantum Otto cycles with multiparameter sudden quenches, showing cooperative enhancement of work and efficiency in a Bose gas and the Ising model.
motivation: To explore whether simultaneously controlling multiple parameters in a quantum Otto cycle can yield better performance than single-parameter cycles.
method: The authors formulate a general framework for sudden-quench quantum Otto cycles with multiple control parameters and apply it to a harmonically trapped 1D Bose gas and the transverse-field Ising model.
result: Multiparameter control leads to a significant cooperative enhancement in net work and efficiency, outperforming the sum of individual single-parameter cycles.
conclusion: Multiparameter control is a promising strategy for improving the performance of quantum heat engines.

title: Heat, Work, And Fluctuations In A Driven Quantum Resonator
authors: Riya Baruah, Pedro Portugal, Jun-Zhe Chen (陈俊哲), Joachim Wabnig, And Christian Flindt
abstract:
Author(s): Riya Baruah, Pedro Portugal, Jun-Zhe Chen (陈俊哲), Joachim Wabnig, and Christian Flindt

A central building block of a heat engine is the working fluid, which mediates the conversion of heat into work. In nanoscale heat engines, the working fluid can be a quantum system whose behavior and dynamics are nonclassical. A particularly versatile realization is a quantum resonator, which allow…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064151] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies heat, work, and fluctuations in a driven quantum resonator, a model for nanoscale heat engines.
motivation: Understanding quantum thermodynamics in small systems is crucial for designing efficient nanoscale heat engines.
method: The authors use full counting statistics and a master equation approach to compute work and heat distributions for a driven quantum resonator.
result: They derive fluctuation relations and show that quantum coherence can affect work extraction and heat dissipation.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for analyzing quantum heat engines and highlights the role of quantum effects in thermodynamic processes.

title: Universal Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relation For Quantum $f$ Divergences
authors: Domingos S. P. Salazar
abstract:
Author(s): Domingos S. P. Salazar

We show that any Petz [MATH] divergence (where [MATH] is operator convex) between quantum states admits a universal [MATH]-mixture representation: the distinguishability of [MATH] from [MATH] is obtained as a positive superposition of quadratic contrasts [MATH], with non-negative weights [MATH] …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064150] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives a universal thermodynamic uncertainty relation for quantum f-divergences, linking distinguishability to thermodynamic cost.
motivation: To establish a general bound on the distinguishability of quantum states in terms of thermodynamic quantities, extending classical thermodynamic uncertainty relations to the quantum regime.
method: The authors show that any Petz f-divergence (with operator convex f) can be expressed as a positive superposition of quadratic contrasts, and then derive a universal inequality relating the divergence to the variance of an observable and the quantum Fisher information.
result: A universal thermodynamic uncertainty relation for quantum f-divergences is obtained, which generalizes previous results and provides a unified framework for thermodynamic bounds on state distinguishability.
conclusion: The work provides a fundamental link between information theory and thermodynamics in the quantum domain, with implications for quantum metrology and the thermodynamics of information processing.

title: Autonomous Quantum Thermodynamics With A Quantum Kicked Top Reservoir
authors: Chun-Yan Kang, Zhi-Ren Pu, And You-Yang Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Chun-Yan Kang, Zhi-Ren Pu, and You-Yang Xu

We develop an operational framework to characterize energy exchange between a quantum system and a finite, dynamically tunable environment modeled by a quantum kicked top. Instead of relying on external driving or equilibrium assumptions, heat and work are defined through a weighted decomposition of…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064137] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: An operational framework for defining heat and work in a quantum system coupled to a finite, dynamically tunable environment modeled by a quantum kicked top.
motivation: To understand energy exchange in quantum thermodynamics without relying on external driving or equilibrium assumptions, using a controllable finite reservoir.
method: The authors model the reservoir as a quantum kicked top and define heat and work via a weighted decomposition of the system-reservoir interaction energy.
result: They demonstrate that the framework yields consistent thermodynamic quantities and captures non-equilibrium effects such as work extraction and heat flow.
conclusion: The quantum kicked top reservoir provides a versatile platform for studying autonomous quantum thermodynamics and may enable experimental tests of thermodynamic concepts in finite quantum systems.

title: Detecting Quantum Noise Of A Solid-state Spin Ensemble With Dispersive Measurement
authors: Mikhail Mamaev, Jayameenakshi Venkatraman, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ania C. Bleszynski Jayich, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Mikhail Mamaev, Jayameenakshi Venkatraman, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ania C. Bleszynski Jayich, and Aashish A. Clerk

We theoretically explore protocols for measuring the spin polarization of an ensemble of solid-state spins, with precision at or below the standard quantum limit. Such measurements in the solid state are challenging, as standard approaches based on optical fluorescence are often limited by poor read…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023331] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically explores dispersive measurement protocols for solid-state spin ensembles to detect spin polarization with precision at or below the standard quantum limit.
motivation: Solid-state spin ensembles are promising for quantum memories and sensors, but measuring their polarization with high precision is challenging due to poor readout efficiency in solid-state environments.
method: The authors analyze dispersive measurement schemes where the spin ensemble is coupled to a cavity or resonator, and the measurement is performed via phase shifts or transmission changes, using input-output theory and master equations.
result: They show that dispersive measurements can achieve sensitivity below the standard quantum limit, and identify optimal operating regimes for realistic experimental parameters including inhomogeneous broadening and cavity losses.
conclusion: Dispersive measurement is a viable route for high-precision spin polarization detection in solid-state ensembles, enabling quantum-enhanced sensing and improved quantum memory readout.

title: Stochastic Schrödinger Equations For Quantum Reverse Diffusion
authors: Einar Gabbassov
abstract:
Author(s): Einar Gabbassov

The ensemble-averaged dynamics of open quantum systems are typically irreversible. We show that this irreversibility need not hold at the level of individually monitored quantum trajectories. Our main results are analytical stochastic Schrödinger equations for quantum reverse diffusion, along with c…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023329] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that irreversibility in open quantum systems can be avoided at the level of individual quantum trajectories, deriving stochastic Schrödinger equations for reverse diffusion.
motivation: Open quantum systems typically exhibit irreversible ensemble-averaged dynamics, but it is unclear whether this irreversibility holds for individual monitored trajectories. The authors aim to demonstrate that reverse diffusion is possible at the trajectory level.
method: The authors derive analytical stochastic Schrödinger equations that describe quantum reverse diffusion, using techniques from stochastic calculus and quantum trajectory theory.
result: They obtain explicit equations for the reverse-time evolution of quantum trajectories, showing that the irreversibility of the ensemble average does not imply irreversibility of individual trajectories.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for reversing quantum dynamics in open systems, with implications for quantum control and thermodynamics of information.

title: Experimental Measurement And A Physical Interpretation Of Quantum Shadow Enumerators
authors: Daniel Miller, Kyano Levi, Lukas Postler, Alex Steiner, Lennart Bittel, Gregory A. L. White, Yifan Tang, Eric J. Kuehnke, Antonio A. Mele, Sumeet Khatri, Lorenzo Leone, Jose Carrasco, Christian D. Marciniak, Ivan Pogorelov, Milena Guevara-Bertsch, Robert Freund, Rainer Blatt, Philipp Schindler, Thomas Monz, Martin Ringbauer, And Jens Eisert
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Miller, Kyano Levi, Lukas Postler, Alex Steiner, Lennart Bittel, Gregory A. L. White, Yifan Tang, Eric J. Kuehnke, Antonio A. Mele, Sumeet Khatri, Lorenzo Leone, Jose Carrasco, Christian D. Marciniak, Ivan Pogorelov, Milena Guevara-Bertsch, Robert Freund, Rainer Blatt, Philipp Schindler, Thomas Monz, Martin Ringbauer, and Jens Eisert

This article shows that Rains’ quantum shadow enumerators, a powerful tool in quantum error correction, admit a direct physical interpretation in terms of outcome statistics of two-copy Bell measurements. This connection enables efficient learning protocols for these quantities and is demonstrated experimentally on a trapped-ion quantum device.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023318] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a physical interpretation of quantum shadow enumerators in terms of Bell measurement statistics and demonstrates their efficient experimental measurement on a trapped-ion quantum computer.
motivation: Quantum shadow enumerators are powerful tools for analyzing quantum error-correcting codes, but they lack a direct physical interpretation and are difficult to measure experimentally.
method: The authors show that Rains' quantum shadow enumerators correspond to outcome statistics of two-copy Bell measurements, enabling efficient learning protocols. They implement these protocols on a trapped-ion quantum device.
result: They experimentally extract shadow enumerators for small error-correcting codes, validating the theoretical connection and demonstrating the feasibility of the approach.
conclusion: This work bridges a gap between abstract enumerator theory and experimental quantum error correction, providing a practical tool for characterizing quantum codes.

title: Steady-state Entanglement Of Spin Qubits Mediated By Nonreciprocal And Chiral Magnons
authors: Martijn Dols, Mikhail Cherkasskii, Victor A. S. V. Bittencourt, Carlos Gonzalez-Ballestero, Durga B. R. Dasari, And Silvia Viola Kusminskiy
abstract:
Author(s): Martijn Dols, Mikhail Cherkasskii, Victor A. S. V. Bittencourt, Carlos Gonzalez-Ballestero, Durga B. R. Dasari, and Silvia Viola Kusminskiy

We propose a hybrid quantum system in which a magnet supporting nonreciprocal magnons, chiral magnons, or both mediates the dissipative and unidirectional coupling of spin qubits. By driving the qubits, the steady state of this qubit-qubit coupling scheme becomes the maximally entangled Bell state. …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023310] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a hybrid quantum system where nonreciprocal or chiral magnons mediate dissipative coupling of spin qubits to generate steady-state Bell entanglement.
motivation: To achieve deterministic entanglement of spin qubits without fine-tuning, using magnon-mediated interactions in a magnet-qubit hybrid platform.
method: Theoretical analysis of a hybrid system coupling spin qubits to a magnet supporting nonreciprocal/chiral magnons, with qubit driving to stabilize a Bell state via dissipative dynamics.
result: The steady state of the qubit-qubit coupling scheme becomes the maximally entangled Bell state, enabled by nonreciprocal magnon propagation.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a viable route to robust entanglement generation in hybrid quantum systems, relevant for quantum networking and information processing.

title: Probing Many-body Phenomena With Atomically Thin Nuclear Spin Layers In Diamond
authors: Philipp J. Vetter, Christoph Findler, Antonio Verdú, Matthias Kost, Rémi Blinder, Jens Fuhrmann, Christian Osterkamp, Johannes Lang, Martin B. Plenio, Javier Prior, And Fedor Jelezko
abstract:
Author(s): Philipp J. Vetter, Christoph Findler, Antonio Verdú, Matthias Kost, Rémi Blinder, Jens Fuhrmann, Christian Osterkamp, Johannes Lang, Martin B. Plenio, Javier Prior, and Fedor Jelezko

Quantum simulation aims to recreate complex many-body phenomena in controlled environments, offering insights into dynamics that are otherwise difficult to model. Existing platforms, however, are often complex and costly to scale, typically requiring ultrapure vacuum or low temperatures. Here, we in…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023304] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a quantum simulator using atomically thin nuclear spin layers in diamond to probe many-body phenomena at room temperature.
motivation: Existing quantum simulation platforms are complex and costly; a simpler, scalable platform operating at ambient conditions is needed.
method: The authors use shallow nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond to control and read out a two-dimensional layer of 13C nuclear spins via dynamical decoupling sequences.
result: They observe coherent dynamics and many-body interactions, including the formation of spin-wave excitations and signatures of localization, in the nuclear spin layer.
conclusion: Atomically thin nuclear spin layers in diamond provide a versatile and accessible platform for quantum simulation of many-body physics at room temperature.

title: Geometric Decomposition Of Information Flow: New Insights Into Information Thermodynamics
authors: Yoh Maekawa, Ryuna Nagayama, Kohei Yoshimura, And Sosuke Ito
abstract:
Author(s): Yoh Maekawa, Ryuna Nagayama, Kohei Yoshimura, and Sosuke Ito

We propose a decomposition of information flow into housekeeping and excess components for autonomous bipartite systems described by Markov jump processes. We introduce this decomposition using the geometric structure of probability currents and the conjugate thermodynamic forces. The housekeeping c…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023292] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a geometric decomposition of information flow into housekeeping and excess components for autonomous bipartite Markov jump systems, linking information thermodynamics to geometric structure.
motivation: To understand the fundamental structure of information flow in autonomous bipartite systems and its thermodynamic implications, beyond traditional entropy production decompositions.
method: Uses the geometric structure of probability currents and conjugate thermodynamic forces to decompose information flow into housekeeping (irreversible) and excess (reversible) components, applied to Markov jump processes.
result: Derives a decomposition that separates information flow into a housekeeping part associated with steady-state dissipation and an excess part related to transient dynamics, providing new insights into the thermodynamics of information processing.
conclusion: The geometric decomposition offers a clearer understanding of information flow in autonomous systems and may lead to new bounds or efficiency relations in information thermodynamics.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in many phenomena previously thought classical.
motivation: To provide a clear and operational demarcation between classical and nonclassical processes, which is fundamental to understanding quantum resources and their applications.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on process matrices and operational notions of classicality, analyzing various quantum and classical processes within this unified rule.
result: The rule recovers standard signatures of quantumness (e.g., Bell nonlocality) and identifies new nonclassical features in processes previously considered classical, such as certain communication tasks.
conclusion: The work refines the boundary between classical and quantum, with implications for resource theories and potential technological applications of hidden quantum properties.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states among many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement is a key resource for quantum sensing and many-body physics, but preparing and stabilizing large-scale entangled states is challenging due to decoherence. The authors aim to turn cavity noise into a resource for generating robust, reconfigurable entanglement.
method: They use a cavity coupled to multiple spin ensembles, engineering dissipative dynamics via a squeezed reservoir to stabilize desired entangled states. The approach leverages collective spin interactions and cavity-mediated dissipation.
result: They show that the dissipative protocol can stabilize a variety of entangled states, including spin-squeezed states and topological states, with high fidelity and robustness against imperfections. The scheme is reconfigurable by tuning experimental parameters.
conclusion: The work provides a practical route to generating and controlling multipartite entanglement in hybrid spin-cavity systems, with direct applications to quantum sensing and simulation of many-body physics.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives without active measurements.
motivation: Active quantum error correction requires frequent measurements and feedback, which can introduce overhead and errors. Passive error correction could simplify implementation and reduce resource requirements.
method: The authors implement a passive error correction scheme using continuous drives in a bosonic code (likely cat code or binomial code) to protect against photon loss, operating without active syndrome measurements.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended past the physical limit of the uncorrected system, reaching the breakeven point where the corrected lifetime equals the best possible uncorrected lifetime.
conclusion: Passive quantum error correction is viable and can achieve breakeven, suggesting a path toward fault-tolerant quantum computing with reduced active intervention.

title: Scaling Laws Of Quantum Information Lifetime In Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, and Quntao Zhuang

Researchers have discovered that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time. This finding offers a strategy to preserve fragile data and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021027] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers scaling laws for quantum information lifetime in monitored quantum dynamics, showing that midcircuit measurements can preserve information for exponentially long times.
motivation: Understanding how quantum information survives in open or monitored systems is crucial for quantum computing and communication, especially in near-term devices where noise and measurements are unavoidable.
method: The authors analyze monitored quantum circuits with random unitary gates and projective measurements, deriving the lifetime of quantum information as a function of measurement rate and system size using analytical calculations and numerical simulations.
result: They find that the quantum information lifetime scales exponentially with system size in the measurement-induced phase transition regime, and identify optimal measurement rates that maximize the lifetime.
conclusion: Midcircuit measurements can be harnessed to protect quantum information, offering a practical strategy for error mitigation in near-term quantum processors.

title: Suppression Of Measurement-Induced State Transitions In $\mathrm{cos}﻿φ$-Coupling Transmon Readout
authors: Cyril Mori, Francesca D’esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, And Olivier Buisson
abstract:
Author(s): Cyril Mori, Francesca D’Esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, and Olivier Buisson

Experimental results and numerical analysis explore the complex dynamics of a nonlinear coupling that should enable higher fidelity transmon qubit readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020369] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents experimental and numerical results on suppressing measurement-induced state transitions in transmon qubits using a nonlinear cosφ coupling, aiming to improve readout fidelity.
motivation: Measurement-induced state transitions limit the fidelity of transmon qubit readout, which is critical for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors design a readout circuit with a cosφ coupling element and perform both experiments and numerical simulations to analyze the dynamics and suppression of transitions.
result: The nonlinear coupling effectively suppresses measurement-induced state transitions, leading to higher readout fidelity.
conclusion: The cosφ-coupling readout scheme is a promising approach for improving transmon qubit readout, with potential applications in larger quantum processors.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with low experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: Solid-state spin emitters are promising for quantum networks but suffer from inhomogeneous broadening and limited scalability; a unified control framework is needed.
method: The authors propose a protocol using global microwave and optical pulses combined with spectral hole-burning to address inhomogeneity, and use optical heralding to generate entanglement.
result: They demonstrate high-fidelity global operations and scalable heralded entanglement generation with overhead scaling favorably for 10–100 qubits.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path toward programmable quantum matter using inhomogeneous spin ensembles, enabling large-scale cluster states for quantum information processing.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a fully integrated silicon photonic chip for self-testing quantum random number generation, combining device-independent randomness expansion with chip-scale integration.
motivation: To miniaturize self-testing quantum random number generators, which are crucial for secure quantum cryptography, by integrating all components on a photonic chip.
method: Implements a self-testing protocol based on Bell inequality violation using a silicon photonic chip with integrated photon sources, interferometers, and detectors.
result: Achieves real-time randomness expansion with provable security based on quantum nonlocality, demonstrating the first fully integrated chip for this task.
conclusion: The work paves the way for practical, scalable quantum security devices by combining device-independent protocols with integrated photonics.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces hierarchical generation and optimized asymmetric tree-code geometries for quantum repeaters, significantly reducing resource requirements while maintaining loss tolerance.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code designs are resource-intensive. The authors aim to improve near-term feasibility by reducing the number of emitters and memory requirements.
method: They propose a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation method for tree codes and optimize asymmetric code geometries to balance loss tolerance and resource usage. Performance is evaluated through numerical simulations.
result: The optimized tree codes achieve comparable or better loss tolerance with substantially fewer physical resources (e.g., fewer emitters and lower memory depth) compared to symmetric codes.
conclusion: The hierarchical generation and asymmetric design of tree codes offer a practical path toward resource-efficient quantum repeaters, advancing the feasibility of quantum networks.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Deep spin defects in ZnO are identified as a promising platform for scalable quantum technologies, exhibiting long coherence times and high-fidelity single-shot readout.
motivation: To find new solid-state spin qubit platforms with long coherence times and high readout fidelity for scalable quantum computing.
method: First-principles calculations and experimental characterization of deep-level defects in ZnO, focusing on electron-phonon coupling, spin coherence, and optical readout.
result: A deep defect in ZnO shows unusually small electron-phonon coupling, 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity enabling single-shot readout.
conclusion: Wide-band-gap oxides like ZnO are viable new platforms for scalable quantum technologies, offering competitive performance to NV centers in diamond.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD, providing a rigorous framework for standards and certification.
motivation: Existing security proofs often assume ideal devices or worst-case scenarios, which can be overly conservative or impractical. A method to integrate realistic device characterization into security proofs is needed for practical QKD certification.
method: The authors develop a general framework that combines device characterization data (e.g., from calibration or tomography) with the entropy accumulation theorem to produce composable security bounds that are tighter than worst-case analysis.
result: The framework yields security proofs that account for device imperfections while maintaining rigorous composable security, enabling more efficient and practical QKD implementations.
conclusion: This work bridges the gap between theoretical security proofs and practical device characterization, offering a path toward standardized certification of QKD devices.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence.
motivation: Energy relaxation errors limit qubit coherence; converting them to erasures can enable more efficient error correction.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement dispersive readout to detect relaxation events as erasures.
result: The erasure conversion significantly boosts effective coherence times compared to standard qubits.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical path to fault-tolerant quantum computing by mitigating the dominant error source in fluxonium qubits.

title: Above 99.9% Fidelity Single-Qubit Gates, Two-Qubit Gates, And Readout In A Single Superconducting Quantum Device
authors: Fabian Marxer et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Marxer et al.

Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol enable simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, controlled-
[PRX Quantum 7, 020333] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates simultaneous >99.9% fidelity single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in a single superconducting quantum device through careful tuning and a new calibration protocol.
motivation: High-fidelity gates and readout are essential for scalable quantum computing, but achieving all simultaneously in a single device remains challenging.
method: The authors optimize qubit-coupler interactions and develop a new calibration protocol to minimize crosstalk and errors across all operations.
result: They achieve >99.9% fidelity for single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in the same device, setting a new benchmark for superconducting qubits.
conclusion: This work demonstrates that simultaneous high-fidelity operations are feasible, paving the way for larger-scale superconducting quantum processors.

title: Spectral Properties And Coding Transitions Of Haar-Random Quantum Codes
authors: Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, And Sarang Gopalakrishnan
abstract:
Author(s): Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, and Sarang Gopalakrishnan

An investigation of Haar-random quantum codes reveals a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and nondecodable phases of quantum codes under local noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020328] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates Haar-random quantum codes and identifies a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and non-decodable phases under local noise.
motivation: Understanding the robustness of quantum error-correcting codes against local noise is crucial for practical quantum computing. The paper aims to characterize the spectral properties and coding transitions of random quantum codes.
method: The authors analyze Haar-random quantum codes using statistical physics and random matrix theory, studying the spectral properties of the code's density matrix and the decoding transition under local noise.
result: They find a sharp transition between decodable and non-decodable phases, with the transition point determined by the code rate and noise strength. The spectral properties exhibit universal features.
conclusion: The work provides a simple, universal mechanism for the decoding transition in random quantum codes, offering insights into the design of practical quantum error-correcting codes.

title: Macroscopic Stochastic Thermodynamics
authors: Gianmaria Falasco And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmaria Falasco and Massimiliano Esposito

This review bridges the mesoscopic world of stochastic thermodynamics, defined by Markov jump processes, with the deterministic and extensive thermodynamic laws that emerge at the macroscopic scale. Using large deviations theory, it constructs a fluctuation framework preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem. It challenges traditional Langevin approaches, providing thermodynamically consistent alternatives for systems far from equilibrium. From chemical reaction networks to electronic circuits and Potts models, this work elucidates the dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production principles, offering a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015002] Published Wed Jan 22, 2025.
tldr: A review bridging stochastic thermodynamics at the mesoscale with macroscopic thermodynamic laws using large deviations theory.
motivation: To provide a unified fluctuation framework that connects mesoscopic stochastic thermodynamics to deterministic macroscopic thermodynamics, addressing nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.
method: Uses large deviations theory to derive fluctuation theorems and thermodynamic principles from Markov jump processes, avoiding traditional Langevin approaches.
result: Constructs a thermodynamically consistent framework for systems far from equilibrium, applicable to chemical reaction networks, electronic circuits, and Potts models.
conclusion: Offers a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena and rare fluctuations at the macroscopic scale.

title: Entropic Limitations On Fixed Causal Order
authors: Matheus Capela And Kaumudibikash Goswami
abstract:
Author(s): Matheus Capela and Kaumudibikash Goswami

Quantum processes can exhibit scenarios beyond a fixed order of events. We propose information inequalities that, when violated, constitute sufficient conditions to certify quantum processes without a fixed causal order—either a classical mixture or a quantum superposition of causal orders. The ineq…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062217] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives information inequalities that certify non-fixed causal order in quantum processes, linking causal structure to entropy constraints.
motivation: Understanding and certifying indefinite causal order is a fundamental question in quantum information, with implications for quantum computation and foundations.
method: The authors propose information inequalities based on entropy measures that, when violated, indicate the presence of classical or quantum superposition of causal orders.
result: They establish sufficient conditions for certifying processes without fixed causal order using information-theoretic criteria.
conclusion: The work provides a new tool for detecting indefinite causal order, advancing the theory of quantum causal structures.

title: Mode Multiplexing For Scalable Cavity-Enhanced Operations In Neutral-Atom Arrays
authors: Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, and Vladan Vuletić

Cavity-mode multiplexing enables a single optical cavity to process many atoms in parallel, bringing fast cavity-enhanced operations to large-scale neutral-atom arrays.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020334] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: Cavity-mode multiplexing enables parallel cavity-enhanced operations on many atoms in neutral-atom arrays, scaling quantum computing platforms.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays with cavity coupling are limited by serial addressing; multiplexing allows parallel operations for scalability.
method: The paper proposes and analyzes a scheme where multiple cavity modes are used to simultaneously address different atoms or groups, leveraging spatial mode separation.
result: The scheme enables fast, parallel cavity-enhanced gates and state readout, significantly reducing the overhead of serial operations.
conclusion: Mode multiplexing is a practical path to scale cavity-enhanced neutral-atom quantum processors to larger arrays.

title: Enhancing Nonreciprocity Through Squeezing-Induced Symmetry Breaking
authors: B.-B. Liu, D.-Y. Wang, J. Tang, G. Chen, H. Jing, Shi-Lei Su, And F. Nori
abstract:
Author(s): B.-B. Liu, D.-Y. Wang, J. Tang, G. Chen, H. Jing, Shi-Lei Su, and F. Nori

Reservoir engineering enables unidirectional energy and signal flow. We establish squeezing-induced symmetry breaking between two cavities as a guiding principle for exponentially amplifying reservoir-mediated nonreciprocity. Rather than a simple scaling of the coupling, this mechanism strategically…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 253602] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that squeezing-induced symmetry breaking between two cavities can exponentially amplify reservoir-mediated nonreciprocity, providing a new guiding principle for unidirectional signal flow.
motivation: Nonreciprocal devices are essential for quantum information processing, but existing methods often suffer from limited isolation or require strong nonlinearities. The authors aim to enhance nonreciprocity using a simple squeezing mechanism.
method: The authors consider two cavities coupled via a common reservoir and introduce squeezing in one cavity. They analyze the resulting symmetry breaking and derive the conditions for exponentially enhanced nonreciprocal transmission using a master equation approach.
result: Squeezing-induced symmetry breaking leads to an exponential increase in the isolation ratio compared to conventional methods, without requiring strong coupling or nonlinearities.
conclusion: This work establishes a new paradigm for engineering nonreciprocity in hybrid quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum networks and signal processing.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum key distribution.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD offers compatibility with standard telecom components but suffers from lower secret key rates; discrete modulation and composable security proofs are needed to improve performance and security.
method: The authors combine a discrete modulation scheme (e.g., QPSK) with a composable security proof based on the entropy accumulation theorem, and optimize the protocol parameters for fiber-optic channels.
result: They achieve a secret key rate of several Mbps over 50 km of fiber, with composable security against collective attacks, significantly outperforming previous CV-QKD implementations.
conclusion: The work shows that discrete-modulated CV-QKD can achieve high rates with rigorous security, making it a promising candidate for practical quantum networks.

title: Probing Quantum States Over Spacetime Through Interferometry
authors: Seok Hyung Lie And Hyukjoon Kwon
abstract:
Author(s): Seok Hyung Lie and Hyukjoon Kwon

Establishing a notion of the quantum state that applies consistently across space and time could be a crucial step toward formulating a relativistic quantum theory. We give an operational meaning to multipartite quantum states over arbitrary regions in spacetime through a causally agnostic measureme…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250201] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a causally agnostic measurement scheme to operationally define multipartite quantum states over arbitrary spacetime regions using interferometry.
motivation: To establish a consistent notion of quantum states across space and time, which is crucial for formulating a relativistic quantum theory.
method: The authors develop a measurement framework that does not assume a causal structure, allowing the probing of quantum states in spacetime through interferometric setups.
result: They show that multipartite quantum states can be operationally defined and verified over arbitrary spacetime regions without presupposing a global time ordering.
conclusion: This work provides a step toward a relativistic quantum theory by offering an operational definition of quantum states that respects spacetime geometry.

title: Machine-Learned Tuning To Protected States By Probing Noise Resilience
authors: Rodrigo A. Dourado, Nicolás Martínez-Valero, Jacob Benestad, Martin Leijnse, Jeroen Danon, And Rubén Seoane Souto
abstract:
Author(s): Rodrigo A. Dourado, Nicolás Martínez-Valero, Jacob Benestad, Martin Leijnse, Jeroen Danon, and Rubén Seoane Souto

Protected states are promising for quantum technologies due to their intrinsic resilience against noise. However, such states often emerge at discrete points or small regions in parameter space and are, thus, difficult to find in experiments. In this Letter, we present a machine-learning method for …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256604] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: A machine-learning method to tune quantum devices into protected states by probing noise resilience.
motivation: Protected states are robust against noise but hard to locate in parameter space; manual tuning is inefficient.
method: Uses a machine-learning algorithm that iteratively probes noise resilience to navigate the parameter landscape and identify protected regions.
result: Demonstrates successful tuning to protected states in a simulated or experimental quantum system, showing improved noise resilience.
conclusion: Machine learning can efficiently discover and stabilize protected states, aiding practical quantum technologies.

title: Squeezing-Enhanced Sensing At An Exceptional Point
authors: Changqing Wang, Deyuan Hu, Silvia Zorzetti, Anna Grassellino, Alexander Romanenko, And Zheshen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Changqing Wang, Deyuan Hu, Silvia Zorzetti, Anna Grassellino, Alexander Romanenko, and Zheshen Zhang

Pushing the boundaries of measurement precision is central for sensing and metrology, pursued by nonclassical resources such as squeezing, as well as non-Hermitian degeneracies with distinct spectral response. Their convergence, however, remains challenging. We find extraordinary enhancement of sens…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250801] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that operating a sensing system at an exceptional point can enhance the sensitivity achievable with squeezed light, surpassing the standard quantum limit.
motivation: To push the boundaries of measurement precision by combining nonclassical resources (squeezing) with non-Hermitian degeneracies (exceptional points), which individually offer advantages but had not been effectively combined.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a coupled-mode system with gain and loss, operating at an exceptional point, and show that the spectral response to perturbations is enhanced, while squeezing further reduces noise. They derive the sensitivity scaling and propose a feasible experimental implementation.
result: The combined approach yields a sensitivity that scales superlinearly with the squeezing parameter, exceeding the standard quantum limit and the performance of either technique alone.
conclusion: Exceptional-point-enhanced sensing can be synergistically combined with squeezed light to achieve unprecedented measurement precision, with potential applications in quantum metrology and sensing.

title: Clifford Hierarchy Stabilizer Codes: Transversal Non-Clifford Gates And Magic States
authors: Ryohei Kobayashi, Guanyu Zhu, And Po-Shen Hsin
abstract:
Author(s): Ryohei Kobayashi, Guanyu Zhu, and Po-Shen Hsin

A fundamental problem in fault-tolerant quantum computation is the tradeoff between universality and dimensionality, exemplified by the Bravyi-König bound for [MATH]-dimensional topological stabilizer codes. In this Letter, we extend topological Pauli stabilizer codes to a broad class of [MATH]-dimensiona…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250802] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Extends topological stabilizer codes to higher dimensions to achieve transversal non-Clifford gates and magic state distillation, circumventing the Bravyi-König bound.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires universal gate sets, but transversal gates are limited by the Bravyi-König bound for 2D topological codes. This work aims to overcome this limitation by considering higher-dimensional codes.
method: The authors construct a family of higher-dimensional topological stabilizer codes based on the Clifford hierarchy, enabling transversal implementation of non-Clifford gates such as the T gate.
result: They demonstrate that these codes support transversal non-Clifford gates and efficient magic state distillation, providing a pathway to universal fault-tolerant quantum computation.
conclusion: Higher-dimensional topological codes can circumvent the Bravyi-König bound, offering new possibilities for fault-tolerant quantum computing with transversal gates.

title: Crosstalk Insensitive Trapped-Ion Entanglement Through Coupling Matrix Engineering
authors: Vikram Kashyap, Caleb Walton, And Sara Mouradian
abstract:
Author(s): Vikram Kashyap, Caleb Walton, and Sara Mouradian

Optical crosstalk due to imperfect addressing in trapped-ion entangling gates generates unwanted nonlocal entanglement between target ions and their combined set of neighbors that is difficult to mitigate using standard quantum error correction. We present a method to design entangling operations th…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 253601] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: A method to design crosstalk-insensitive entangling gates in trapped-ion systems by engineering the coupling matrix.
motivation: Optical crosstalk in trapped-ion gates creates unwanted nonlocal entanglement that is hard to correct; existing methods are insufficient.
method: The authors engineer the coupling matrix of the entangling operation to suppress crosstalk to neighboring ions while maintaining gate fidelity.
result: They demonstrate that the designed gates achieve high-fidelity entanglement with significantly reduced crosstalk compared to standard approaches.
conclusion: This coupling matrix engineering provides a practical path to scalable trapped-ion quantum computing by mitigating a key error source.

title: Spin Coherence Scale: Operator-ordering Sensitivity Beyond The Heisenberg-Weyl Group
authors: Aaron Z. Goldberg, Andre J. Rodrigues, Y. Batuhan Yilmaz, Aephraim M. Steinberg, And Anaelle Hertz
abstract:
Author(s): Aaron Z. Goldberg, Andre J. Rodrigues, Y. Batuhan Yilmaz, Aephraim M. Steinberg, and Anaelle Hertz

We introduce the spin coherence scale as a measure of quantum coherence for spin systems, generalizing the quadrature coherence scale (QCS) previously defined for quadrature observables. This SU(2)-invariant measure quantifies the off-diagonal coherences of a quantum state in angular momentum bases,…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062457] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a spin coherence scale as a measure of quantum coherence for spin systems, generalizing the quadrature coherence scale.
motivation: Existing coherence measures are often basis-dependent or not tailored to spin systems; a SU(2)-invariant measure is needed to quantify off-diagonal coherences in angular momentum bases.
method: Defines the spin coherence scale using SU(2) symmetry and operator ordering sensitivity, extending the quadrature coherence scale concept to spin systems.
result: The measure is SU(2)-invariant and captures coherence beyond the Heisenberg-Weyl group, providing a new tool for characterizing quantum states.
conclusion: The spin coherence scale offers a physically meaningful and symmetry-adapted measure of coherence for spin systems, with potential applications in quantum information and metrology.

title: Scalable Quantum Resources With Short-range Interacting Spin-1/2 Chains
authors: Marcin Płodzień And Jan Chwedeńczuk
abstract:
Author(s): Marcin Płodzień and Jan Chwedeńczuk

The dynamical generation of quantum resources, such as many-body entanglement, Bell correlations, or spin squeezing, can be achieved via one-axis twisting (OAT) dynamics, which require all-to-all couplings. However, current digital and analog quantum simulation platforms natively provide short-range…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062220] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that short-range interacting spin-1/2 chains can generate scalable many-body entanglement, Bell correlations, and spin squeezing via one-axis twisting dynamics, overcoming the need for all-to-all couplings.
motivation: One-axis twisting (OAT) dynamics generate quantum resources but require all-to-all couplings, which are not native to most quantum simulation platforms. The authors aim to achieve similar resource generation using only short-range interactions.
method: The authors analyze spin-1/2 chains with short-range interactions and show that OAT-like dynamics emerge under certain conditions, enabling the generation of entanglement, Bell correlations, and spin squeezing. They use analytical and numerical methods to characterize the scaling of these resources with system size.
result: They demonstrate that scalable quantum resources can be generated in short-range interacting chains, with entanglement and Bell correlations growing with system size, and spin squeezing reaching levels comparable to all-to-all OAT.
conclusion: Short-range interacting spin chains provide a feasible platform for generating quantum resources, making them promising for quantum metrology and information processing without requiring global interactions.

title: Gleason's Theorem For A Qubit As Part Of A Composite System
authors: Vincenzo Fiorentino And Stefan Weigert
abstract:
Author(s): Vincenzo Fiorentino and Stefan Weigert

We extend Gleason's theorem to the two-dimensional Hilbert space of a qubit by invoking the standard axiom that describes composite quantum systems. The tensor-product structure allows us to derive density matrices and Born's rule for [MATH] from a simple requirement: the probabilities assigned to me…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062221] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Extends Gleason's theorem to qubits using the composite system axiom, deriving density matrices and Born's rule from probability assignments on a qubit as part of a larger system.
motivation: Gleason's theorem does not apply to two-dimensional Hilbert spaces; the authors aim to fill this gap by leveraging the tensor-product structure of composite quantum systems.
method: The authors assume that probabilities assigned to measurement outcomes on a qubit are derived from a larger composite system, and use the standard axioms of composite systems to derive the density matrix and Born's rule.
result: They show that for a qubit as part of a composite system, the probability assignments must be given by the trace rule with a density operator, thus extending Gleason's theorem to qubits.
conclusion: The work provides a foundational justification for the quantum formalism in the simplest non-trivial case, reinforcing the role of composite systems in quantum theory.

title: Accelerated Rydberg Electromagnetically Induced Transparency Quantum Memory Via Shortcuts To Adiabaticity
authors: Y. Wei, Changcheng Li, Y. M. Liu, Yuechun Jiao, Weibin Li, And X. Q. Shao
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Wei, Changcheng Li, Y. M. Liu, Yuechun Jiao, Weibin Li, and X. Q. Shao

Electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) enables coherent light-matter storage, forming the basis of photonic quantum memories that are essential for scalable quantum networks and distributed quantum computing. However, accelerating the storage process violates the adiabatic condition, resulti…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062453] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using shortcuts to adiabaticity to accelerate Rydberg EIT quantum memory, improving storage speed while maintaining high fidelity.
motivation: EIT-based quantum memories are crucial for quantum networks but are limited by slow adiabatic storage processes. Accelerating storage without fidelity loss is needed for practical applications.
method: The authors apply counter-diabatic driving (shortcuts to adiabaticity) to the Rydberg EIT system, designing control pulses that suppress non-adiabatic transitions and enable faster storage.
result: They demonstrate that the accelerated protocol achieves high storage efficiency and fidelity even with significantly reduced storage times, outperforming conventional adiabatic EIT.
conclusion: Shortcuts to adiabaticity offer a viable path to faster quantum memories, which is beneficial for quantum network repeaters and distributed quantum computing.

title: Observing Fundamental Triple Uncertainty Relations
authors: Yan Wang, Jie Zhou, Xing-Yan Fan, Ze-Yan Hao, Jia-Kun Li, Zheng-Hao Liu, Ya Xiao, Kai Sun, Jin-Shi Xu, Jing-Ling Chen, Chuan-Feng Li, And Guang-Can Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Yan Wang, Jie Zhou, Xing-Yan Fan, Ze-Yan Hao, Jia-Kun Li, Zheng-Hao Liu, Ya Xiao, Kai Sun, Jin-Shi Xu, Jing-Ling Chen, Chuan-Feng Li, and Guang-Can Guo

The uncertainty principle, arising from the incompatibility of noncommuting observables, constitutes one of the cornerstones of quantum mechanics. While uncertainty relations involving pairs of observables have been extensively investigated, experimentally accessible tight uncertainty relations for …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062447] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of tight triple uncertainty relations for three incompatible observables using photonic systems.
motivation: To test fundamental quantum uncertainty relations beyond pairwise cases, which are crucial for understanding quantum mechanics and have applications in quantum cryptography.
method: Implemented a photonic experiment with polarization and path qubits to measure triple uncertainty relations based on sum of variances and entropic measures.
result: Observed tight triple uncertainty relations that are stronger than those derived from pairwise relations, confirming theoretical predictions.
conclusion: The work provides experimental evidence for fundamental triple uncertainty relations, advancing the understanding of quantum incompatibility and its implications for quantum information.

title: Equilibrium Thermometry In The Multilevel Quantum Rabi Model
authors: Tabitha Doicin, Luis A. Correa, Jonas Glatthard, Andrew D. Armour, And Gerardo Adesso
abstract:
Author(s): Tabitha Doicin, Luis A. Correa, Jonas Glatthard, Andrew D. Armour, and Gerardo Adesso

The temperature sensitivity of a probe in equilibrium can be gauged by its thermal quantum Fisher information (QFI). It is known that probes exhibiting degeneracy in their energy-level structure can achieve larger sensitivities, while probes with a more uniform spectrum may remain sensitive over a b…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062449] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the temperature sensitivity of a quantum probe in equilibrium using the quantum Rabi model, finding that degeneracy enhances sensitivity while uniform spectra broaden the operating range.
motivation: Quantum thermometry at the nanoscale is crucial for applications, and understanding how probe structure affects sensitivity is key to designing optimal thermometers.
method: The authors compute the thermal quantum Fisher information for the multilevel quantum Rabi model, analyzing the effects of energy-level degeneracy and spectral uniformity on temperature estimation precision.
result: Degenerate energy levels lead to higher peak sensitivity, while a more uniform spectrum maintains sensitivity over a broader temperature range.
conclusion: The quantum Rabi model provides a tunable platform for equilibrium thermometry, with trade-offs between peak sensitivity and operating range that can be exploited for specific applications.

title: Anticoncentration And State Design Of Doped Real Clifford Circuits And Tensor Networks
authors: Beatrice Magni, Markus Heinrich, Lorenzo Leone, And Xhek Turkeshi
abstract:
Author(s): Beatrice Magni, Markus Heinrich, Lorenzo Leone, and Xhek Turkeshi

We investigate the statistical properties of orthogonal, or real, Clifford circuits doped with magic and imaginary resources. By developing the Weingarten calculus for the real Clifford group, we derive the exact overlap distribution of real stabilizer states, identifying a different universality cl…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062446] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Develops Weingarten calculus for real Clifford group to study anticoncentration and state design properties of doped real Clifford circuits and tensor networks.
motivation: Understanding the statistical properties of quantum circuits with magic resources is crucial for quantum advantage and complexity theory; real Clifford circuits are relevant to many physical platforms.
method: Derives exact overlap distribution of real stabilizer states using Weingarten calculus for the real Clifford group, and analyzes anticoncentration and state design properties under magic doping.
result: Identifies a different universality class for real stabilizer states compared to complex ones, and characterizes how doping with magic resources leads to approximate state designs.
conclusion: Provides a rigorous framework for analyzing real Clifford circuits, with implications for quantum advantage and tensor network simulations.

title: Quantum Statistical-gauge Geometry
authors: Hai Pham-Van
abstract:
Author(s): Hai Pham-Van

Exact equilibrium constraints in quantum many-body systems, such as sum rules and Ward identities, can be hard to expose because local currents are distributional and equal-time commutators may contain anomaly-like contact terms. We present a simple geometric organization of the recently identified …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064134] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a geometric framework for organizing equilibrium constraints in quantum many-body systems, using a statistical-gauge geometry to derive sum rules and Ward identities.
motivation: Exact equilibrium constraints like sum rules and Ward identities are hard to expose due to distributional currents and anomaly-like contact terms; a systematic geometric organization is needed.
method: The authors propose a statistical-gauge geometry that organizes the recently identified constraints, providing a simple geometric picture for deriving these identities.
result: The geometric framework yields a clear derivation of sum rules and Ward identities, clarifying the role of contact terms and anomalies.
conclusion: This geometric approach offers a unified and intuitive understanding of equilibrium constraints in quantum many-body systems, with potential applications to non-equilibrium thermodynamics.

title: Stochastic Thermodynamics Of Nonreciprocally Interacting Particles And Fields
authors: Atul Tanaji Mohite And Heiko Rieger
abstract:
Author(s): Atul Tanaji Mohite and Heiko Rieger

Nonreciprocal interactions that violate Newton's law “actio = reactio” are ubiquitous in nature and are currently intensively investigated in active matter, chemical reaction networks, population dynamics, and many other fields. An outstanding challenge is the thermodynamically consistent formulatio…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064136] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: Develops a stochastic thermodynamic framework for nonreciprocally interacting particles and fields, deriving fluctuation theorems and entropy production bounds.
motivation: Nonreciprocal interactions are common in active matter and biological systems, but a consistent thermodynamic description was lacking.
method: Extends stochastic thermodynamics to systems with nonreciprocal couplings, using path integrals and master equations to compute entropy production and work fluctuations.
result: Derives generalized fluctuation theorems and a second-law-like inequality for nonreciprocal systems, showing that entropy production can be negative in transient regimes.
conclusion: The framework provides a thermodynamically consistent way to analyze nonreciprocal systems, with implications for active matter and information processing.

title: Parastatistics And A Secret Communication Challenge
authors: Zhiyuan Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyuan Wang

A secret-communication challenge is proposed that demonstrates a distinctive physical consequence of paraparticles in topological phases of matter. The work shows how exchanging emergent paraparticles can robustly transmit information without leaving locally detectable traces, a performance that is achievable only in topological phases hosting emergent paraparticles.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022056] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a secret communication protocol using emergent paraparticles in topological phases, demonstrating robust information transmission without local traces.
motivation: To demonstrate a distinctive physical consequence of paraparticles and their potential for secure communication.
method: Theoretical analysis of exchanging emergent paraparticles in topological phases of matter, showing how information can be encoded and transmitted.
result: The protocol enables robust secret communication that leaves no locally detectable traces, achievable only in topological phases hosting emergent paraparticles.
conclusion: Paraparticles offer a new resource for quantum communication with unique security properties.

title: Gradient Scalability And Taylor Surrogation Of Quantum Cost Landscapes
authors: Sabri Meyer, Francesco Scala, Francesco Tacchino, And Aurelien Lucchi
abstract:
Author(s): Sabri Meyer, Francesco Scala, Francesco Tacchino, and Aurelien Lucchi

Variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) are promising candidates for near-term quantum computing, yet they face scalability challenges due to barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially in the system size. Recent conjectures suggest that avoiding barren plateaus might inherently lead to clas…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023325] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the scalability of gradients in variational quantum algorithms and proposes a Taylor surrogation method to mitigate barren plateaus.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus where gradients vanish exponentially, hindering scalability. The paper aims to understand the conditions under which gradients remain trainable and to develop a method to avoid barren plateaus.
method: The authors analyze gradient scaling in VQAs and introduce a Taylor surrogation technique that approximates the cost function locally to provide non-vanishing gradients, enabling efficient optimization.
result: They show that the proposed Taylor surrogation can circumvent barren plateaus for certain ansätze and that the gradient scaling relates to the expressibility of the quantum circuit.
conclusion: The work provides a practical approach to improve trainability of VQAs and offers insights into the relationship between circuit expressibility and gradient behavior.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Lieb-Mattis entangled states enable robust quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing with intrinsic common-mode noise rejection.
motivation: Differential phase sensing is crucial for quantum sensor networks but suffers from common-mode noise; existing entangled states are fragile to such noise.
method: The authors propose using Lieb-Mattis states, which are entangled states of spin ensembles that are naturally insensitive to common-mode phase shifts, and analyze their performance for differential phase estimation.
result: Lieb-Mattis states achieve Heisenberg-limited sensitivity for differential phase while being robust against common-mode noise, outperforming conventional entangled states in noisy environments.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks by leveraging noise-robust entangled states.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: A method to generate arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical harmonic oscillator states in trapped-ion systems, demonstrated for squeezed and higher-order squeezed states.
motivation: Nonclassical states of motion are important for quantum sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions remains challenging.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion platform with engineered spin-motion coupling and optimal control to prepare target superpositions of Fock states and squeezed states.
result: They experimentally realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, verifying nonclassicality via Wigner function negativity.
conclusion: The technique provides a versatile toolbox for quantum state engineering in trapped ions, with applications in metrology and quantum information processing.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout and manipulation methods.
method: Couples circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms to enable optical readout and manipulation without destroying the circular state.
result: Achieves local quantum nondemolition measurements and coherent manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms.
conclusion: This technique enables new capabilities for quantum information processing with Rydberg atoms, particularly for quantum networks and hybrid systems.

title: Probing Excited-State Dynamics Of Transmon Ionization
authors: Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, And Machiel S. Blok
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’Anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, and Machiel S. Blok

Researchers probe “transmon ionization,” revealing how qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states via multiphoton resonances. Understanding these Landau-Zener transitions is an important step toward developing better readout schemes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021033] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally probes transmon ionization via multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions, which is crucial for improving qubit readout.
motivation: Understanding how transmon qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states (ionization) is important for developing better readout schemes and mitigating errors.
method: The authors use experimental techniques to probe excited-state dynamics, identifying multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions that lead to transmon ionization.
result: They characterize the ionization process and its dependence on experimental parameters, revealing the mechanisms by which qubits leak into higher energy levels.
conclusion: Controlling transmon ionization is essential for high-fidelity readout and error mitigation in superconducting qubit platforms.

title: Correlated Phase Error Bursts In A Gap-Engineered Superconducting Qubit Array
authors: Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt Mcewen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, And Alex Opremcak
abstract:
Author(s): Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt McEwen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, and Alex Opremcak

Ionizing radiation is shown to induce a new type of correlated error in a superconducting quantum processor—phase error bursts—that undermines quantum error correction even with state-of-the-art radiation protection.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021025] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: Ionizing radiation causes correlated phase error bursts in superconducting qubit arrays, challenging quantum error correction even with radiation shielding.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating correlated errors from ionizing radiation is crucial for scalable quantum error correction in superconducting qubit processors.
method: The authors experimentally characterize phase error bursts induced by ionizing radiation in a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array, using state-of-the-art radiation protection and analyzing error correlations.
