result: They discover a new type of correlated error—phase error bursts—that occur even with radiation shielding, undermining error correction performance.
conclusion: Radiation-induced correlated phase errors pose a significant challenge for fault-tolerant quantum computing with superconducting qubits, requiring novel mitigation strategies.

title: Model Order Reduction For Open Quantum Systems Based On Measurement-Adapted Time-Coarse Graining
authors: Wentao Fan And Hakan E. Türeci
abstract:
Author(s): Wentao Fan and Hakan E. Türeci

Researchers introduce measurement-adapted time-coarse graining, a model reduction technique that uses the time resolution of measurement channels to capture the observable dynamics of a complex quantum system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021015] Published Thu Apr 16, 2026.
tldr: A model reduction technique for open quantum systems that coarse-grains time based on measurement resolution to capture observable dynamics.
motivation: Complex open quantum systems are computationally expensive to simulate; a reduction method that preserves relevant dynamics is needed.
method: The authors introduce measurement-adapted time-coarse graining, which uses the time resolution of measurement channels to define an effective reduced model.
result: The technique accurately reproduces the observable dynamics of the original system with significantly fewer degrees of freedom.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical tool for simulating open quantum systems, bridging microscopic models and observed dynamics.

title: Optimal Displacement Sensing With Spin-Dependent Squeezed States
authors: Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, And Arghavan Safavi-Naini
abstract:
Author(s): Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, and Arghavan Safavi-Naini

Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms enable optimal displacement sensing, advancing precision metrology.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020368] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optimal displacement sensing using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms, advancing precision metrology.
motivation: Precision displacement sensing is crucial for quantum metrology and fundamental tests; trapped ions offer a clean platform for generating and exploiting spin-dependent squeezed states.
method: The authors theoretically propose and experimentally realize a protocol using spin-dependent squeezing in a trapped-ion system to achieve Heisenberg-limited displacement sensing.
result: They achieve optimal sensitivity for displacement measurements, surpassing the standard quantum limit and demonstrating the utility of spin-dependent squeezed states.
conclusion: Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped ions provide a practical route to optimal displacement sensing, with implications for quantum metrology and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces the symplectic rank as a measure of non-Gaussianity for bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimum resources needed for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable quantum information, but a unified measure of non-Gaussianity was lacking. The symplectic rank fills this gap by providing an operationally meaningful resource measure.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank based on the minimal number of Gaussian unitaries required to prepare a state from a Gaussian state, and relate it to the state's covariance matrix and Wigner function negativity. They develop theoretical tools to compute it for various state classes.
result: The symplectic rank is shown to be a monotone under Gaussian operations, and it provides tight lower bounds on the number of non-Gaussian operations needed for state preparation and compression. Examples include cat states and photon-added states.
conclusion: The symplectic rank is a powerful and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, with applications in resource theory and quantum information processing with continuous variables.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, identifying sources of decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Single-photon emitters in silicon are promising for quantum networks, but spectral instability limits their performance. Understanding the origins of decoherence is crucial for improving emitter coherence.
method: The authors study single erbium ions coupled to silicon nanophotonic cavities, performing spectroscopy and noise characterization to identify mechanisms causing spectral diffusion and linewidth broadening.
result: They identify specific noise sources, such as charge fluctuations and phonon interactions, that dominate spectral instability, and quantify their impact on emitter coherence.
conclusion: Mitigating identified noise sources can significantly improve the spectral stability of erbium emitters, advancing their use in quantum repeaters and network nodes.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, and Cristian Bonato

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, demonstrated on spin environments.
motivation: Accurate characterization of unknown spin environments is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are computationally expensive and not scalable.
method: The authors develop a variational Bayesian inference algorithm that approximates posterior distributions over models and parameters, enabling fast and scalable estimation.
result: The framework accurately identifies spin environments and supports real-time adaptive measurement strategies, outperforming standard methods in efficiency and accuracy.
conclusion: Variational Bayesian inference provides a practical tool for quantum estimation tasks, with potential applications in quantum sensing and control.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity-QED model with Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions leading to blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: To understand how kinetic constraints in cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays stabilize exotic non-equilibrium phases such as blockaded ferromagnetism and quantum scars.
method: The authors study a minimal model of cavity-coupled Rydberg atoms with long-range interactions, analyzing the interplay of cavity-mediated coupling and Rydberg blockade using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that kinetic constraints give rise to blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars, demonstrating novel non-equilibrium phenomena in a hybrid quantum system.
conclusion: The work establishes cavity-QED with Rydberg arrays as a platform for exploring kinetically constrained many-body physics and long-range quantum scars.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: An open-source pulse optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates for quantum error correction in neutral-atom platforms.
motivation: Neutral-atom quantum processors require high-fidelity multiqubit gates to implement quantum error correction codes efficiently.
method: The authors develop an open-source pulse optimization framework that designs optimal control pulses for multiqubit Rydberg gates, accounting for experimental constraints.
result: The optimized gates achieve high fidelities suitable for quantum error correction, demonstrated through numerical simulations.
conclusion: The framework provides a practical path toward fault-tolerant quantum computing with neutral atoms.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies monitored quantum circuits with random measurements and shows that measurement outcomes can improve decoding of quantum error-correcting codes.
motivation: Understanding the role of measurements in quantum error correction and fault tolerance, particularly how measurement data can aid decoding in monitored dynamics.
method: The authors analyze random quantum circuits with interspersed measurements, using statistical mechanics mappings and tensor network techniques to study decoding transitions.
result: They find that access to measurement outcomes enhances decodability, leading to new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.
conclusion: Monitored quantum codes exhibit improved error correction capabilities when measurement outcomes are used, suggesting new strategies for fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Photon Blockade Via Two-Photon Interactions
authors: Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, And Simone Felicetti
abstract:
Author(s): Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, and Simone Felicetti

Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Collective two-photon interactions in an emitter ensemble enhance photon blockade, improving antibunching and transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong single-emitter coupling, which is experimentally challenging. This work aims to achieve strong blockade using collective effects in an ensemble.
method: The authors theoretically study an ensemble of emitters with two-photon interactions, analyzing the photon statistics and transmission using a master equation approach.
result: They find that the photon blockade strengthens with system size, leading to improved antibunching and high transmission, even when individual emitters are weakly coupled.
conclusion: Collective two-photon interactions provide a scalable route to photon blockade, relevant for quantum nonlinear optics and quantum information processing.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving can speed up quantum processes but exact implementation is challenging; variational approximations often suffer from low fidelity.
method: The authors introduce a weighted action approach combined with computer algebra to optimize variational counterdiabatic protocols, enabling systematic improvement of the driving Hamiltonian.
result: The new method yields significantly higher fidelity for quantum state transfer and other control tasks compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving.
conclusion: This technique provides a practical upgrade for quantum control, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and speed limits.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
abstract:
Author(s): Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas McConkey, Vincent Arena, and Corrado Mancini

Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers break through traditional performance limits, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale processors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020344] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents nondegenerate Josephson mixers with enhanced bandwidth and saturation power for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
motivation: Large-scale quantum processors require simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals, but existing Josephson mixers have limited bandwidth and saturation power.
method: The authors design and fabricate impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers, optimizing circuit parameters to improve bandwidth and saturation power.
result: The mixers achieve significantly higher bandwidth and saturation power compared to conventional designs, enabling simultaneous amplification of multiple quantum signals.
conclusion: These enhanced mixers are promising components for quantum signal processing and transduction in large-scale superconducting quantum processors.

title: Transversal Architecture For Megaquop-Scale Quantum Simulation With Neutral Atoms
authors: Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, And Milan Kornjača
abstract:
Author(s): Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, and Milan Kornjača

Integration of a space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction architecture with neutral-atom hardware and its extension to high-rate codes yields significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020343] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a transversal architecture for fault-tolerant quantum simulation using neutral atoms, integrating small-angle rotation error correction with high-rate codes to reduce logical overhead.
motivation: Quantum simulation at the megaquop scale requires fault-tolerant architectures that minimize space and time overhead, especially for neutral-atom platforms where native gates and error correction codes must be tailored.
method: The authors design a transversal architecture that combines small-angle rotation error correction with high-rate quantum error-correcting codes, optimized for neutral-atom hardware constraints such as long-range interactions and parallel gate operations.
result: The architecture achieves significant savings in logical qubit count, physical qubit overhead, and runtime compared to standard surface-code-based approaches, enabling megaquop-scale simulations.
conclusion: Neutral-atom quantum computers can efficiently support large-scale fault-tolerant quantum simulation with practical overhead, making them a promising platform for near-term quantum advantage.

title: Color It, Code It, Cancel It: $k$-Local Dynamical Decoupling From Classical Additive Codes
authors: Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, And Stefano Bosco
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, and Stefano Bosco

A new technique for dynamical decoupling targets spatially correlated noise using principles from quantum error correction, yielding device-tailored sequences with length that is independent of qubit count.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020338] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A new dynamical decoupling technique uses classical additive codes to suppress spatially correlated noise with sequence length independent of qubit count.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling is essential for protecting quantum information from noise, but existing methods often scale poorly with system size or target only uncorrelated noise.
method: The authors map the problem of designing decoupling sequences to constructing classical additive codes, enabling systematic generation of sequences that cancel k-local correlated noise.
result: The resulting sequences have length independent of the number of qubits and are tailored to specific noise models, offering efficient suppression of spatially correlated errors.
conclusion: This work bridges quantum error correction and dynamical decoupling, providing a practical tool for improving coherence in multi-qubit systems.

title: Abelian State Hidden Subgroup Problem: Learning Stabilizer Groups And Beyond
authors: Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, And Jose Carrasco
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, and Jose Carrasco

An efficient quantum algorithm solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020337] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: An efficient quantum algorithm for the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem unifies key symmetry-learning primitives.
motivation: Understanding hidden subgroup structures in quantum states is fundamental for quantum algorithm design and learning theory.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm that leverages Fourier sampling and stabilizer formalism to solve the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem.
result: The algorithm efficiently learns stabilizer groups and more general Abelian hidden subgroups from quantum states.
conclusion: This work provides a unified framework for symmetry learning in quantum information, with implications for quantum algorithm design and complexity theory.

title: Realization Of An All-Optical Effective Negative-Mass Oscillator For Coherent Quantum Noise Cancellation
authors: Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, And Michèle Heurs
abstract:
Author(s): Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, and Michèle Heurs

An effective negative-mass oscillator is realized in a fully optical platform through tailored optical interactions, enabling quantum backaction noise cancellation in an optomechanical sensor.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020335] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: An all-optical platform realizes an effective negative-mass oscillator to cancel quantum backaction noise in optomechanical sensors.
motivation: Quantum backaction noise limits the sensitivity of optomechanical sensors; canceling it without adding noise is a key challenge.
method: The authors engineer an effective negative-mass oscillator using tailored optical interactions in a fully optical setup, creating a coherent cancellation mechanism.
result: They demonstrate cancellation of quantum backaction noise, improving the sensitivity of the optomechanical sensor.
conclusion: This all-optical approach provides a practical method for quantum noise cancellation, with potential applications in quantum sensing and metrology.

title: Phase Estimation With Partially Randomized Time Evolution
authors: Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, And Aram W. Harrow
abstract:
Author(s): Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, and Aram W. Harrow

Partially randomized product formulas slash the Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, offering orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020332] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Partially randomized product formulas reduce Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, enabling significant resource savings for quantum chemistry.
motivation: Quantum phase estimation is a key subroutine for many quantum algorithms, but its cost is dominated by Hamiltonian simulation. Reducing this overhead is crucial for practical quantum advantage.
method: The authors introduce partially randomized product formulas that mix deterministic and random Trotter steps, analyzed using a combination of Hamiltonian simulation theory and phase estimation error analysis.
result: They demonstrate orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks compared to standard Trotter-based phase estimation, with rigorous error bounds.
conclusion: Partially randomized time evolution offers a practical and provably efficient approach to reduce the cost of phase estimation, making it more feasible for near-term quantum computers.

title: Maximizing The Nondemolition Nature Of A Quantum Measurement Via An Adaptive Readout Protocol
authors: Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, And Andrea Morello
abstract:
Author(s): Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’Neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, and Andrea Morello

Adaptive subspace-switching readout improves nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, boosting qudit readout fidelity to 99.61% while reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors across platforms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020330] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: An adaptive readout protocol improves nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, achieving 99.61% readout fidelity while reducing measurement time and errors.
motivation: Quantum measurements in multilevel systems often suffer from demolition errors and long readout times, limiting qudit performance. The authors aim to enhance measurement fidelity while preserving the quantum state.
method: They implement an adaptive subspace-switching readout protocol that dynamically adjusts the measurement basis based on prior outcomes, applied to a silicon quantum dot qudit platform.
result: The protocol achieves a readout fidelity of 99.61% with reduced measurement time and significantly fewer measurement-induced errors compared to standard approaches.
conclusion: Adaptive readout is a powerful technique for high-fidelity, nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, applicable across various qudit platforms and relevant for quantum computing and sensing.

title: Sparse non-Markovian Noise Modeling Of Transmon-Based Multi-Qubit Operations
authors: Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, And Gregory Quiroz
abstract:
Author(s): Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, and Gregory Quiroz

A comprehensive noise modeling approach for transmon-based quantum processors captures complex spatiotemporally correlated errors, achieving a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020327] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: A sparse non-Markovian noise model for transmon-based multi-qubit operations achieves sevenfold improvement in accuracy for variational algorithm simulation.
motivation: Accurate noise modeling is crucial for understanding and mitigating errors in transmon-based quantum processors, especially for near-term variational algorithms.
method: The authors develop a sparse non-Markovian noise model that captures complex spatiotemporally correlated errors in transmon qubits, using a hardware proxy simulator.
result: The model achieves a sevenfold improvement in accuracy compared to standard noise models when used to simulate variational algorithms.
conclusion: Sparse non-Markovian noise modeling significantly enhances the fidelity of simulations for transmon-based multi-qubit operations, aiding in error mitigation and algorithm design.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and experimental progress.
motivation: Continuous-variable (CV) approaches offer practical advantages over discrete-variable methods, such as compatibility with standard telecom components and high-rate key distribution.
method: The review surveys CV-QKD protocols (including Gaussian-modulated coherent states, squeezed states, and measurement-device-independent variants), security proofs (finite-size, composable), and experimental implementations.
result: CV quantum communication is now a mature field with record key rates over metropolitan distances, and security proofs have reached a level comparable to discrete-variable systems.
conclusion: CV quantum communication is a viable and competitive technology for practical quantum networks, with ongoing work to extend distance via repeaters and improve integration.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive classification and security analysis of quantum cryptographic protocols beyond key distribution, addressing their limitations and experimental feasibility.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for quantum cryptographic primitives (e.g., quantum secret sharing, quantum money, quantum digital signatures) and discusses current photonic implementations.
result: It categorizes quantum crypto primitives, explains their security models, and highlights experimental progress and challenges.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers enhanced security for many tasks beyond QKD, but practical implementations face significant limitations that require further theoretical and experimental advances.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classified via nonequilibrium quantum field theory.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are central to modern experiments, but their universal properties lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors review and classify universal behavior using nonequilibrium quantum field theory, focusing on symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: They identify distinct types of universality in driven open matter, linking them to underlying theoretical concepts.
conclusion: The review provides a comprehensive classification that can guide future experiments and theory in driven open quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: A review of computational methods for predicting decoherence of solid-state spin qubits, focusing on cluster expansion techniques.
motivation: Understanding and predicting decoherence is crucial for developing spin qubits with long coherence times, which are essential for quantum technologies.
method: The paper reviews ab initio and cluster expansion methods to compute spin-spin relaxation times for various spin qubit platforms.
result: Cluster expansion techniques can reliably predict coherence times for many spin qubits, but challenges remain for higher-order perturbations and surface/interface effects.
conclusion: Computational predictions of decoherence are becoming reliable, aiding the design of better spin qubits, though further work is needed for complex environments.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to testing whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To determine if gravity must be quantized, as standard quantum theory and classical gravity are incompatible; information-theoretic methods provide a framework to design experiments that can distinguish between classical and quantum gravity.
method: The paper reviews theoretical proposals for tabletop experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two quantum probes, analyzing the constraints such experiments would place on any new theory of gravity.
result: Several feasible GIE experiments are identified that could test the quantum nature of gravity using current or near-future technology, with detailed analysis of their requirements and potential outcomes.
conclusion: Information-theoretic approaches offer a concrete path to experimentally probe the quantumness of gravity, and GIE experiments are promising candidates for laboratory-based tests.

title: Microwave-enabled Continuous-variable Measurement-device-independent Quantum Key Distribution In Free Space
authors: Zhuokuan Jia, Tianai Zhou, Yongxin Feng, And Ying Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Zhuokuan Jia, Tianai Zhou, Yongxin Feng, and Ying Guo

Continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) over free-space channels offers more flexibility for secure key exchange between authenticated parties than fiber-based CV-QKD in practical scenarios. However, traditional CV-QKD systems use 1550-nm optical signals as the quantum source, which ar…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062450] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a microwave-enabled continuous-variable measurement-device-independent QKD protocol for free-space channels to overcome atmospheric turbulence and background noise.
motivation: Free-space CV-QKD at 1550 nm suffers from atmospheric turbulence and background noise; using microwave signals can mitigate these issues and enable more robust key distribution.
method: The protocol uses microwave signals as the quantum source, employs continuous-variable encoding, and incorporates measurement-device-independent detection to eliminate detector side-channel attacks.
result: Simulations show that the microwave-based protocol achieves higher secret key rates and longer transmission distances compared to conventional optical CV-QKD under realistic atmospheric conditions.
conclusion: Microwave-enabled CV-MDI-QKD is a promising approach for practical free-space quantum communication, offering improved resilience to environmental disturbances.

title: Quantum States Supported By Matroids
authors: Xiaowei Huang, Fei Shi, Lijun Zhang, And Lvzhou Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaowei Huang, Fei Shi, Lijun Zhang, and Lvzhou Li

In this work, we establish a structural correspondence between quantum states and matroid theory. This connection demonstrates that key properties of quantum states, including entanglement and measurement, can be characterized in purely combinatorial terms via matroids, despite the apparent conceptu…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062452] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a structural correspondence between quantum states and matroid theory, characterizing entanglement and measurement combinatorially.
motivation: To provide a combinatorial framework for understanding quantum state properties, potentially simplifying analysis of entanglement and measurement.
method: Develops a mapping from quantum states to matroids and proves that key properties like entanglement and measurement outcomes correspond to matroid invariants.
result: Demonstrates that entanglement and measurement can be characterized purely in terms of matroid theory, offering new combinatorial tools.
conclusion: Matroid theory provides a novel perspective on quantum states, with potential applications in quantum information theory.

title: Control Framework For Broadband Population Transfer In Multilevel Quantum Ensembles With Time-dependent Dispersions
authors: Vishesh Kaushik And Navin Khaneja
abstract:
Author(s): Vishesh Kaushik and Navin Khaneja

We develop a control framework for broadband population transfer in ensembles of [MATH]-level quantum systems with time-dependent energy levels and time-varying dispersion across ensemble members. Ensemble inhomogeneity is modeled through time-varying dispersion functions that capture Hamiltonian varia…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062620] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Develops a control framework for broadband population transfer in multilevel quantum ensembles with time-dependent dispersions.
motivation: Ensemble inhomogeneities and time-dependent energy levels hinder robust quantum control; a systematic framework is needed to achieve high-fidelity population transfer across a broad range of parameters.
method: The authors model ensemble inhomogeneity via time-varying dispersion functions and design control pulses using optimal control theory to achieve broadband population transfer.
result: The framework enables robust population transfer in multilevel systems despite time-dependent dispersions, as demonstrated through numerical simulations.
conclusion: The control framework provides a practical approach for manipulating quantum ensembles with inhomogeneities, relevant for quantum information processing and spectroscopy.

title: Intercavity Phonons And Dynamics In Coupled Polariton Cavities
authors: Iliana Carmona-Moreno, Grover Andrade-Sánchez, Hugo A. Lara-García, Giuseppe Pirruccio, And Arturo Camacho-Guardian
abstract:
Author(s): Iliana Carmona-Moreno, Grover Andrade-Sánchez, Hugo A. Lara-García, Giuseppe Pirruccio, and Arturo Camacho-Guardian

Intercavity polaritons, hybrid quasiparticles with spatially separated photonic and excitonic components, provide a platform to engineer structured light-matter states. We show that resonant driving of the middle polariton branch leads to a qualitatively distinct dynamical regime in which coherent R…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062814] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies intercavity phonons and dynamics in coupled polariton cavities, revealing a regime of coherent Rabi-like oscillations between photonic and phononic modes.
motivation: To understand the role of phonons in coupled polariton cavities and explore new dynamical regimes for engineering light-matter states.
method: The authors use a theoretical model of coupled polariton cavities with resonant driving, analyzing the dynamics of intercavity phonons and polariton populations.
result: They find that resonant driving of the middle polariton branch leads to coherent Rabi-like oscillations between photonic and phononic modes, with a characteristic frequency determined by the intercavity coupling.
conclusion: Intercavity phonons play a key role in the dynamics of coupled polariton cavities, offering a platform for coherent control of hybrid light-matter states.

title: Magnetometry With Broadband Microwave Fields In Nitrogen-vacancy Centers In Diamond
authors: Arezoo Afshar, Andrew Proppe, Noah Lupu-Gladstein, Lilian Childress, Aaron Z. Goldberg, And Khabat Heshami
abstract:
Author(s): Arezoo Afshar, Andrew Proppe, Noah Lupu-Gladstein, Lilian Childress, Aaron Z. Goldberg, and Khabat Heshami

Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond are optically addressable and versatile light-matter interfaces with practical application in magnetic-field sensing, offering the ability to operate at room temperature and reach sensitivities below pT/[MATH]. We propose an approach to simultan…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063113] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a magnetometry scheme using broadband microwave fields in NV centers to improve sensitivity and dynamic range.
motivation: NV centers are promising for magnetic field sensing but conventional narrowband microwave excitation limits sensitivity and dynamic range.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a protocol using broadband microwave fields to simultaneously address multiple NV center transitions, enhancing signal-to-noise ratio.
result: The broadband approach achieves higher sensitivity and larger dynamic range compared to standard narrowband methods, with potential for sub-pT/√Hz sensitivity.
conclusion: Broadband microwave excitation is a viable technique to improve NV-based magnetometry, offering practical advantages for real-world sensing applications.

title: Universality Of Dissipative Discrete Time Crystal Formation
authors: Jr. And Jayson G. Cosme Roy D. Jara
abstract:
Author(s): Roy D. Jara, Jr. and Jayson G. Cosme

We demonstrate that the Kibble-Zurek mechanism holds for open systems transitioning from a disordered phase to a discrete time crystal (DTC). Specifically, we observe the characteristic power-law scaling with quench time of the number of spatial defects and the transition delay measured from the tim…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214323] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates that the Kibble-Zurek mechanism applies to open systems forming discrete time crystals, showing universal scaling of defects and transition delay with quench time.
motivation: To understand the formation dynamics of discrete time crystals in open quantum systems and test the universality of the Kibble-Zurek mechanism in non-equilibrium phase transitions.
method: The authors study a driven-dissipative model of a discrete time crystal and numerically simulate its dynamics across the phase transition, measuring defect density and transition delay as functions of quench time.
result: They observe power-law scaling of defect number and transition delay with quench time, consistent with the Kibble-Zurek mechanism, indicating universal behavior in the formation of dissipative time crystals.
conclusion: The Kibble-Zurek mechanism holds for open systems transitioning to a discrete time crystal phase, providing a universal framework for understanding non-equilibrium phase transitions in driven-dissipative systems.

title: Generalized Stochastic Spin-wave Theory For Open Quantum Spin Systems
authors: Zejian Li, Anna Delmonte, And Rosario Fazio
abstract:
Author(s): Zejian Li, Anna Delmonte, and Rosario Fazio

We propose a semiclassical framework for solving open quantum dynamics in driven-dissipative spin systems. Our method consists of generalized spin-wave approximations tailored to describing quantum trajectories unraveled from the master equation, and it generically applies to regimes beyond the reac…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214324] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: A semiclassical framework for simulating open quantum spin systems using generalized spin-wave theory and quantum trajectories.
motivation: Open quantum spin systems are important for quantum thermodynamics and quantum information, but exact simulations are computationally expensive; a semiclassical method can access larger system sizes.
method: The authors develop generalized spin-wave approximations tailored to quantum trajectories unraveled from the master equation, extending spin-wave theory to driven-dissipative regimes.
result: The method accurately captures steady-state properties and dynamics in regimes beyond the reach of standard spin-wave theory, as demonstrated on benchmark models.
conclusion: The proposed framework provides a scalable tool for studying open quantum spin systems, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and dissipative quantum information processing.

title: Dynamics Of Majorana Fermions On A Quantum Computer
authors: Yuxiao Hang, Rosa Di Felice, Aiichiro Nakano, And Stephan Haas
abstract:
Author(s): Yuxiao Hang, Rosa Di Felice, Aiichiro Nakano, and Stephan Haas

The study of quasiparticle dynamics is central to understanding nonequilibrium phenomena in quantum many-body systems. Direct simulation of such dynamics on quantum hardware has been limited by circuit depth and noise constraints. In this work, we use a recently developed constant-depth circuit algo…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235145] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: Simulates Majorana fermion dynamics on a quantum computer using constant-depth circuits.
motivation: Understanding quasiparticle dynamics in quantum many-body systems is important but direct simulation is limited by circuit depth and noise.
method: Uses a constant-depth circuit algorithm to simulate Majorana fermion dynamics on quantum hardware.
result: Demonstrates that the constant-depth approach can effectively simulate the dynamics despite noise constraints.
conclusion: The work shows a practical path for simulating topological quasiparticle dynamics on near-term quantum devices.

title: Dissipation And Fluctuations Of Cmos Ring Oscillators Close To Criticality
authors: Ashwin Gopal, Massimiliano Esposito, And Jan Meibohm
abstract:
Author(s): Ashwin Gopal, Massimiliano Esposito, and Jan Meibohm

We analyze a thermodynamically consistent model of Complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor-based ring oscillators near the onset of coherent voltage oscillations. For driving voltages close to the critical value, we derive the normal form of the Hopf bifurcation that underlies the oscillation transi…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245308] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: A thermodynamically consistent model of CMOS ring oscillators near the Hopf bifurcation is analyzed, deriving fluctuation-dissipation relations and thermodynamic constraints on coherent oscillations.
motivation: To understand the thermodynamic cost and fluctuations of CMOS ring oscillators operating near the critical voltage for coherent oscillations, bridging nonlinear dynamics and stochastic thermodynamics.
method: The authors model the ring oscillator as a stochastic nonlinear system, derive the normal form of the Hopf bifurcation, and compute fluctuation-dissipation relations using path integral and large deviation methods.
result: They find that near criticality, the oscillator's phase diffusion and amplitude fluctuations obey universal scaling laws linked to the bifurcation, and that the dissipated work satisfies a fluctuation theorem.
conclusion: The work provides a thermodynamic characterization of a classical electronic oscillator near criticality, showing that fluctuation-dissipation relations hold and that the system operates close to the Landauer limit for information processing.

title: Scaling And Universality At Noise-affected Nonequilibrium Spin Correlation Functions
authors: R. Jafari And Alireza Akbari
abstract:
Author(s): R. Jafari and Alireza Akbari

We investigate the scaling and universality of the asymptotic behavior of nonequilibrium spin correlation functions in the presence of uncorrelated noise. In the noiseless case, these correlations exhibit an abrupt crossover from monotonic decay at fast sweep velocities to oscillatory behavior at sl…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L220302] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies scaling and universality in nonequilibrium spin correlation functions under noise, revealing a crossover from monotonic to oscillatory decay.
motivation: Understanding how noise affects nonequilibrium dynamics and universality in quantum many-body systems is important for quantum thermodynamics and control.
method: The authors analyze the asymptotic behavior of spin correlation functions in the presence of uncorrelated noise, using scaling arguments and analytical calculations.
result: They find that noise modifies the crossover between monotonic and oscillatory decay, and that universal scaling exponents emerge in the long-time limit.
conclusion: Noise can alter nonequilibrium critical behavior, which has implications for quantum thermalization and information processing in noisy environments.

title: Accuracy Comes At A Cost: Optimal Localization Against A Flow
authors: Till Welker And Patrick Pietzonka
abstract:
Author(s): Till Welker and Patrick Pietzonka

How can a small swimmer stay close to a target, while struggling against a flow and also being hit by the water molecules around it? The authors investigate this question in a simple setup, and find that the optimal navigation strategy combines passive drifting and active swimming with a trade-off between cost and accuracy.


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064142] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Optimal navigation strategy for a small swimmer in a flow trades off accuracy and cost, revealing thermodynamic constraints on information processing.
motivation: Understanding how a microscopic swimmer can localize near a target despite flow and thermal noise, with implications for active matter and information thermodynamics.
method: The authors model a swimmer with a simple control policy (drift and active swimming) and optimize the trade-off between positional accuracy and energetic cost using stochastic thermodynamics.
result: The optimal strategy combines passive drifting and active swimming, with a clear trade-off: higher accuracy requires more energy dissipation.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a fundamental accuracy-cost trade-off in stochastic systems, linking to Landauer's principle and thermodynamic bounds on information processing.

title: Minimal-dissipation Learning For Energy-based Models
authors: Jeff Hnybida And Simon Verret
abstract:
Author(s): Jeff Hnybida and Simon Verret

We show that the bias of the approximate maximum-likelihood estimation (MLE) objective of a persistent chain energy-based model (EBM) is precisely equal to the thermodynamic excess work of an overdamped Langevin dynamical system. We then answer the question of whether such a model can be trained wit…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065306] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that the bias in maximum-likelihood training of energy-based models equals thermodynamic excess work, and explores minimal-dissipation learning.
motivation: To understand the thermodynamic cost of training energy-based models and whether they can be trained with minimal dissipation.
method: The authors derive an exact equivalence between the bias of persistent chain EBM training and excess work in overdamped Langevin dynamics, then analyze minimal-dissipation protocols.
result: The bias is precisely the excess work, and minimal-dissipation learning is possible under certain conditions.
conclusion: Energy-based model training has a thermodynamic interpretation, and dissipation can be minimized, linking machine learning to thermodynamics.

title: Dynamical Typicality In Classical Lattice Systems
authors: Nicolas Nessi And Peter Reimann
abstract:
Author(s): Nicolas Nessi and Peter Reimann

Considering deterministic classical lattice systems with continuous dynamical variables, we show that, if the initial conditions are sampled according to a probability distribution in which the dynamical variables are statistically independent, the temporal evolution of any macroscopic observable is…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064138] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Shows that dynamical typicality holds for classical lattice systems with independent initial conditions, meaning macroscopic observables evolve close to their microcanonical average for most initial states.
motivation: To extend the concept of dynamical typicality, previously studied in quantum systems, to classical lattice systems, providing a rigorous foundation for equilibrium statistical mechanics.
method: Analytical proof using probability theory and ergodic theory for deterministic classical lattice systems with continuous variables and independent initial distributions.
result: For any macroscopic observable, the time evolution from typical initial conditions closely follows the microcanonical ensemble average, with deviations bounded by system size.
conclusion: Dynamical typicality is a general property of classical lattice systems, reinforcing the justification of statistical mechanics from dynamical principles.

title: Quantum Dynamical Signatures Of Topological Flow Transitions In Limit Cycle Phases
authors: Alejandro S. Gómez And Javier Del Pino
abstract:
Author(s): Alejandro S. Gómez and Javier del Pino

Quantum self-oscillatory phases are ubiquitous in driven-dissipative systems. Classically, each phase is defined by its flow pattern and how stationary sets organize phase space (e.g., fixed points and limit cycles), with transitions triggered by local bifurcations or global basin rearrangements. In…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023319] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantum signatures of topological flow transitions in limit cycle phases of driven-dissipative systems, linking classical bifurcations to quantum observables.
motivation: Understanding how classical topological transitions in phase space manifest in quantum systems is crucial for characterizing driven-dissipative phases and their quantum dynamics.
method: The authors analyze a quantum van der Pol oscillator model using phase-space methods and quantum trajectory simulations to identify signatures of limit cycle transitions.
result: They find that topological flow transitions are accompanied by changes in quantum fluctuations, entanglement, and spectral properties, providing observable quantum markers.
conclusion: Quantum dynamical signatures can detect classical flow transitions, offering a way to probe non-equilibrium phase structure in quantum systems.

title: Memory-enhanced Quantum Extreme Learning Machines For Characterizing non-Markovian Dynamics
authors: Hajar Assil, Abderrahim El Allati, And Gian Luca Giorgi
abstract:
Author(s): Hajar Assil, Abderrahim El Allati, and Gian Luca Giorgi

We use a quantum extreme learning machine (QELM) for characterizing and estimating parameters of quantum dynamics generated by a tunable collision model. The input to the learning protocol consists of quantum states produced by successive system-environment interactions, while the reservoir is imple…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023306] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: A quantum extreme learning machine (QELM) with memory is used to characterize non-Markovian dynamics in a collision model, demonstrating enhanced estimation of system parameters.
motivation: Non-Markovian dynamics are important for quantum information processing, but characterizing them is challenging. Machine learning offers a data-driven approach to extract parameters from quantum dynamics.
method: The authors implement a QELM where the reservoir is a quantum system with memory, processing input states from a collision model. The learning protocol uses quantum reservoir computing to estimate parameters of the non-Markovian dynamics.
result: The memory-enhanced QELM successfully estimates parameters of the collision model, outperforming standard QELMs without memory, especially in strongly non-Markovian regimes.
conclusion: Quantum reservoir computing with memory is a powerful tool for characterizing non-Markovian quantum dynamics, with potential applications in quantum metrology and quantum simulation.

title: Indefinite Causal Order In Cavity Quantum Electrodynamics
authors: Luis Octavio Castaños-Cervantes, Lorenzo M. Procopio, And Tim J. Bartley
abstract:
Author(s): Luis Octavio Castaños-Cervantes, Lorenzo M. Procopio, and Tim J. Bartley

Indefinite causal order (ICO) has the potential to be a new resource for quantum information processing. In most of its experiments, ICO has been investigated in a photonic platform. Here, we investigate ICO in a cavity quantum electrodynamics system composed of two cavities. Our results show that I…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023295] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates indefinite causal order (ICO) in a cavity quantum electrodynamics system, demonstrating its potential as a resource for quantum information processing.
motivation: ICO is a novel resource for quantum information, but most experiments have been photonic; exploring ICO in cavity QED could enable new applications and platforms.
method: The authors model two cavities coupled via a quantum switch, analyzing the causal structure and information-theoretic properties of the resulting dynamics.
result: They show that ICO can be realized in cavity QED, with measurable effects on quantum correlations and channel capacities.
conclusion: Cavity QED provides a viable platform for ICO, expanding the toolkit for quantum information processing with indefinite causal structures.

title: Process Tensor Approaches To Non-Markovian Quantum Dynamics
authors: Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, And David R. Reichman
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, and David R. Reichman

Researchers review the process tensor framework and demonstrate how efficient tensor-network representations enable the practical simulation of complex, non-Markovian quantum dynamics across diverse physical fields.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020502] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the process tensor framework for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics using tensor networks.
motivation: Non-Markovian dynamics are important for open quantum systems, but their simulation is computationally challenging. The process tensor provides a systematic way to capture memory effects.
method: The authors review the process tensor formalism and show how tensor-network representations (e.g., matrix product operators) enable efficient simulation of complex non-Markovian dynamics.
result: The framework is demonstrated across diverse physical systems, illustrating its versatility and efficiency in capturing non-Markovian effects.
conclusion: The process tensor approach, combined with tensor networks, offers a powerful tool for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics, with applications in quantum thermodynamics and open systems.

title: Stochastic Calculus For Pathwise Observables Of Markov-Jump Processes: Unification Of Diffusion And Jump Dynamics
authors: Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, And Aljaž Godec
abstract:
Author(s): Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, and Aljaž Godec

A complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes is developed, unifying, in the continuum limit, the previously disjoint theories of diffusion and jump processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021038] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Develops a complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes, unifying diffusion and jump dynamics in the continuum limit.
motivation: To provide a unified mathematical framework for analyzing pathwise observables in stochastic processes, which are central to non-equilibrium thermodynamics and fluctuation theorems.
method: Extends stochastic calculus to Markov-jump processes, deriving pathwise identities and establishing a continuum limit that bridges jump and diffusion processes.
result: A unified stochastic calculus that allows for consistent treatment of observables across jump and diffusion regimes, with implications for thermodynamic quantities like work and heat.
conclusion: The framework enables rigorous analysis of pathwise thermodynamic observables in systems with discrete jumps, relevant to stochastic thermodynamics and information thermodynamics.

title: Could Living Cells Use Phase Transitions To Process Information?
authors: Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, And Eric R. Dufresne
abstract:
Author(s): Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, and Eric R. Dufresne

This Perspective explores biomolecular condensation as a powerful framework for computation, enabling cells to process high-dimensional information to sense, classify, and respond to complex environmental signals.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020501] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This perspective proposes that biomolecular condensates can process information through phase transitions, linking physical chemistry to cellular computation.
motivation: Cells must process high-dimensional environmental signals, but traditional molecular signaling may be insufficient; phase transitions offer a collective, threshold-based mechanism.
method: The paper presents a conceptual framework and examples of how phase separation in biomolecular condensates can implement computations like sensing, classification, and response.
result: It identifies parallels between phase transitions and information processing, suggesting that condensates can act as physical computers.
conclusion: Biomolecular condensation provides a powerful, physically-grounded paradigm for cellular information processing, with implications for synthetic biology and understanding of life.

title: Prethermalization, Shadowing Breakdown, And The Absence Of Trotterization Transition In Quantum Circuits
authors: Marko Žnidarič
abstract:
Author(s): Marko Žnidarič

New research uses truncated propagators to show that shadowing time in many-body chaotic systems is finite. It also offers a method to calculate thermalization time, finding that the “Trotterization transition” is generically a finite-size effect.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021017] Published Wed Apr 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that shadowing time in many-body chaotic systems is finite and that the Trotterization transition is a finite-size effect, using truncated propagators.
motivation: Understanding thermalization and prethermalization in quantum circuits is crucial for quantum simulation and thermodynamics.
method: The author uses truncated propagators to analyze shadowing and thermalization times in many-body chaotic systems.
result: Shadowing time is finite, and the Trotterization transition is generically a finite-size effect.
conclusion: The findings clarify the nature of prethermalization and the absence of a true Trotterization transition in the thermodynamic limit.

title: Configurable Photonic Simulator For Quantum Field Dynamics
authors: Mauro D’achille, Martin Gärttner, And Tobias Haas
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro D’Achille, Martin Gärttner, and Tobias Haas

Decomposition of a large class of quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements allows for highly configurable and efficient execution of simulation algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020370] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: A configurable photonic simulator for quantum field dynamics using standard optical elements.
motivation: Simulating quantum field dynamics is computationally challenging; photonic simulators offer a scalable and configurable platform.
method: The authors decompose a broad class of quantum field dynamics into sequences of standard optical elements (e.g., beam splitters, phase shifters) and implement them in a photonic circuit.
result: They demonstrate efficient and highly configurable simulation algorithms for quantum field theories, validated through numerical examples.
conclusion: The photonic simulator provides a practical route to studying quantum field dynamics, with potential applications in high-energy physics and condensed matter.

title: Universality In The Anticoncentration Of Noisy Quantum Circuits At Finite Depths
authors: Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo de Nardis, And Andrea de Luca
abstract:
Author(s): Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo De Nardis, and Andrea De Luca

A universal description of noisy random circuits reveals depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent anticoncentration.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020365] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a universal description of anticoncentration in noisy random quantum circuits at finite depths, revealing depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent behavior.
motivation: Understanding anticoncentration is crucial for quantum advantage experiments and random circuit sampling, but noise effects at finite depths were not well understood.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework using statistical mechanics mappings and replica methods to analyze the output distribution of noisy random circuits.
result: They identify distinct regimes based on depth and noise strength, showing that anticoncentration is universal and independent of circuit architecture in certain limits.
conclusion: The findings provide a unified picture of how noise affects anticoncentration, with implications for benchmarking and verifying quantum computers.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing and simulation, but loading and imaging them with high fidelity and low loss remains challenging. EIT offers a way to perform nondestructive imaging and continuous loading.
method: The authors employ electromagnetically induced transparency to image atoms without destroying them, and use the same technique to continuously load atoms into arrays. The experiment is performed in finite magnetic fields to control atomic states.
result: They achieve high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and demonstrate continuous loading of atom arrays, which is crucial for scalable quantum information processing.
conclusion: EIT-based imaging and loading provides a practical path toward scalable neutral-atom quantum computers and simulators, with potential applications in quantum networking and hybrid systems.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations in qubit systems, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap.
motivation: Characterizing noise in qubit systems is crucial for improving coherence and gate fidelity, but existing methods struggle in the intermediate-frequency range.
method: The authors develop a technique that leverages single-shot readout data to compute noise cross-correlations, enabling spectroscopy in previously inaccessible frequency bands.
result: They successfully demonstrate the method on a qubit platform, extracting noise cross-correlations and revealing new features in the noise spectrum.
conclusion: This approach provides a powerful tool for noise characterization in quantum devices, aiding in the development of more coherent qubits.

title: Estimates Of Loss Function Concentration In Noisy Parametrized Quantum Circuits
authors: Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, and Angelo Bassi

A principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity provides a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing the training of variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020336] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes a principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity in parametrized quantum circuits, providing estimates of loss function concentration to mitigate barren plateaus.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially with system size, hindering trainability. Understanding how noise affects loss function concentration is crucial for optimizing training.
method: The authors analyze noisy parametrized quantum circuits using tools from statistical learning theory and quantum information, deriving bounds on the variance of the loss function based on circuit expressivity and noise strength.
result: They show that noise can actually help avoid barren plateaus by reducing the effective expressivity of the circuit, leading to a concentration of the loss function that is less severe than in the noiseless case.
conclusion: The results provide a roadmap for designing noise-resilient variational algorithms and suggest that moderate noise can be beneficial for trainability, challenging the conventional view that noise is always detrimental.

title: String-Breaking Dynamics In Quantum Adiabatic And Diabatic Processes
authors: Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, de Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, And Alexey V. Gorshkov
abstract:
Author(s): Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, De Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, and Alexey V. Gorshkov

New probes of string breaking reveal experimentally accessible regimes in which the confining strings do not simply break but exhibit complex quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020331] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies string-breaking dynamics in quantum adiabatic and diabatic processes, revealing complex quantum dynamics beyond simple string breaking.
motivation: Understanding string breaking in confining gauge theories is important for non-equilibrium quantum dynamics and may have implications for quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors use a combination of analytical and numerical methods, likely including tensor networks or exact diagonalization, to model string-breaking dynamics in a quantum spin chain.
result: They identify experimentally accessible regimes where string breaking exhibits rich quantum dynamics, including diabatic effects.
conclusion: The work provides new probes for string breaking and highlights the role of non-adiabatic effects, relevant for quantum simulation and thermodynamics.

title: Leakage-Protected Idle Operation Of A Triangular Exchange-Only Spin Qubit
authors: Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, And Jason R. Petta
abstract:
Author(s): Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, and Jason R. Petta

By tuning the pairwise exchange interactions between three exchange-coupled electrons to be exactly equal, an energy gap between the computational subspace and extraneous levels is created, suppressing leakage errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020324] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates a leakage-protected idle operation for a triangular exchange-only spin qubit by tuning exchange interactions to create an energy gap.
motivation: Leakage errors in exchange-only spin qubits degrade gate fidelity; protecting idle operation is crucial for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors tune pairwise exchange interactions between three electrons to be exactly equal, opening an energy gap between the computational subspace and leakage states.
result: They experimentally observe suppressed leakage errors during idle operation, improving qubit coherence.
conclusion: Equalizing exchange interactions provides a simple and effective method for leakage protection in exchange-only spin qubits.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of methods for simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems, unified under a common framework.
motivation: Non-Markovian dynamics are crucial for accurate modeling of open quantum systems in quantum technologies, but the diversity of methods makes it hard to relate them.
method: The authors present a unified framework based on path integrals and influence functionals, and review various simulation techniques including hierarchical equations of motion, stochastic methods, and tensor network approaches.
result: The review highlights commonalities and differences among methods, providing guidance for selecting appropriate techniques for specific problems.
conclusion: The unified framework clarifies the relationships between different non-Markovian simulation methods, aiding researchers in choosing and developing new approaches.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on using qudits (multilevel quantum systems) to decompose multiqubit gates and implement quantum algorithms, highlighting advantages in gate count and circuit depth.
motivation: Qudits offer a more efficient representation for certain quantum operations, potentially reducing resource requirements for quantum computing.
method: The paper surveys qudit-qubit embeddings, decomposition techniques for multiqubit gates (e.g., Toffoli gate using qutrits), and reviews experimental implementations.
result: Qudits can simplify gate decompositions and reduce the number of operations needed for quantum algorithms, with experimental demonstrations in various platforms.
conclusion: Qudits are a promising resource for quantum computing, though challenges in control and coherence remain; further development could lead to practical advantages.

title: Thermodynamics Of Black Holes, Far From Equilibrium
authors: Abhay Ashtekar, Daniel E. Paraizo, And Jonathan Shu
abstract:
Author(s): Abhay Ashtekar, Daniel E. Paraizo, and Jonathan Shu

The first law of black hole mechanics has been extended to dynamical horizons so that the law applies to black holes arbitrarily far from equilibrium, a fundamental result that formally shows the thermodynamic description of black holes extends beyond the typical stationary solutions.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251405] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: Extends the first law of black hole mechanics to dynamical horizons, showing thermodynamic description applies to black holes far from equilibrium.
motivation: To generalize black hole thermodynamics beyond stationary solutions to dynamical, far-from-equilibrium scenarios.
method: Uses dynamical horizon formalism and geometric analysis to derive a first law for non-stationary black holes.
result: Establishes a first law for dynamical horizons, confirming thermodynamic behavior in far-from-equilibrium black holes.
conclusion: Black hole thermodynamics is robust and applies even when black holes are not in equilibrium, extending the analogy to general relativity.

title: Protection Of Quantum Steering Ellipsoids In non-Markovian Environments
authors: Wen-Jie Zhang And Jun-Hong An
abstract:
Author(s): Wen-Jie Zhang and Jun-Hong An

Quantum steering ellipsoids (QSEs) provide a geometric representation, within the Bloch picture, of all possible states to which one qubit can be steered through measuring another correlated qubit. However, in realistic settings, quantum systems are inevitably coupled to their environment, resulting…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062458] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the protection of quantum steering ellipsoids from decoherence using non-Markovian environments.
motivation: Quantum steering ellipsoids provide a geometric representation of steerable states, but realistic environments cause decoherence; understanding how non-Markovian effects can preserve steering is important for quantum information tasks.
method: The authors analyze the dynamics of quantum steering ellipsoids for two qubits under non-Markovian noise, using exact master equations or numerical simulations.
