result: Non-Markovian environments can significantly protect the volume and shape of steering ellipsoids compared to Markovian environments, delaying the loss of steerability.
conclusion: Engineering non-Markovian environments may be a viable strategy to preserve quantum steering for quantum communication and cryptography.

title: Accelerated Spin-adapted Ground-state Preparation With Nonvariational Quantum Algorithms
authors: Takumi Kobori, Taichi Kosugi, Hirofumi Nishi, Synge Todo, And Yu-Ichiro Matsushita
abstract:
Author(s): Takumi Kobori, Taichi Kosugi, Hirofumi Nishi, Synge Todo, and Yu-ichiro Matsushita

Various methods have been explored to prepare the spin-adapted ground state—the lowest energy state within the Hilbert space constrained by externally specified values of the total spin magnitude and the spin-[MATH] component. In such problem settings, nonvariational methods incorporate penalty terms i…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062454] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes nonvariational quantum algorithms for preparing spin-adapted ground states using penalty terms and quantum phase estimation.
motivation: Preparing ground states with specific spin symmetry is important for quantum chemistry and condensed matter physics, but variational methods can be inefficient.
method: Uses a nonvariational approach combining penalty terms to enforce spin constraints with quantum phase estimation to project onto the ground state.
result: Demonstrates accelerated convergence to the spin-adapted ground state compared to variational methods in numerical simulations.
conclusion: Nonvariational algorithms can efficiently prepare symmetry-constrained ground states, offering a practical advantage for near-term quantum devices.

title: Identifying The Three-qubit $w$ State With The Quantum Uncertainty Relation
authors: Zhi-Jie Liu, Hao-Nan Qiang, Jie Zhou, Mi Xie, And Jing-Ling Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Zhi-Jie Liu, Hao-Nan Qiang, Jie Zhou, Mi Xie, and Jing-Ling Chen

The [MATH] state, a canonical representative of multipartite quantum entanglement, plays a crucial role in quantum information science due to its robust entanglement properties. Quantum uncertainty relations, on the other hand, form a fundamental cornerstone of quantum mechanics. This work introduces a…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062451] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses quantum uncertainty relations to identify the three-qubit W state, a canonical entangled state.
motivation: To provide a method for identifying the W state using uncertainty relations, which are fundamental in quantum mechanics.
method: The authors derive a quantum uncertainty relation and apply it to distinguish the W state from other three-qubit states.
result: They show that the W state saturates a specific uncertainty relation, enabling its identification.
conclusion: The work offers a new characterization of the W state via uncertainty relations, contributing to entanglement theory.

title: Temperature-driven False-vacuum Decay In Coherently Coupled Bose Superfluids
authors: Paniyanchatha Moolayil Sivasankar, Franco Dalfovo, Alessio Recati, And Arko Roy
abstract:
Author(s): Paniyanchatha Moolayil Sivasankar, Franco Dalfovo, Alessio Recati, and Arko Roy

The relaxation of a quantum field from a metastable state (false vacuum) to a stable one (true vacuum), also known as false-vacuum decay, is a fundamental problem in quantum field theory and cosmology. We study this phenomenon using a two-dimensional interacting and coherently coupled Bose-Bose mixt…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063323] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies false-vacuum decay in a two-dimensional Bose-Bose mixture, focusing on thermal effects and bubble nucleation dynamics.
motivation: False-vacuum decay is a fundamental process in quantum field theory and cosmology, and understanding its thermal activation in a controlled quantum system is of interest.
method: The authors use numerical simulations of the Gross-Pitaevskii equation for a coherently coupled Bose-Bose mixture to model the decay from a metastable false vacuum to a true vacuum.
result: They find that temperature enhances the decay rate and modifies the bubble nucleation dynamics, with a crossover from quantum tunneling to thermal activation.
conclusion: The work provides insights into thermal effects on false-vacuum decay, but the connection to quantum information or thermodynamics is indirect.

title: Incoherent Repumping Scheme In The $^{88}\mathrm{Sr}^{+}$ Five-level Manifold
authors: Valentin Martimort, Sacha Guesne, Derwell Drapier, Vincent Tugayé, Lilay Gros-Desormeaux, Valentin Cambier, Albane Douillet, Luca Guidoni, And Jean-Pierre Likforman
abstract:
Author(s): Valentin Martimort, Sacha Guesne, Derwell Drapier, Vincent Tugayé, Lilay Gros-Desormeaux, Valentin Cambier, Albane Douillet, Luca Guidoni, and Jean-Pierre Likforman

Laser-cooled trapped ions are at the heart of modern quantum technologies and their cooling dynamics often deviate from the simplified two-level atom model. Doppler cooling of the [MATH] ion involves several electronic levels and repumping channels that strongly influence fluorescenc…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063109] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an incoherent repumping scheme for Doppler cooling of Sr+ ions, analyzing its effect on fluorescence and cooling dynamics.
motivation: Doppler cooling of trapped ions often involves multiple electronic levels and repumping channels, complicating the cooling dynamics. Understanding and optimizing repumping is important for quantum technologies.
method: The authors model the five-level manifold of Sr+ and propose an incoherent repumping scheme, analyzing the steady-state fluorescence and cooling forces using rate equations.
result: The incoherent repumping scheme modifies the fluorescence spectrum and cooling efficiency compared to coherent repumping, with potential benefits for certain experimental conditions.
conclusion: Incoherent repumping offers a practical alternative for cooling Sr+ ions, but the work is primarily an experimental technique paper without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Giant Magnetoelasticity In FeRh Thin Films Evidenced Via Strong Phonon-magnon Coupling
authors: D. Ourdani, C. Gourdon, J. A. Arregi, V. Uhlíř, Y. Roussigné, And L. Thevenard
abstract:
Author(s): D. Ourdani, C. Gourdon, J. A. Arregi, V. Uhlíř, Y. Roussigné, and L. Thevenard

FeRh is best known for its metamagnetic transition and giant volume magnetostriction. Here, the authors reveal remarkably strong phonon–magnon coupling in epitaxial FeRh. Combining Brillouin light scattering experiments with magnetoacoustic modeling, they demonstrate giant magnetoelasticity and show that Love surface acoustic waves provide an efficient mechanism for coherent magnon-polaron formation in magnetic thin films, highlighting FeRh as a promising platform for spin-acoustic information processing.


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214450] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: FeRh thin films exhibit giant magnetoelasticity and strong phonon-magnon coupling, enabling coherent magnon-polaron formation for spin-acoustic information processing.
motivation: To explore FeRh as a platform for spin-acoustic information processing by investigating its magnetoelastic properties and phonon-magnon coupling.
method: Brillouin light scattering experiments combined with magnetoacoustic modeling to study phonon-magnon coupling in epitaxial FeRh thin films.
result: Strong phonon-magnon coupling and giant magnetoelasticity are observed, with Love surface acoustic waves efficiently forming coherent magnon-polarons.
conclusion: FeRh is a promising material for spin-acoustic information processing due to its giant magnetoelasticity and strong phonon-magnon coupling.

title: Rotation Sensor Based On An Atom-cavity System
authors: Jim Skulte, Jayson G. Cosme, And Ludwig Mathey
abstract:
Author(s): Jim Skulte, Jayson G. Cosme, and Ludwig Mathey

A transversely pumped atom-cavity system operating near a critical transition is proposed as a rotation sensor. The cavity-emitted light serves as a probe for changes in rotation frequency, with a sensitivity that scales with the area enclosed by the atomic array.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022057] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a rotation sensor using a transversely pumped atom-cavity system near a critical transition, with sensitivity scaling with the enclosed area.
motivation: To develop a rotation sensor with high sensitivity using quantum optical systems, leveraging critical phenomena in atom-cavity setups.
method: Theoretical analysis of an atom-cavity system operating near a critical point, where cavity-emitted light probes changes in rotation frequency.
result: The sensor's sensitivity scales with the area enclosed by the atomic array, offering a potential advantage over classical sensors.
conclusion: The atom-cavity system provides a promising platform for rotation sensing, though experimental realization remains challenging.

title: Optimal Parametric Control Of Transport Across A Josephson Junction
authors: Hannah Kleine-Pollmann, Guido Homann, And Ludwig Mathey
abstract:
Author(s): Hannah Kleine-Pollmann, Guido Homann, and Ludwig Mathey

We present optimal control strategies for the dc transport across a Josephson junction. Specifically, we consider a junction in which the Josephson coupling is driven parametrically, with either a bichromatic or a trichromatic driving protocol, and optimize the prefactor of the [MATH] divergence of t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023313] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Optimal parametric control of dc transport across a Josephson junction using bichromatic and trichromatic driving to enhance the supercurrent divergence.
motivation: To improve control over transport in Josephson junctions, which are key components in superconducting circuits, by optimizing parametric driving protocols.
method: The authors apply optimal control theory to design bichromatic and trichromatic driving waveforms for the Josephson coupling, maximizing the prefactor of the current divergence.
result: They achieve enhanced supercurrent transport with optimized driving, demonstrating improved control over the junction's nonlinear dynamics.
conclusion: Parametric control can significantly boost transport in Josephson junctions, with potential applications in superconducting electronics and quantum devices.

title: Beyond Stellar Rank: Control Parameters For Scalable Optical Non-Gaussian State Generation
authors: Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, And Akira Furusawa
abstract:
Author(s): Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, and Akira Furusawa

Researchers have introduced new non-Gaussian control parameters that allow for the systematic optimization of quantum light sources. This breakthrough can increase the success rate of generating essential quantum states by orders of magnitude.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021034] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: Introduces non-Gaussian control parameters to systematically optimize optical non-Gaussian state generation, increasing success rates by orders of magnitude.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum information processing but their generation is inefficient; the paper aims to provide a systematic optimization framework.
method: The authors define new control parameters beyond stellar rank and use them to design and optimize experimental setups for generating non-Gaussian states.
result: The proposed parameters enable orders-of-magnitude improvement in success probability for generating target non-Gaussian states.
conclusion: The work offers a practical tool for scalable generation of non-Gaussian optical states, advancing quantum information applications.

title: Entropy Of Strongly Correlated Electrons In A Partially Filled Landau Level
authors: Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, And Andrea F. Young
abstract:
Author(s): Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, and Andrea F. Young

Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal the successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, reaching sensitivities that constrain the isolation of topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021016] Published Fri Apr 17, 2026.
tldr: Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, with sensitivity to topological entropy in non-Abelian phases.
motivation: Understanding entropy in strongly correlated electron systems, particularly in fractional quantum Hall states, is crucial for probing topological order and non-Abelian anyons.
method: Experimental entropy measurements using a graphene-based device in a partially filled Landau level, combined with theoretical modeling.
result: Successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom is observed, and the sensitivity approaches the level needed to isolate topological entropy.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a path toward measuring topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases, but the focus is on condensed matter physics rather than information thermodynamics.

title: Magic Tricycles: Efficient Magic-State Generation With Finite Block-Length Quantum Ldpc Codes
authors: Varun Menon, J. Pablo Bonilla Ataides, Rohan Mehta, Andi Gu, Daniel Bochen Tan, And Mikhail D. Lukin
abstract:
Author(s): Varun Menon, J. Pablo Bonilla Ataides, Rohan Mehta, Andi Gu, Daniel Bochen Tan, and Mikhail D. Lukin

Quantum computing needs “magic states” for universality, but they are costly to make. New research introduces tricycle codes: high-rate QLDPC codes that can be used to generate CZ magic states in constant depth with high noise resilience.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021014] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: Introduces tricycle codes, high-rate QLDPC codes for efficient magic-state generation in constant depth with high noise resilience.
motivation: Magic states are essential for universal quantum computing but costly to produce; efficient generation is needed.
method: Proposes tricycle codes, a family of QLDPC codes with high encoding rate and constant-depth encoding circuits, used to distill magic states.
result: Demonstrates that tricycle codes can generate CZ magic states with high fidelity and low overhead, outperforming existing protocols.
conclusion: Tricycle codes offer a practical path to efficient magic-state generation, advancing fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Quantum Computational Complexity Of Matrix Functions
authors: Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, And Leandro Aolita
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, and Leandro Aolita

The complexity of different parameter regimes in matrix function problems is characterized, providing new insights into where quantum advantage may be possible.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020364] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Characterizes the computational complexity of matrix functions, identifying regimes where quantum advantage may exist.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of matrix functions is fundamental for quantum algorithms and determining where quantum computers can outperform classical ones.
method: The authors analyze different parameter regimes of matrix function problems using computational complexity theory, likely employing reductions and oracle models.
result: They provide a complexity classification for matrix functions, highlighting regimes that are classically hard but quantumly tractable.
conclusion: The work offers new insights into potential quantum advantage for matrix function problems, but is primarily a complexity-theoretic result rather than a direct contribution to quantum information theory.

title: Efficient Quantum-Enhanced Classical Simulation For Patches Of Quantum Landscapes
authors: Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, and Zoë Holmes

Classically surrogating a small subregion of an expectation landscape can be done efficiently, potentially using initial data acquired from quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020359] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an efficient classical surrogate for small subregions of expectation value landscapes in quantum computing, using initial quantum data.
motivation: Understanding and simulating expectation landscapes is crucial for variational quantum algorithms, but full classical simulation is costly; the authors aim to reduce this cost by focusing on local patches.
method: The authors develop a method to classically surrogate a small subregion of an expectation landscape by leveraging initial data from quantum computers, likely using techniques from quantum machine learning or classical surrogates.
result: They demonstrate that classical surrogates for patches of quantum landscapes can be constructed efficiently, potentially enabling faster optimization or analysis of variational algorithms.
conclusion: The work provides a practical approach to reduce quantum resource requirements for variational quantum algorithms by combining quantum and classical computation.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation sensitivity.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, offering a resource for surpassing classical limits in sensing.
method: Reviews theoretical frameworks for critical quantum sensing, including scaling of quantum Fisher information near critical points.
result: Shows how criticality can be exploited to achieve Heisenberg-limited or super-Heisenberg scaling in estimation precision.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing is a promising paradigm, but practical challenges remain in exploiting it experimentally.

title: From Linear Differential Equations To Unitaries: A Moment-Matching Dilation Framework With Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithms
authors: Xiantao Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiantao Li

Mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, enabling the near optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020350] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A moment-matching dilation framework maps nonunitary dynamics to a tight-binding lattice for near-optimal quantum simulation.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers is challenging due to connectivity constraints; this work aims to overcome that.
method: The authors develop a dilation approach that embeds the nonunitary evolution into a larger unitary system using a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice, leveraging moment-matching techniques.
result: The method achieves near-optimal quantum algorithms for simulating linear differential equations, with improved resource scaling.
conclusion: The framework provides an efficient way to simulate nonunitary processes on quantum hardware, with potential applications in quantum simulation and differential equation solving.

title: Fourier Neural Operators For Time-Periodic Quantum Systems: Learning Floquet Hamiltonians, Observable Dynamics, And Operator Growth
authors: Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, and Christopher Earls

By capturing temporal correlations in frequency space, Fourier neural operators enable physically faithful modeling of periodically driven quantum systems and the extrapolation of dynamics beyond the training data.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020340] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: Uses Fourier neural operators to learn Floquet Hamiltonians and dynamics of time-periodic quantum systems.
motivation: Modeling periodically driven quantum systems is computationally expensive; neural operators offer a data-driven approach to capture temporal correlations.
method: Applies Fourier neural operators to learn the Floquet Hamiltonian and predict observable dynamics and operator growth from training data.
result: The method accurately extrapolates dynamics beyond the training time window and captures operator growth behavior.
conclusion: Fourier neural operators are effective for learning and predicting the behavior of time-periodic quantum systems.

title: Abelian Multi-Cycle Codes For Single-Shot Error Correction
authors: Hsiang-Ku Lin, Pak Kau Lim, Alexey A. Kovalev, And Leonid P. Pryadko
abstract:
Author(s): Hsiang-Ku Lin, Pak Kau Lim, Alexey A. Kovalev, and Leonid P. Pryadko

A new family of quantum low-density parity-check codes, which are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes, achieves single-shot fault tolerance and an approximately 1.1% pseudothreshold with significantly shorter block lengths.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020326] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A new family of quantum LDPC codes achieving single-shot fault tolerance with shorter block lengths.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum error correction typically requires multiple rounds of syndrome measurement; single-shot error correction reduces this overhead.
method: The authors construct Abelian multi-cycle codes, which are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes, and analyze their single-shot error correction properties.
result: The codes achieve a pseudothreshold of approximately 1.1% with significantly shorter block lengths compared to existing codes.
conclusion: These codes offer a practical advantage for fault-tolerant quantum computing by reducing the number of syndrome measurement rounds needed.

title: Parallel Logical Measurements Via Quantum Code Surgery
authors: Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, And Theodore J. Yoder
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, and Theodore J. Yoder

Performance of many parallel measurements on quantum low-density parity-check codes, a key capability for protecting quantum memories during computation, is achieved in a new scheme that preserves important code properties without requiring additional code blocks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020325] Published Fri May 08, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a scheme for parallel logical measurements on quantum LDPC codes using code surgery without additional code blocks.
motivation: Efficient parallel measurement is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, but existing methods often require extra resources or degrade code properties.
method: The scheme leverages code surgery techniques on quantum low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes to perform multiple logical measurements simultaneously while preserving the code's distance and other properties.
result: The method enables parallel measurements without needing additional code blocks, maintaining key code parameters.
conclusion: This work advances practical fault-tolerant quantum computing by enabling efficient parallel logical operations on LDPC codes.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining that such violations arise from violating underlying assumptions, and discusses how to engineer materials that exploit these effects.
motivation: Classical thermodynamic bounds are widely assumed to be fundamental, but many measurements exceed them; understanding why and how to design materials that circumvent these bounds is of practical interest.
method: The paper surveys a wide range of examples from different fields where measured properties exceed thermodynamic bounds, and analyzes which assumptions (e.g., equilibrium, linear response, homogeneity) are violated in each case.
result: It identifies common mechanisms for apparent bound violations, such as non-equilibrium conditions, anisotropy, or internal resonances, and shows that these can be harnessed to create materials with extreme properties.
conclusion: While not violating thermodynamics, these materials challenge the universality of classical bounds and offer pathways to novel material design, but the paper is a review without new theoretical or experimental contributions.

title: On-Chip Generation Of Copolarized And Spectrally Separable Photon Pairs
authors: Xiaojie Wang, Lin Zhou, Yue Li, Sakthi Sanjeev Mohanraj, Xiaodong Shi, Zhuoyang Yu, Ran Yang, Xu Chen, Guangxing Wu, Hao Hao, Sihao Wang, Veerendra Dhyani, And Di Zhu
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaojie Wang, Lin Zhou, Yue Li, Sakthi Sanjeev Mohanraj, Xiaodong Shi, Zhuoyang Yu, Ran Yang, Xu Chen, Guangxing Wu, Hao Hao, Sihao Wang, Veerendra Dhyani, and Di Zhu

On-chip generation of high-purity single photons is essential for scalable photonic quantum technologies. Spontaneous parametric down conversion (SPDC) is widely used to generate photon pairs for heralded single-photon sources, but intrinsic spectral correlations of the pairs often limit the purity …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 253801] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: On-chip generation of copolarized and spectrally separable photon pairs via SPDC for high-purity heralded single-photon sources.
motivation: Scalable photonic quantum technologies require high-purity single photons; intrinsic spectral correlations in SPDC limit purity.
method: Design and fabrication of an on-chip SPDC source with engineered phase matching to produce copolarized, spectrally separable photon pairs.
result: Demonstrated generation of photon pairs with high spectral purity and indistinguishability, suitable for heralded single-photon sources.
conclusion: The on-chip source advances integrated photonic quantum information processing by providing high-quality photon pairs.

title: Dissipation Due To Bulk Localized Low-Energy Modes In Strongly Disordered Superconductors
authors: Anton V. Khvalyuk And Mikhail V. Feigel’man
abstract:
Author(s): Anton V. Khvalyuk and Mikhail V. Feigel’man

Microwave dissipation in strongly disordered superconductors is driven by localized collective modes within rare weak spots, a theoretical insight which provides a fresh strategy to enhance coherence times in quantum devices.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256001] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper identifies localized collective modes in rare weak spots as a source of microwave dissipation in strongly disordered superconductors, offering insights to improve coherence times in quantum devices.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating microwave dissipation is crucial for enhancing coherence times in superconducting qubits, a key challenge in quantum computing.
method: The authors theoretically analyze strongly disordered superconductors, focusing on rare weak spots that host localized low-energy collective modes, and compute their contribution to microwave dissipation.
result: They find that dissipation is dominated by these localized modes, providing a microscopic mechanism for loss in disordered superconductors.
conclusion: The results suggest strategies to reduce dissipation by engineering disorder or material properties, potentially improving qubit coherence.

title: Higher-order Liouvillian Exceptional Points In The Dissipative Dynamics Of Quadratic Fermions
authors: Mingtao Xu And Wei Yi
abstract:
Author(s): Mingtao Xu and Wei Yi

We propose a general class of open fermionic models where quadratic Liouvillians governing the dissipative dynamics feature analytically characterized higher-order exceptional points (EPs). Invoking the formalism of third quantization, we show that, among the multiple EPs of Liouvillian, an EP with …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062455] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies higher-order exceptional points in the dissipative dynamics of quadratic fermions, focusing on Liouvillian spectral properties.
motivation: Exceptional points in open quantum systems are of interest for understanding non-Hermitian physics and potential applications in sensing, but the paper's focus is on spectral degeneracies rather than thermodynamic or information-theoretic aspects.
method: The authors use the third quantization formalism to analytically characterize higher-order exceptional points in quadratic fermionic Liouvillians.
result: They identify and classify multiple exceptional points, including an EP with order scaling with system size, and analyze their properties.
conclusion: The work provides a systematic framework for studying higher-order exceptional points in quadratic fermionic dissipative systems, but does not directly address information thermodynamics or quantum information.

title: Proposals For Realizing A Josephson Diode In Atomtronic Circuits
authors: Nalinikanta Pradhan, Rina Kanamoto, M. Bhattacharya, And Pankaj Kumar Mishra
abstract:
Author(s): Nalinikanta Pradhan, Rina Kanamoto, M. Bhattacharya, and Pankaj Kumar Mishra

Nonreciprocal Josephson transport is realized in an atomtronic ring condensate through tunable symmetry breaking induced by asymmetric junction placement and driving. The resulting Josephson diode effect achieves efficiencies up to 91%, providing a highly controllable neutral-atom platform for future quantum circuitry and atomtronic devices.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L061502] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a Josephson diode in atomtronic circuits using asymmetric junction placement and driving to achieve nonreciprocal transport with up to 91% efficiency.
motivation: To realize a highly controllable neutral-atom platform for quantum circuitry and atomtronic devices by demonstrating a Josephson diode effect.
method: The authors use a ring condensate with asymmetric junction placement and driving to break symmetry and achieve nonreciprocal Josephson transport.
result: They achieve a Josephson diode effect with efficiencies up to 91%.
conclusion: The work provides a controllable neutral-atom platform for future quantum circuitry and atomtronic devices.

title: Phonon Scattering From Spatial Relaxation Of One-dimensional Bose Gases
authors: Bilal Alilou, Clément Duval, Frederick Del Pozo, And Nicolas Cherroret
abstract:
Author(s): Bilal Alilou, Clément Duval, Frederick Del Pozo, and Nicolas Cherroret

We theoretically investigate the nonequilibrium relaxation of a spatial density modulation in a one-dimensional nonintegrable Bose gas and its connection to the equilibrium scattering rate [MATH] of the system's phononic excitations. We show that the density relaxation is generically go…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063321] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies nonequilibrium relaxation of density modulations in 1D Bose gases and connects it to phonon scattering rates.
motivation: Understanding relaxation dynamics in low-dimensional quantum gases is important for non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics.
method: Theoretical analysis using hydrodynamic and kinetic approaches to relate density relaxation to phonon scattering.
result: Density relaxation is generically governed by the equilibrium phonon scattering rate, with a crossover from ballistic to diffusive behavior.
conclusion: The work provides a link between non-equilibrium relaxation and equilibrium scattering, relevant for quantum thermalization.

title: Signatures Of Quantum Chaos And Complexity In The Ising Model On Random Graphs
authors: G. J. Sreejith And Sandipan Manna
abstract:
Author(s): G. J. Sreejith and Sandipan Manna

We investigate signatures of quantum chaos in the mixed-field quantum Ising model on finite-size Erdős–Rényi graphs using probes scalable on near-term quantum devices. Upon tuning the graph connectivity, the system exhibits a crossover from a localized regime at low connectivity, through a chaotic r…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214322] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: Studies signatures of quantum chaos and complexity in the mixed-field Ising model on random graphs using probes scalable on near-term quantum devices.
motivation: To understand the crossover from localized to chaotic regimes in quantum many-body systems on random graphs, which is relevant for quantum simulation and complexity.
method: Uses spectral statistics (level spacing ratio) and out-of-time-ordered correlators (OTOCs) as probes of quantum chaos, applied to the mixed-field Ising model on Erdős–Rényi graphs with varying connectivity.
result: Observes a crossover from localized to chaotic behavior as graph connectivity increases, with OTOCs showing signatures of scrambling and complexity growth.
conclusion: The random graph Ising model provides a tunable platform to study quantum chaos and complexity, with potential implications for quantum simulation and understanding thermalization.

title: Nonuniversal Thermal Hall Responses In Fractional Quantum Hall Droplets
authors: Fei Tan, Yuzhu Wang, Xinghao Wang, And Bo Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Fei Tan, Yuzhu Wang, Xinghao Wang, and Bo Yang

We analytically compute the thermal Hall conductance (THC) of fractional quantum Hall droplets under realistic conditions that go beyond the idealized linear edge theory with conformal symmetry. Specifically, we consider finite-size effects at low temperature, nonzero self-energies of quasiholes, an…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L241118] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: Analytical computation of thermal Hall conductance in fractional quantum Hall droplets beyond idealized edge theory, including finite-size and self-energy effects.
motivation: To understand deviations from universal thermal Hall conductance predictions in realistic finite-size quantum Hall systems.
method: Analytical calculation using conformal field theory and edge state formalism with corrections for finite temperature and quasihole self-energies.
result: The thermal Hall conductance is nonuniversal and depends on system size, temperature, and quasihole self-energies, deviating from the expected quantized value.
conclusion: Realistic fractional quantum Hall droplets exhibit nonuniversal thermal Hall responses, which must be accounted for in experiments and interpretations.

title: Engineering Biquadratic Interactions In Spin-1 Chains By Spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ Spacers
authors: Yasser Saleem, Weronika Pasek, Marek Korkusinski, Moritz Cygorek, And Paweł Potasz
abstract:
Author(s): Yasser Saleem, Weronika Pasek, Marek Korkusinski, Moritz Cygorek, and Paweł Potasz

Low-dimensional quantum systems host a variety of exotic states, such as symmetry-protected topological ground states in spin-1 Haldane chains. Real-world realizations of such states could serve as practical quantum simulators for quantum phases if the interactions can be controlled. However, many p…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235143] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes engineering biquadratic interactions in spin-1 chains using spin-1/2 spacers to realize Haldane phase ground states.
motivation: To achieve controllable interactions in low-dimensional quantum systems for simulating exotic quantum phases like symmetry-protected topological states.
method: The authors design a spin-1 chain with spin-1/2 spacers and analyze the effective interactions using perturbation theory and numerical simulations.
result: They show that biquadratic interactions can be engineered and tuned, enabling the realization of the Haldane phase.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical route to building quantum simulators for topological phases in spin chains.

title: Two-temperature Ashkin-Teller Model
authors: Sertac Cengiz And M. Cemal Yalabik
abstract:
Author(s): Sertac Cengiz and M. Cemal Yalabik

Phase diagram of the two-temperature Ashkin-Teller model with Kawasaki dynamics has been investigated. The system is placed in contact with two heat baths at different temperatures, each of which controls the dynamics of nearest-neighbor exchange in the two perpendicular directions. It was observed …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064144] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Phase diagram of a two-temperature Ashkin-Teller model with Kawasaki dynamics is studied.
motivation: To understand non-equilibrium steady states in a system coupled to two heat baths at different temperatures.
method: Monte Carlo simulations of the Ashkin-Teller model with Kawasaki dynamics, where exchange rates in perpendicular directions are controlled by separate heat baths.
result: Observed phase transitions and phase diagram features under the two-temperature drive.
conclusion: The two-temperature Ashkin-Teller model exhibits rich non-equilibrium behavior, but the work is primarily a statistical mechanics study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics of computation.

title: Vanishing Correlations In Stochastic And Bistochastic Controlled Circuits
authors: Pavel Kos, Bruno Bertini, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Pavel Kos, Bruno Bertini, and Tomaž Prosen

We study the dynamics of circuits composed of stochastic and bistochastic controlled gates. This type of dynamics arises from quantum circuits with random controlled gates, as well as in stochastic circuits and deterministic classical cellular automata. We prove that stochastic and bistochastic cont…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064139] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper proves that correlations vanish in stochastic and bistochastic controlled circuits, with implications for quantum circuits and classical cellular automata.
motivation: Understanding the dynamics of random quantum circuits and their classical counterparts is important for quantum information and statistical mechanics.
method: The authors analyze circuits composed of stochastic and bistochastic controlled gates, using mathematical proofs to show that correlations decay to zero.
result: They prove that for both stochastic and bistochastic controlled circuits, all correlations vanish after a finite number of steps.
conclusion: This result establishes a fundamental property of such circuits, which may inform the design of quantum circuits and the study of thermalization.

title: Tunable Intertwining Via Collective Excitations
authors: András Szabó And R. Chitra
abstract:
Author(s): András Szabó and R. Chitra

Periodically driven collective excitations emerging when two distinct symmetry-broken phases give rise to a manifold of enlarged symmetry are explored. The work proposes that the resulting driven phase diagram hosting out-of-equilibrium intertwined phases is accessible in state-of-the-art matter-cavity experimental setups.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022053] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies periodically driven collective excitations in symmetry-broken phases, proposing a tunable intertwined phase accessible in matter-cavity setups.
motivation: To explore out-of-equilibrium phases arising from driving collective excitations in systems with enlarged symmetry manifolds.
method: Theoretical analysis of periodically driven symmetry-broken phases, deriving the driven phase diagram and identifying conditions for intertwined phases.
result: A tunable intertwined phase is predicted, which can be realized in state-of-the-art matter-cavity experiments.
conclusion: The work provides a pathway to engineer and control intertwined phases in driven quantum systems.

title: Optical Spin Pumping In Silicon
authors: Stefano Achilli, Damiano Marian, Mario Lodari, Luca Moreschini, Emiliano Bonera, Giordano Scappucci, Jacopo Pedrini, Michele Virgilio, And Fabio Pezzoli
abstract:
Author(s): Stefano Achilli, Damiano Marian, Mario Lodari, Luca Moreschini, Emiliano Bonera, Giordano Scappucci, Jacopo Pedrini, Michele Virgilio, and Fabio Pezzoli

The optical generation of an out-of-equilibrium spin population is a keystone process for quantum technologies and spintronics alike. Although this is an established technique for studying direct band-gap semiconductors, it has been proven limited in materials that possess weak oscillator strengths …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023302] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optical spin pumping in silicon, a key process for quantum technologies and spintronics, but focuses on material characterization rather than quantum information or networking applications.
motivation: Optical spin pumping is essential for generating spin polarization in semiconductors, but its application in indirect band-gap materials like silicon has been limited due to weak oscillator strengths.
method: The authors use optical excitation and detection techniques to generate and measure out-of-equilibrium spin populations in silicon, analyzing the spin dynamics and polarization.
result: They achieve efficient optical spin pumping in silicon, demonstrating significant spin polarization and long spin lifetimes.
conclusion: The work establishes silicon as a viable platform for optical spin control, relevant for spintronics and potential quantum technologies, but does not directly address quantum information processing or networking.

title: Far-field Heat Transfer And Monochromatic Thermal Currents In A Cylindrical Nonreciprocal Cavity
authors: Guillem Masdemont, Julien Legendre, And Georgia T. Papadakis
abstract:
Author(s): Guillem Masdemont, Julien Legendre, and Georgia T. Papadakis

Breaking Kirchhoff's law of thermal radiation yields opportunities in one-way radiative thermal transport and circuitry. We investigate its consequences in the far-field regime in cylindrical cavities, by employing a specular ray-tracing algorithm. At thermal equilibrium, we show that violation of K…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023293] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies far-field heat transfer and monochromatic thermal currents in cylindrical nonreciprocal cavities, focusing on breaking Kirchhoff's law.
motivation: To explore the consequences of nonreciprocal thermal radiation in far-field regimes for one-way radiative thermal transport and circuitry.
method: A specular ray-tracing algorithm is employed to analyze thermal equilibrium and heat transfer in cylindrical cavities with nonreciprocal materials.
result: Violation of Kirchhoff's law enables monochromatic thermal currents and directional heat transfer in the far-field.
conclusion: Nonreciprocal cavities offer new opportunities for thermal management and energy conversion, but the work is primarily applied and not directly tied to quantum information or thermodynamics of computation.

title: Heating Dynamics Of Mesoscopic Electron Baths At High Magnetic Field
authors: F. Zanichelli, A. Veillon, C. Piquard, A. Aassime, Y. Sato, A. Cavanna, Y. Jin, J. Folk, U. Gennser, A. Anthore, And F. Pierre
abstract:
Author(s): F. Zanichelli, A. Veillon, C. Piquard, A. Aassime, Y. Sato, A. Cavanna, Y. Jin, J. Folk, U. Gennser, A. Anthore, and F. Pierre

Time-resolved noise thermometry on mesoscopic metallic islands reveals a two-step thermalization process arising from the interplay between electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021013] Published Tue Apr 14, 2026.
tldr: Time-resolved noise thermometry reveals a two-step thermalization process in mesoscopic metallic islands at high magnetic field, involving electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.
motivation: Understanding thermalization dynamics in mesoscopic systems is important for quantum thermodynamics and device applications, but the paper focuses on a specific condensed matter system rather than general principles.
method: The authors use time-resolved noise thermometry to measure electron temperature dynamics in mesoscopic metallic islands under high magnetic field.
result: They observe a two-step thermalization process attributed to the interplay between electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.
conclusion: The work provides insight into heating dynamics in mesoscopic systems but is not directly aligned with core information thermodynamics topics like fluctuation theorems or quantum heat engines.

title: Symmetry-Accelerated Classical Simulation Of Clifford-Dominated Circuits
authors: Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, And Juani Bermejo-Vega
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, and Juani Bermejo-Vega

Strong and weak symmetry reductions render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020356] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents symmetry-accelerated classical simulation of Clifford-dominated circuits using optimal stabilizer decompositions.
motivation: Classical simulation of quantum circuits is important for benchmarking and verification, but stabilizer-based methods become inefficient for circuits with many non-Clifford gates. The authors aim to extend the reach of classical simulation by exploiting symmetries.
method: They develop strong and weak symmetry reduction techniques to render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries, enabling simulation of circuits with a high proportion of Clifford gates.
result: The symmetry reductions significantly lower the computational cost of stabilizer decompositions, allowing simulation of larger circuits than previously possible.
conclusion: Symmetry-accelerated stabilizer decompositions provide a practical classical simulation method for Clifford-dominated circuits, which are common in many quantum algorithms.

title: Nontrivial Multiproduct Commutation Relation Toward Reducing $T$-Count In Sequential Pauli-Based Computation
authors: Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, and Keisuke Fujii

By harnessing nontrivial commuting structures in quantum circuits, a novel multiproduct commutation relation significantly reduces the costly
[PRX Quantum 7, 020345] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: A multiproduct commutation relation reduces T-count in sequential Pauli-based computation.
motivation: Reducing T-count is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, but existing methods are limited.
method: The authors derive a nontrivial commutation relation for multiproducts of Pauli operators and apply it to sequential Pauli-based circuits.
result: The relation enables significant T-count reduction compared to standard approaches.
conclusion: This work provides a new tool for optimizing fault-tolerant quantum circuits.

title: Quantifying Robustness And Locality Of Majorana Bound States In Interacting Systems
authors: William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, And Viktor Svensson
abstract:
Author(s): William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, and Viktor Svensson

Motivated by recent quantum-dot experiments, this work rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems to quantify their protection and feasibility for non-Abelian braiding.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020341] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: Defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems and quantifies their robustness and locality for non-Abelian braiding.
motivation: Recent quantum-dot experiments motivate a rigorous definition of Majorana bound states in interacting systems to assess their protection and feasibility for topological quantum computing.
method: The authors develop theoretical criteria to quantify the robustness and locality of Majorana bound states in the presence of interactions, using numerical simulations and analytical models.
result: They provide a framework to distinguish true Majorana bound states from trivial Andreev bound states, and quantify how interactions affect their non-Abelian properties.
conclusion: The work establishes practical measures for identifying Majorana bound states in realistic interacting systems, guiding experimental efforts toward topological qubits.

title: Efficient Simulation Of Logical Magic State Preparation Protocols
authors: Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, And Isaac H. Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, and Isaac H. Kim

Classical simulation of a large class of logical magic state preparation protocols is made scalable and efficient via propagating errors to the end of the circuit.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020329] Published Thu May 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents an efficient classical simulation method for logical magic state preparation protocols by propagating errors to the end of the circuit.
motivation: Magic state preparation is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but simulating these protocols classically is computationally expensive. The authors aim to make such simulations scalable and efficient.
method: They develop a technique that propagates errors through the circuit to the end, reducing the complexity of simulating logical magic state preparation protocols.
result: The method achieves efficient classical simulation for a large class of logical magic state preparation protocols, enabling analysis of error thresholds and resource requirements.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for evaluating magic state preparation protocols, which is important for the development of fault-tolerant quantum computers.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, unifying approaches for complex systems in chemistry, ecology, and epidemiology.
motivation: Stochastic reaction-diffusion systems model many complex phenomena, but existing methods are diverse and fragmented; a unified framework is needed.
method: The authors review field-theoretic techniques, including path integrals and Doi-Peliti formalism, to treat stochastic reaction-diffusion processes.
result: They show how these methods provide a systematic way to compute correlation functions, fluctuation spectra, and large deviations.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods offer a powerful and unifying approach for analyzing stochastic reaction-diffusion systems across disciplines.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlations and optical control.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated systems for novel material properties.
method: Comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental advances, including dynamical mean-field theory and pump-probe spectroscopy.
result: Identifies key mechanisms for photodoping, metastable phases, and nonthermal orders like superconductivity and magnetism.
conclusion: Photoexcitation in Mott insulators enables rich nonequilibrium phenomena with potential for ultrafast control of material properties.

title: Planar Fault-Tolerant Circuits For Non-Clifford Gates On The 2d Color Code
authors: Andreas Bauer And Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente
abstract:
Author(s): Andreas Bauer and Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente

A family of scalable circuits designed for universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings called twisted color circuits is introduced and can achieve fault tolerance with a “just-in-time” decoder.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020367] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces planar fault-tolerant circuits for non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code, enabling universal quantum computing with a just-in-time decoder.
motivation: Fault-tolerant implementation of non-Clifford gates is a key challenge for universal quantum computing, especially on planar architectures with nearest-neighbor couplings.
method: The authors design twisted color circuits that achieve fault tolerance for non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code, using a just-in-time decoder to handle errors.
result: The proposed circuits are scalable and compatible with planar chips, demonstrating a practical path to universal fault-tolerant quantum computing.
conclusion: Twisted color circuits provide a viable approach for implementing non-Clifford gates fault-tolerantly on the 2D color code, advancing toward scalable quantum computers.

title: Hexapartite Active Nonlinear Feedback Control In Four-wave Mixing With A Spatially Structured Pump
authors: Guanjun Zeng, Xiaozhou Pan, Kai Zhang, And Jietai Jing
abstract:
Author(s): Guanjun Zeng, Xiaozhou Pan, Kai Zhang, and Jietai Jing

In the field of quantum information science, feedback control has become an important method for preparing and manipulating nonclassical beams. Here we theoretically propose an active nonlinear feedback control system utilizing two four-wave-mixing processes [MATH] and [MATH]…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062448] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a hexapartite active nonlinear feedback control system using two four-wave-mixing processes with a spatially structured pump for manipulating nonclassical beams.
motivation: Feedback control is important for preparing and manipulating nonclassical beams in quantum information science, and the authors aim to extend this to a hexapartite system.
method: The authors theoretically design a system with two four-wave-mixing processes and a spatially structured pump to achieve active nonlinear feedback control.
result: The system generates hexapartite entangled states and allows control over the entanglement structure.
conclusion: The proposed scheme provides a method for generating and controlling multipartite entanglement, which may be useful for quantum information processing.

title: Real-Space Topology And Charge Order In The Haldane-Holstein Model
authors: Sebastião Dos A. Sousa-Júnior, Julián Faúndez, Tarik P. Cysne, Richard T. Scalettar, And Rubem Mondaini
abstract:
Author(s): Sebastião dos A. Sousa-Júnior, Julián Faúndez, Tarik P. Cysne, Richard T. Scalettar, and Rubem Mondaini

We study the half-filled Haldane-Holstein model, where a paradigmatic Chern insulator is coupled to fully dynamical phonons, and provide an unbiased characterization of how retarded electron-phonon interactions destabilize Chern topology. Using determinant quantum Monte Carlo, we find that increasin…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256501] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Haldane-Holstein model, focusing on how electron-phonon interactions destabilize Chern topology and induce charge order, using determinant quantum Monte Carlo.
motivation: To understand the interplay between topological order and electron-phonon coupling in a Chern insulator, which is relevant for condensed matter physics but not directly tied to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Determinant quantum Monte Carlo simulations of the half-filled Haldane-Holstein model with dynamical phonons.
result: Increasing electron-phonon coupling leads to a transition from a Chern insulator to a charge-ordered state, destroying the topological phase.
conclusion: Retarded electron-phonon interactions can destabilize Chern topology, highlighting the fragility of topological phases in the presence of strong coupling to phonons.

title: Increasing The Stability Of A Superfluid In A Rotating Necklace Potential
authors: Giulio Nesti And Luca Pezzè
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Nesti and Luca Pezzè

Recent experiments have probed the stability of ring superfluids in the presence of Josephson barriers or Gaussian impurities. Here we present a theoretical analysis that extends beyond the regimes explored so far. We study the onset of dynamical instabilities in a ring superfluid, addressing both t…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063326] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies dynamical instabilities in a ring superfluid with a rotating necklace potential, focusing on stability beyond previous experimental regimes.
motivation: Recent experiments probed ring superfluid stability with barriers; this work extends the theoretical analysis to new parameter regimes.
method: Theoretical analysis using mean-field and Bogoliubov methods to study onset of dynamical instabilities in a ring superfluid with a rotating necklace potential.
result: Identifies conditions for increased stability and characterizes instability thresholds as a function of potential strength and rotation speed.
conclusion: The rotating necklace potential can enhance superfluid stability under certain conditions, relevant for ultracold atom experiments.

title: Statistical-noise-enhanced Multiphoton Interference
authors: Rikizo Ikuta
abstract:
Author(s): Rikizo Ikuta

Photon statistics plays a governing role in multiphoton interference. While interference visibility in the standard two-photon case, known as Hong-Ou-Mandel interference, monotonically degrades with higher intensity correlation functions, we show that this monotonicity does not hold for three-photon…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063731] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that statistical noise can enhance multiphoton interference visibility beyond the monotonic degradation expected from standard two-photon interference.
motivation: To understand how higher-order intensity correlations affect multiphoton interference, specifically whether the monotonic degradation seen in two-photon Hong-Ou-Mandel interference extends to three-photon cases.
method: Theoretical analysis of multiphoton interference with statistical noise, using correlation functions and quantum optics formalism.
result: For three-photon interference, the visibility does not monotonically degrade with higher-order correlations; statistical noise can actually enhance interference.
conclusion: Statistical noise can be beneficial in multiphoton interference, challenging the conventional wisdom that noise always degrades quantum interference.

title: Triggering And Switching Of Topological Phases And non-Hermitian Transitions In A Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Circuit With Long-range Hopping And Synthetic Gauge Fields
authors: Jing Cheng, Cheng-Jun Han, Jin-Yan Hu, Mo-Nan Wang, And Y. P. Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Jing Cheng, Cheng-Jun Han, Jin-Yan Hu, Mo-Nan Wang, and Y. P. Wang

We propose an extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain that integrates long-range hopping and a synthetic Peierls phase, providing a tunable circuit platform to trigger and control non-Hermitian transitions and topological phase transitions. We show that the long-range hopping strength acts as a trigger …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063732] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological phase transitions and non-Hermitian transitions in a Su-Schrieffer-Heeger circuit with long-range hopping and synthetic gauge fields.
motivation: To understand how long-range hopping and synthetic gauge fields can trigger and control topological and non-Hermitian transitions in a tunable circuit platform.
method: The authors propose an extended SSH chain model with long-range hopping and a synthetic Peierls phase, and analyze its topological phases and non-Hermitian transitions using theoretical and numerical methods.
result: They show that long-range hopping strength acts as a trigger for topological phase transitions, and synthetic gauge fields enable switching between different topological phases.
conclusion: The work provides a platform for controlling topological and non-Hermitian phenomena, with potential applications in topological photonics and quantum simulation.

title: Theory Of Anomalous Landau-Zener Tunneling Induced By Nonlinear Coupling
authors: Wen-Yuan Wang And Hong-Juan Meng
abstract:
Author(s): Wen-Yuan Wang and Hong-Juan Meng

We develop a general theory of Landau-Zener (LZ) tunneling in a two-level system with amplitude-dependent, sign-reversible nonlinear coupling, distinguishing it fundamentally from conventional on-site nonlinearity. Through a combination of analytical and phase-space analysis, we show that beyond a c…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062218] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Develops a theory of Landau-Zener tunneling in a two-level system with amplitude-dependent nonlinear coupling.
motivation: To understand the effect of nonlinear coupling on Landau-Zener tunneling, which differs from conventional on-site nonlinearity.
method: Combines analytical and phase-space analysis to study the two-level system.
result: Shows that beyond a critical coupling, anomalous tunneling behavior emerges.
conclusion: The work provides a general theory for nonlinear Landau-Zener tunneling with sign-reversible coupling.

title: Equilibrium And Dynamical Quantum Phase Transitions In Dipolar Atomic Josephson Junctions
authors: Cesare Vianello, Giovanni Mazzarella, And Luca Salasnich
abstract:
Author(s): Cesare Vianello, Giovanni Mazzarella, and Luca Salasnich

An atomic Josephson junction realized with dipolar bosons in a double-well potential can be described by an extended Bose-Hubbard model in which dipolar interactions generate an effective on-site interaction and nearest-neighbor pair tunneling. Using mean-field theory and exact diagonalization, we i…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063318] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies equilibrium and dynamical quantum phase transitions in dipolar atomic Josephson junctions using mean-field theory and exact diagonalization.
motivation: To understand the effects of dipolar interactions and pair tunneling on quantum phase transitions in a bosonic Josephson junction.
method: The authors employ a mean-field approach and exact diagonalization of an extended Bose-Hubbard model with on-site and nearest-neighbor interactions.
result: They identify equilibrium phase transitions and dynamical transitions, showing that dipolar interactions and pair tunneling significantly alter the phase diagram and dynamics.
conclusion: The work provides insights into quantum phase transitions in dipolar systems but does not directly connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Exceptional Rings Emerging In A non-Hermitian Rice-Mele Ladder
authors: Ensuo Ma And Zhi Song
abstract:
Author(s): Ensuo Ma and Zhi Song

Weyl exceptional lines typically occur in three-dimensional (3D) topological semimetals; however, they also emerge in the parameter space of one-dimensional (1D) systems. In this work, we study the impact of dissipation on the nodal ring in a 3D topological semimetal. We find that the energy spectru…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235150] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies exceptional rings in a non-Hermitian Rice-Mele ladder, focusing on topological semimetal physics in parameter space.
motivation: To understand the impact of dissipation on nodal rings in 3D topological semimetals by studying a 1D model.
method: The authors analyze a non-Hermitian Rice-Mele ladder model with dissipation, deriving the energy spectrum and identifying exceptional rings in parameter space.
result: Exceptional rings emerge in the parameter space of the 1D system, analogous to Weyl exceptional lines in 3D.
conclusion: The work extends the concept of exceptional rings to lower-dimensional systems, revealing topological features in non-Hermitian settings.

title: Taxonomy Of Integrable And Ground-state Solvable Models: Jastrow Wave Functions On Graphs And Parent Hamiltonians
authors: Nilanjan Sasmal And Adolfo Del Campo
abstract:
Author(s): Nilanjan Sasmal and Adolfo del Campo

We introduce a family of many-body systems of distinguishable continuous-variable particles in which interparticle interactions are set by the adjacency matrix of a graph. The ground-state wave function of such systems is of a generalized Jastrow form involving the product of pair-correlation functi…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235151] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a family of many-body systems with Jastrow ground states on graphs, focusing on integrability and exact solvability.
motivation: To classify and construct exactly solvable many-body models with Jastrow wave functions, linking graph theory to quantum many-body physics.
method: Defines a Hamiltonian based on the adjacency matrix of a graph, with ground state given by a generalized Jastrow product of pair-correlation functions.
result: Identifies conditions for integrability and exact solvability, providing a taxonomy of models on various graphs.
conclusion: The framework unifies several known solvable models and offers a systematic way to generate new ones, but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Model With Competing Rashba Spin-orbit Interactions, Higher Order Hopping, And Domain Wall
authors: Hemant Kumar Sharma, Arijit Saha, And Saptarshi Mandal
abstract:
Author(s): Hemant Kumar Sharma, Arijit Saha, and Saptarshi Mandal

We investigate an extended spin-full Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model preserving chiral symmetry. It contains spin-mixing and nonmixing Rashba spin-orbit interactions, complex next to next nearest neighbor (NNNN) hopping. Using the theory of non-Hermitian matrices, we construct a Hamiltonian functio…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245143] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies an extended SSH model with Rashba spin-orbit interactions and higher-order hopping, focusing on topological phases and domain walls.
motivation: To understand the interplay of spin-orbit coupling and longer-range hopping in topological insulators, extending the well-known SSH model.
method: Constructs a non-Hermitian Hamiltonian function and analyzes topological invariants and domain wall states.
result: Identifies topological phases characterized by winding numbers and finds domain wall states at interfaces.
conclusion: The extended SSH model exhibits rich topological behavior due to spin-orbit and higher-order hopping, relevant for spintronics and topological matter.

title: Geometric Superfluid Weight In Multigap Superconductors
authors: Jie Cao, Fenghua Qi, Yuanyuan Xiang, And Guojun Jin
abstract:
Author(s): Jie Cao, Fenghua Qi, Yuanyuan Xiang, and Guojun Jin

Driven by quantum geometric effects, nontrivial superfluid weight in flat-band superconductors has recently attracted considerable attention. In this paper, we show that for multigap superconductors, in which each band possesses a distinct gap function, the second-order correction to the gap functio…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214518] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies geometric contributions to superfluid weight in multigap superconductors, focusing on band geometry and gap functions.
motivation: Understanding superfluid weight in flat-band superconductors is important, but the paper's focus on multigap superconductors and geometric effects is not aligned with the user's research interests.
method: The authors derive second-order corrections to the gap function and compute superfluid weight using a multiband BCS-like formalism.
result: They find that geometric superfluid weight can be significant in multigap systems, depending on band structure and gap symmetry.
conclusion: Geometric effects play a crucial role in superfluid weight of multigap superconductors, but the work is primarily a condensed matter physics result without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Deconfined Gapless Phases And Criticalities In The Shastry-Sutherland Antiferromagnet
authors: Lv-Cheng Chen And Zheng-Xin Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Lv-Cheng Chen and Zheng-Xin Liu

Antiferromagnets on the Shastry-Sutherland lattice have attracted lots of research interest due to the possible existence of deconfined criticality. In the present work, we study the [MATH] model using variational Monte Carlo (VMC) method, where [MATH], a…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224440] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies deconfined criticality in the Shastry-Sutherland antiferromagnet using variational Monte Carlo.
motivation: To investigate the existence of deconfined criticality in a frustrated quantum magnet.
method: Variational Monte Carlo (VMC) method applied to the Shastry-Sutherland model.
result: Identifies deconfined gapless phases and criticalities in the phase diagram.
conclusion: The Shastry-Sutherland antiferromagnet hosts deconfined critical points, relevant to condensed matter physics.

title: Noninvertible Kramers-Wannier Duality Symmetries For The Discrete-time Quantum Ising Chain
authors: Akash Sinha, Pramod Padmanabhan, And Vladimir Korepin
abstract:
Author(s): Akash Sinha, Pramod Padmanabhan, and Vladimir Korepin

Integrable Trotterization provides a method to evolve a continuous-time integrable many-body system in discrete time, such that it retains its conserved quantities. Here, we explicitly show that the first-order Trotterization of the critical transverse-field Ising model is integrable. The discrete-t…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235141] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies noninvertible Kramers-Wannier duality symmetries in the discrete-time quantum Ising chain, focusing on integrability and conserved quantities.
motivation: To understand how integrability is preserved under Trotterization and to explore noninvertible symmetries in discrete-time quantum systems.
method: The authors use integrable Trotterization to discretize the critical transverse-field Ising model and analyze its symmetries, including Kramers-Wannier duality.
result: They show that the first-order Trotterization of the critical transverse-field Ising model is integrable and exhibits noninvertible Kramers-Wannier duality symmetries.
conclusion: The work provides a discrete-time integrable model with noninvertible symmetries, contributing to the study of quantum many-body systems and dualities.

title: Nonreciprocal Blume-Capel Model With Antisymmetric Single-ion Anisotropies
authors: Arjun R, Pratyush Prakash Patra, And A. V. Anil Kumar
abstract:
Author(s): Arjun R, Pratyush Prakash Patra, and A. V. Anil Kumar

We investigate the interplay between nonreciprocal interactions and chemical-potential imbalance in a two-species nonreciprocal Blume-Capel model. Combining a systematic mean-field bifurcation analysis with large-scale Monte Carlo simulations in two and three dimensions, we map the model's dynamical…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064140] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a nonreciprocal Blume-Capel model with antisymmetric single-ion anisotropies using mean-field theory and Monte Carlo simulations.
motivation: To understand the interplay between nonreciprocal interactions and chemical-potential imbalance in a two-species spin model.
method: Combines systematic mean-field bifurcation analysis with large-scale Monte Carlo simulations in two and three dimensions.
result: Maps the dynamical phase diagram and identifies novel phases driven by nonreciprocity.
conclusion: Nonreciprocal interactions lead to rich nonequilibrium behavior in the Blume-Capel model.

title: One-particle Density Matrix Framework For Mode-shell Correspondence: Characterizing Topology In Amorphous Higher-order Topological Insulators
authors: Miguel F. Martínez, Lucien Jezequel, Jens H. Bardarson, Thomas Klein Kvorning, And Julia D. Hannukainen
abstract:
Author(s): Miguel F. Martínez, Lucien Jezequel, Jens H. Bardarson, Thomas Klein Kvorning, and Julia D. Hannukainen

We present a framework for characterizing higher-order topological phases directly from the one-particle density matrix, without any reference to an underlying Hamiltonian. Our approach extends the mode-shell correspondence, originally formulated for single-particle Hamiltonians, to Gaussian states …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023320] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: A framework for characterizing higher-order topological phases in amorphous systems using the one-particle density matrix.
motivation: To extend topological characterization to amorphous materials where traditional band-structure methods fail.
method: Extends the mode-shell correspondence to Gaussian states via the one-particle density matrix, without reference to a Hamiltonian.
result: Demonstrates that higher-order topological invariants can be computed from the density matrix, applicable to amorphous systems.
conclusion: Provides a general method to identify topological phases in disordered systems, broadening the scope of topological insulators.

title: Disorder-induced Topological Phases In A Two-dimensional Chern Insulator With Strong Magnetic Disorder
authors: Devesh Vaish And Michael Potthoff
abstract:
Author(s): Devesh Vaish and Michael Potthoff

Strong directional disorder in local magnetic moments coupled to a Chern insulator gives rise to topological phases that cannot be realized in any clean system and are therefore genuinely disorder driven. We demonstrate this in a spinful Qi-Wu-Zhang model of a two-dimensional Chern insulator coupled…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023312] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies disorder-induced topological phases in a Chern insulator with strong magnetic disorder, which is a condensed matter physics topic without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To explore whether strong directional disorder in local magnetic moments can generate topological phases that are absent in clean systems.
method: The authors use a spinful Qi-Wu-Zhang model of a two-dimensional Chern insulator coupled to magnetic moments and analyze the topological properties under strong disorder.
result: They demonstrate that disorder can induce topological phases that are genuinely disorder-driven and not realizable in clean systems.
conclusion: Disorder can be a resource for realizing novel topological phases in Chern insulators.

title: General Spin Models From Noncollinear Spin Density Functional Theory And Spin-cluster Expansion
authors: Tomonori Tanaka And Yoshihiro Gohda
abstract:
Author(s): Tomonori Tanaka and Yoshihiro Gohda

We present a data-efficient framework for constructing general classical spin Hamiltonians by combining the spin-cluster expansion (SCE) with fully self-consistent noncollinear spin density functional theory (DFT). The key idea is to fit the SCE model to magnetic torques rather than to total energie…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023300] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A data-efficient framework combining spin-cluster expansion with noncollinear spin DFT to construct classical spin Hamiltonians from magnetic torques.
motivation: To efficiently derive accurate spin models for complex magnetic materials without relying on total energy calculations.
method: Fits spin-cluster expansion models to magnetic torques computed from self-consistent noncollinear spin DFT.
result: Demonstrates that torque-based fitting yields accurate spin Hamiltonians with fewer DFT calculations than energy-based methods.
conclusion: The proposed framework is a practical tool for constructing spin models for large-scale simulations of magnetic materials.

title: Complexity-Theoretic Foundations Of BosonSampling With A Linear Number Of Modes
authors: Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, And Michał Oszmaniec
abstract:
Author(s): Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, and Michał Oszmaniec

Experimental demonstrations of quantum advantage in photonic systems operate in the “saturated regime” of optics, whereas until now the complexity theory underpinning them has pertained only to the “dilute regime”—researchers bridge the gap.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021059] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes the complexity-theoretic foundations for BosonSampling in the saturated regime with a linear number of modes, proving that approximate sampling is hard for classical computers under standard assumptions.
motivation: Previous BosonSampling complexity proofs assumed a dilute regime where the number of photons is much smaller than the number of modes, but experimental demonstrations operate in the saturated regime where the number of photons scales linearly with modes. This gap needed to be bridged to justify quantum advantage claims in current experiments.
method: The authors develop new techniques based on the permanent-of-Gaussians conjecture and anticoncentration properties to prove that approximate BosonSampling in the saturated regime is #P-hard, using reductions from random circuit sampling and worst-case to average-case reductions.
