result: They show that BosonSampling with a linear number of modes is classically hard to simulate approximately, assuming the permanent-of-Gaussians conjecture and the non-collapse of the polynomial hierarchy. This provides rigorous complexity-theoretic support for near-term photonic quantum advantage experiments.
conclusion: The work validates that current photonic quantum advantage experiments operating in the saturated regime are indeed demonstrating a quantum computational advantage, and it opens the door to more efficient BosonSampling implementations.

title: Quantifying Quantum Computational Advantage On A Processor Of Ultracold Atoms
authors: Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:

method: Uses an ultracold-atom processor to simulate the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system and benchmarks against classical simulations.
result: The quantum processor outperforms classical methods, indicating a quantum computational advantage.
conclusion: Ultracold-atom processors can achieve quantum advantage for simulating many-body dynamics, with potential for practical applications.

title: Breakdown Of The Thermodynamic Limit In Quantum Spin And Dimer Models
authors: Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, And Victor Galitski
abstract:

[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021020] Published Mon Apr 27, 2026.
tldr: Geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models challenges the thermodynamic limit.
motivation: To understand how domain shape can alter macroscopic ground states in quantum spin and dimer models.
method: Theoretical analysis of quantum dimer models with geometry-induced phase separation.
result: Domain shape fundamentally changes the ground state, breaking the thermodynamic limit assumption.
conclusion: Traditional assumptions about the thermodynamic limit may not hold in certain quantum spin systems.

title: Grand Challenge Of Quantum Applications
authors: Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. Mcclean, Thomas O’brien, And Nicholas C. Rubin
abstract:

[PRX Quantum 7, 020101] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A high-level perspective piece proposing a five-stage framework for achieving useful quantum computing, focusing on scientific milestones rather than technical results.
motivation: To outline a roadmap bridging the gap between theoretical quantum computing and practical applications.
method: Conceptual framework based on expert opinion and analysis of current quantum computing landscape.
result: A five-stage framework detailing milestones for quantum utility.
conclusion: The framework provides a structured path but lacks novel technical contributions.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A review of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality and brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; the paper aims to provide a pedagogical overview of space-time duality as a unifying framework.
method: The review discusses discretizing time evolution on lattice systems, treating space and time on equal footing, and connecting to brickwork quantum circuits.
result: The paper presents a unified view of dynamical evolution in quantum many-body systems through the lens of space-time duality.
conclusion: Space-time duality offers a powerful analogy with quantum computation that simplifies the study of many-body dynamics.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on implementing fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems for quantum simulation.
motivation: To explore quantum many-body physics in nonstandard geometries, enabling simulation of phenomena from condensed matter topology to gravity and cosmology.
method: Reviews experimental and theoretical approaches for realizing fractal lattices, curved spaces, and synthetic dimensions in various platforms.
result: Summarizes progress in creating synthetic quantum matter in exotic geometries and discusses potential for simulating topological and gravitational effects.
conclusion: The field offers a promising avenue for quantum simulation but is not directly aligned with the user's core research directions.

title: Curvature-Induced Magnon Frequency Combs
authors: Hao Zhao, Qianjun Zheng, And Peng Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Hao Zhao, Qianjun Zheng, and Peng Yan

A tiny bump in a magnetic film exposed to microwaves can engender spin waves with precisely spaced frequencies.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256708] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.

motivation: To explore nonlinear spin-wave dynamics and generate frequency combs in magnetic systems for potential applications in signal processing and metrology.
method: Theoretical modeling and numerical simulations of spin-wave excitations in a curved magnetic film driven by microwave fields.
result: Curvature-induced magnon frequency combs are predicted, with precise frequency spacing determined by the geometry and driving conditions.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a new mechanism for generating frequency combs using magnons in curved magnetic films, expanding the toolbox for nonlinear magnonics.

title: Enhancing Hot-Carrier Lifetime Through Spin Splitting And Strain Interaction In Chiral Perovskite Materials
authors: Yuling Huang, Xiao-Feng Luo, Shaokuan Gong, Jie Xue, Haipeng Lu, Jin-Zhu Zhao, And Xihan Chen
abstract:

The dynamical control over electronic properties represents a key area of research in condensed-matter physics. Here, we demonstrate all-optical control of carrier-strain-mediated giant enhancement of spin splitting (100 meV) in a chiral 2D perovskite. Ultrafast circular dichroism measurements and a…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256902] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates all-optical control of spin splitting in chiral 2D perovskites via carrier-strain interaction, enhancing hot-carrier lifetime.
motivation: To achieve dynamical control over electronic properties in condensed-matter systems, specifically to enhance hot-carrier lifetime through spin splitting and strain interaction.

result: Giant enhancement of spin splitting (100 meV) was observed, leading to increased hot-carrier lifetime.

title: Trion Formation And Ordering In The Attractive Su(3) Fermi-Hubbard Model
authors: Jonathan Stepp, Eduardo Ibarra-García-Padilla, Richard T. Scalettar, And Kaden R. A. Hazzard
abstract:

Recent advances in microwave shielding have increased the stability and control of large numbers of polar molecules, allowing for the first realization of a molecular Bose-Einstein condensate. Remarkably, it was also recently realized that shielded polar molecules exhibit an [MATH] symmetr…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250402] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies trion formation and ordering in the attractive SU(3) Fermi-Hubbard model, a strongly correlated fermionic system.
motivation: Understanding trion phases in ultracold polar molecules with SU(3) symmetry may reveal novel quantum states.

result: They find a trion phase with charge density wave order and evidence of a trion superfluid.
conclusion: The SU(3) attractive Hubbard model supports trion formation and ordering, relevant for ultracold molecule experiments.

title: Fluid Flow And Spatiotemporal Chaos In Chemically Active Emulsions
authors: Charu Datt, Jonathan Bauermann, Nazmi Burak Budanur, And Frank Jülicher
abstract:
Author(s): Charu Datt, Jonathan Bauermann, Nazmi Burak Budanur, and Frank Jülicher

We study phase-separating fluid mixtures as they demix in the presence of chemical reactions that maintain them away from thermodynamic equilibrium. We show that in such chemically active emulsions the interplay of chemical reactions, phase separation, and hydrodynamics effects complex self-organiza…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 254001] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies fluid flow and spatiotemporal chaos in chemically active emulsions, focusing on non-equilibrium phase separation and hydrodynamics.
motivation: To understand how chemical reactions and phase separation interact with hydrodynamics to produce complex self-organization in active emulsions.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and numerical simulations of phase-separating fluid mixtures with chemical reactions, analyzing the resulting dynamics.
result: They find that the interplay of reactions, phase separation, and hydrodynamics leads to spatiotemporal chaos and complex fluid flows.
conclusion: Chemically active emulsions exhibit rich non-equilibrium behavior that could be relevant for understanding active matter and biological systems.

title: Geometric Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory
authors: Éric Cancès, Théo Duez, Jari van Gog, Asbjørn Bækgaard Lauritsen, Mathieu Lewin, And Julien Toulouse

abstract:
Author(s): Zhengzhi Wu, Zhou-Quan Wan, Shao-Kai Jian, and Hong Yao

While experimental evidence for spacetime supersymmetry (SUSY) in particle physics remains elusive, condensed matter systems offer a promising arena for its emergence at quantum critical points (QCPs). [Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256502] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a mechanism for emergent spacetime supersymmetry at a 2D fractionalized quantum critical point in a condensed matter system.
motivation: To realize spacetime supersymmetry in a condensed matter setting, which has been elusive in particle physics, by studying quantum critical points with fractionalized excitations.
method: The authors construct a lattice model with fractionalized degrees of freedom and analyze its quantum critical behavior using field-theoretic methods and renormalization group techniques.
result: They show that spacetime supersymmetry emerges at the quantum critical point, characterized by specific scaling relations and operator content.
conclusion: Fractionalized quantum criticality provides a new route to emergent supersymmetry, potentially observable in correlated electron materials.

method: Theoretical analysis of stray-field noise from emergent electrodynamics in quantum spin ice, proposing magnetometry as a detection method.
result: Stray-field magnetometry can directly detect the gapless emergent photon excitations in quantum spin ice.
conclusion: This technique offers a promising experimental route to confirm quantum spin ice and its emergent photon.

method: The authors use a technique based on the theory's symmetries and field equations to extract thermodynamic relations.
result: They derive the complete set of thermodynamic quantities for charged black holes in the given theory.
conclusion: The technique is argued to be broadly applicable to string theory and other gravitational theories.

result: They develop the complete set of techniques needed for an eEDM measurement with this apparatus, demonstrating spin interferometry in a molecular beam.
conclusion: The work establishes a platform for a future eEDM measurement with improved precision, contributing to tests of fundamental symmetries.

Usin…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 253402] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies turbulence-enhanced damping in a Bose-Einstein condensate, an effect analogous to increased viscosity in classical fluids.
motivation: To investigate whether superfluid turbulence, like classical turbulence, enhances momentum transport and damping of collective oscillations.
method: The authors create stationary spin-superflow turbulence in a BEC and measure the damping of collective oscillations.
result: They observe enhanced damping due to the presence of turbulence, analogous to increased viscosity in classical fluids.
conclusion: Superfluid turbulence can effectively increase damping, similar to classical turbulent viscosity, providing insight into quantum fluid dynamics.

motivation: The mathematical foundations of time-dependent density-functional theory (TDDFT) are not fully understood, especially for finite-dimensional systems.
method: The authors reformulate the Schrödinger equation as a constrained dynamical system on a manifold, using geometric methods to analyze existence and uniqueness of solutions.
result: They prove rigorous results on the well-posedness of the constrained dynamics and derive conditions for the validity of the TDDFT mapping.
conclusion: The work provides a solid mathematical framework for TDDFT on finite lattices, clarifying its foundations.

authors: Xiangdong Zhang, Jinbo Hu, Juhao Luo, Chaohong Lee, And Nan Zhao

motivation: Isotope shift due to alkali polarization field is a major systematic error in comagnetometer studies, limiting their accuracy.
method: The authors model the spin-exchange collisions between Xe and alkali-metal atoms and derive the effect of inhomogeneous polarization on the measured signal.
result: They quantify the isotope shift error and show its dependence on experimental parameters.
conclusion: Understanding and mitigating this error is crucial for improving the precision of NMR gyroscopes and comagnetometers.

method: The authors implement the Bogoliubov–de Gennes (BdG) formalism to solve for the ground state of a quasi-1D Fermi gas with spatially varying interaction strength or spin polarization in a box potential.
result: They identify multiple coexisting phases (e.g., superfluid, normal, polarized) in real space and characterize their structures and proximity effects.

title: Atom-chip Interferometer

result: Interference fringes are observed, demonstrating the feasibility of the chip-based interferometer.

title: Gaussian Mode Coupling Of Spectrally Broadband Photons From Bulk Spontaneous Parametric Down-conversion: A Spatial-spectral Mode Analysis Of Fiber Coupling

tldr: This paper analyzes the spatial-spectral mode coupling of broadband photons from bulk SPDC into single-mode fibers, focusing on optimizing pair-collection probability, heralding efficiency, and spectral purity.
motivation: Efficient fiber coupling of SPDC photons is crucial for quantum optics experiments and quantum technologies, but broadband photons suffer from spatial-spectral correlations that degrade performance.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model for Gaussian mode coupling of spectrally broadband photons, analyzing the spatial-spectral mode structure and its impact on fiber coupling efficiency.
result: They derive conditions for optimal fiber coupling and show trade-offs between pair-collection probability, heralding efficiency, and spectral purity.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for designing SPDC sources with improved fiber coupling, but it is primarily an engineering optimization rather than a fundamental advance in quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Unconventional Distance Scaling Of Casimir-Polder Force Between Atomic Arrays

tldr: This paper studies the Casimir-Polder force between atomic arrays and finds unconventional distance scaling due to discrete structure.
motivation: Conventional dispersion forces exhibit universal distance scaling, but the authors question whether this holds for intrinsically discrete systems like atomic arrays.
method: They use a microscopic scattering approach to compute the Casimir-Polder interaction between two atomic arrays.
result: They show that the force decays more slowly than the conventional power law, with scaling depending on array geometry and atomic spacing.
conclusion: Discreteness of the atomic arrays leads to non-universal, geometry-dependent scaling of dispersion forces, challenging conventional expectations.

method: The authors construct the light-particle Hamiltonian and apply the Born-Oppenheimer approximation to derive effective potentials and solve for bound states.
result: They obtain the Efimov spectrum for arbitrary angular momentum and analyze the scaling behavior.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical description of Efimov states in a 2+1 system, but has no direct relevance to the user's research directions.

Bose-Einstein condensates initially arranged in a long chain freely expand and interfere. Even a slight disorder in the initial ph…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063322] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the Talbot effect in a chain of Bose-Einstein condensates under phase disorder, showing that disorder destroys the effect and leads to a transition to a different interference pattern.
motivation: To understand how phase disorder affects the Talbot effect in matter-wave interferometry, which is relevant for precision measurements and quantum simulations.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the free expansion and interference of a chain of Bose-Einstein condensates with random initial phases, using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that even slight phase disorder destroys the Talbot revival, and the density distribution becomes irregular, with a characteristic length scale related to the disorder strength.
conclusion: Phase disorder fundamentally alters the Talbot effect, limiting its applicability in realistic experimental settings with phase noise.

tldr: This paper investigates the effect of the continuous spontaneous localization (CSL) model on a Bragg atom interferometer, proposing a high-contrast setup to test wave-function collapse.
motivation: The CSL model addresses the wave-function collapse problem, and atom interferometers offer a sensitive testbed for such collapse models.
method: The authors analyze the impact of CSL on a Bragg atom interferometer, calculating the decoherence effect and optimizing parameters for high contrast.
result: They find that the CSL-induced decoherence can be detected with high-contrast interferometry, setting new bounds on CSL parameters.
conclusion: The proposed Bragg atom interferometer provides a promising experimental platform to test the CSL model with improved sensitivity.

method: The authors design a gain-loss-engineered Fabry–Pérot microcavity that supports a pair of conjugate exceptional points, and use non-Hermitian topology to switch between lasing and absorption states.

conclusion: This work opens new opportunities for multifunctional photonic devices by leveraging non-Hermitian physics.

[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214325] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how isotopic substitution affects phonon modes and eigenvector transport in solids, focusing on collective mixing and transport phenomena.
motivation: Isotopic substitution is often assumed to simply rescale vibrational frequencies, but in dense phonon manifolds it can cause more complex effects like eigenvector mixing and transport.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and simulations to analyze the parametric Hermitian perturbation induced by mass changes, examining phonon eigenvectors and transport properties.
result: They find that isotopic substitution leads to collective phonon mixing and eigenvector transport, which can significantly alter vibrational dynamics beyond simple frequency shifts.
conclusion: The work highlights that isotopic effects in solids with dense phonon spectra are nontrivial and must be accounted for in understanding thermal and vibrational properties.

conclusion: Provides a unified framework for predicting magnetic properties of bilayer 2D magnets based on stacking, guiding future material design.

conclusion: Antiferromagnetic solitons in NiO show promise for logic operations due to their speed and robust propagation.

conclusion: The study reveals a complex interplay between Hund's coupling, orbital selectivity, and magnetic order, providing insights into the electronic behavior of Hund's metals.

motivation: Accurate modeling of electron-phonon interactions is crucial for understanding material properties, but existing downfolding methods are limited to short-range coupling.
method: The authors extend downfolding theory to include arbitrary-range electron-phonon coupling, starting from mean-field calculations and constructing effective Hamiltonians for the low-energy subspace.
result: They demonstrate that the method captures long-range phonon-mediated interactions and reproduces key features of the electronic structure.
conclusion: The framework provides a systematic way to incorporate electron-phonon coupling into downfolding, enabling more accurate first-principles studies of correlated materials.

title: Emergence Of Multiple Zero Modes Bound To Vortices In Extended Topological Josephson Junctions
authors: Adrian Reich, Kiryl Piasotski, Eytan Grosfeld, And Alexander Shnirman
abstract:
Author(s): Adrian Reich, Kiryl Piasotski, Eytan Grosfeld, and Alexander Shnirman

We study planar Josephson junctions formed on the surface of a three-dimensional topological insulator (Fu-Kane proposal). We examine the experimentally relevant parameter regimes in which the frequently used effective description in terms of two counter-propagating one-dimensional Majorana modes wi…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245426] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies Majorana zero modes bound to vortices in topological Josephson junctions on a topological insulator surface.
motivation: To understand the emergence of multiple zero modes in extended topological Josephson junctions beyond the simple two-mode approximation.
method: The authors analyze the effective Hamiltonian for the junction, considering spatially varying phase profiles and solving for bound states.
result: They find that multiple zero-energy Majorana modes can appear, depending on the junction geometry and phase winding.
conclusion: The results show that the low-energy physics of such junctions is richer than previously thought, with implications for topological quantum computing.

title: Controlled Pairing Symmetries In A Fermi-Hubbard Ladder With Band Flattening
authors: João P. Mendonça, S. Biswas, M. Dziurawiec, U. Bhattacharya, K. Jachymski, M. Aidelsburger, M. Lewenstein, M. M. Maśka, And T. Grass
abstract:
Author(s): João P. Mendonça, S. Biswas, M. Dziurawiec, U. Bhattacharya, K. Jachymski, M. Aidelsburger, M. Lewenstein, M. M. Maśka, and T. Grass

The competition between interactions in systems with slow electrons can drive unusual collective behavior. Here, the authors study a microscopic ladder model featuring both diagonal hopping pathways and complex loop-like electron exchange interactions. They demonstrate that while both mechanisms independently suppress ordinary metallic behavior, they stabilize completely distinct spatial patterns of electron pairing. These findings offer a theoretical framework for engineering specific superconducting states by tuning the competition between pairing mechanisms in platforms like twisted bilayer graphene or cold atoms.


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L241119] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies controlled pairing symmetries in a Fermi-Hubbard ladder with band flattening, focusing on competing pairing mechanisms and their spatial patterns.
motivation: To understand how slow electrons and competing interactions can stabilize distinct superconducting states in systems like twisted bilayer graphene or cold atoms.
method: The authors analyze a microscopic ladder model with diagonal hopping and complex loop-like exchange interactions, using theoretical and numerical methods to study the resulting pairing symmetries.
result: They find that the two mechanisms independently suppress metallic behavior but stabilize completely different spatial patterns of electron pairing.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for engineering specific superconducting states by tuning the competition between pairing mechanisms.

title: Decisive Role Of An Extra Fe Sublattice: Frustration, Criticality, And Skyrmions In The Van Der Waals Ferromagnets ${\mathrm{Fe}}_{5}{\mathrm{GeTe}}_{2}$ Versus ${\mathrm{Fe}}_{3}{\mathrm{GeTe}}_{2}$
authors: Jyoti Saini, Ankita Tiwari, Pawan Kumar Srivastava, Changgu Lee, And Subhasis Ghosh
abstract:

The van der Waals magnets [MATH] and [MATH], chemically similar yet magnetically distinct, provide an ideal platform for probing how structural complexity governs emergent magnetic order, anisotropy, and topological textures. ${\mat…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214451] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the magnetic properties of van der Waals ferromagnets Fe5GeTe2 and Fe3GeTe2, focusing on frustration, criticality, and skyrmions.
motivation: To understand how an extra Fe sublattice in Fe5GeTe2 leads to distinct magnetic behavior compared to Fe3GeTe2, including frustration and skyrmion formation.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and possibly experimental characterization to compare the magnetic structures and phase transitions of the two compounds.
result: They find that the extra Fe sublattice introduces frustration and alters the critical behavior, enabling skyrmion phases in Fe5GeTe2.
conclusion: The work highlights the role of structural complexity in controlling emergent magnetic order and topological textures in van der Waals magnets.

title: Crystal Electric Field Excitations And Spin Dynamics In The Spin-orbit Coupled Distorted Honeycomb Magnet ${\mathrm{BiErGeO}}_{5}$
authors: S. Mohanty, S. Guchhait, S. S. Islam, Surya P. Patra, M. P. Saravanan, J. A. Krieger, T. J. Hicken, H. Luetkens, D. T. Adroja, Gøran J. Nilsen, M. D. Le, And R. Nath
abstract:
Author(s): S. Mohanty, S. Guchhait, S. S. Islam, Surya P. Patra, M. P. Saravanan, J. A. Krieger, T. J. Hicken, H. Luetkens, D. T. Adroja, Gøran J. Nilsen, M. D. Le, and R. Nath

Here, the authors report the magnetic properties, crystal electric field excitations, and spin dynamics of a distorted honeycomb magnet BiErGeO
[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214452] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies crystal electric field excitations and spin dynamics in the distorted honeycomb magnet BiErGeO5, revealing unconventional magnetism without long-range order.
motivation: To understand the magnetic properties and spin dynamics in spin-orbit coupled honeycomb systems, which are relevant for quantum magnetism but not directly for quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Inelastic neutron scattering and muon spin relaxation (μSR) experiments were performed to probe crystal electric field excitations and spin dynamics.
result: A Kramers doublet ground state and anisotropic interactions were found; heat capacity shows an anomaly at ~0.4 K, but μSR rules out magnetic long-range order and indicates persistent spin fluctuations down to 30 mK.
conclusion: The system exhibits unconventional magnetism, likely a quantum spin liquid candidate, but the paper focuses on condensed matter physics without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Nematostriction In Frustrated Two-dimensional Classical Heisenberg Models
authors: Olav F. Syljuåsen And Jens Paaske
abstract:
Author(s): Olav F. Syljuåsen and Jens Paaske

We investigate the nematic phase transition in the Heisenberg [MATH] model on square and triangular lattices, accounting for finite lattice compressibility and bond-length-dependent magnetic exchange. Using Nematic Bond Theory, a diagrammatic self-consistent method, we study the ne…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224437] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nematic phase transitions in frustrated classical Heisenberg models on square and triangular lattices, focusing on magnetoelastic coupling (nematostriction).
motivation: To understand the interplay between lattice distortions and magnetic order in frustrated magnets, specifically the nematic phase transition.
method: Uses Nematic Bond Theory, a diagrammatic self-consistent method, to account for finite lattice compressibility and bond-length-dependent exchange.
result: Finds that lattice coupling can stabilize or modify the nematic phase, with quantitative predictions for lattice distortions.
conclusion: Magnetoelastic effects are important for understanding nematic order in frustrated magnets, and the method provides a framework for further studies.

title: Real-space Spectral Approach To Orbital Magnetization
authors: Kevin J. U. Vidarte, Henrique P. Veiga, João M. Viana Parente Lopes, Ramon Cardias, Aires Ferreira, Tarik P. Cysne, And Tatiana G. Rappoport
abstract:

We present a real-space spectral method for computing the orbital magnetization of crystals. Starting from the commutator form of the orbital magnetization operator, we formulate an energy-resolved spectral function that is amenable to exacting Chebyshev polynomial expansions and yields the total ma…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224438] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: A real-space spectral method using Chebyshev polynomials to compute orbital magnetization in crystals.
motivation: Orbital magnetization is a fundamental property of materials, but existing computational methods are often limited to periodic systems or require expensive Brillouin zone integration.
method: The authors derive an energy-resolved spectral function from the commutator form of the orbital magnetization operator and expand it using Chebyshev polynomials for efficient real-space computation.
result: The method accurately reproduces orbital magnetization for various crystalline systems, including topological insulators, with linear scaling in system size.
conclusion: The real-space spectral approach provides a computationally efficient and accurate alternative for calculating orbital magnetization, especially for large or disordered systems.

title: Heterometallic Spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ Quantum Magnet Under Hydrostatic Pressure
authors: M. J. Coak, D. Kamenskyi, S. P. M. Curley, B. M. Huddart, J. P. Tidey, A. Chmeruk, T. Sakurai, S. Okubo, H. Ohta, S. Kimura, H. Nojiri, D. Graf, S. J. Clark, Z. E. Manson, J. L. Manson, T. Lancaster, And P. A. Goddard
abstract:

tldr: This paper studies a heterometallic spin-1/2 quantum magnet under hydrostatic pressure, focusing on magnetic properties and phase transitions.
motivation: To understand the magnetic behavior of a material with two different spin species forming antiferromagnetic dimers and weak interdimer coupling.
method: Radio-frequency susceptibility measurements under hydrostatic pressure, combined with theoretical modeling.
result: The material exhibits pressure-dependent magnetic transitions and changes in dimer interactions.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the magnetic phase diagram of this heterometallic quantum magnet.

title: Attractive Hopfions And Bimerons In Thin Films Of Chiral Magnets: Cluster Formation And Lattice Instability In The Conical Phase
authors: Andrey O. Leonov And Takayuki Shigenaga
abstract:

We investigate the energetics, interactions, and ordering tendencies of bimerons (cholesteric fingers of the second type, CF-2) and hopfions in thin films of chiral magnets and chiral liquid crystals hosting a conical background state. Although isolated bimerons possess positive eigenenergy with res…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224441] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the energetics and ordering of hopfions and bimerons in chiral magnets, focusing on cluster formation and lattice instability in the conical phase.
motivation: Understanding the behavior of topological solitons like hopfions and bimerons in chiral magnets is important for potential applications in spintronics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use numerical simulations and analytical models to investigate the energetics, interactions, and ordering tendencies of these solitons in thin films with a conical background state.
result: They find that isolated bimerons have positive eigenenergy, but can form clusters and lattices; hopfions also exhibit interesting ordering behavior, with lattice instabilities in the conical phase.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the formation and stability of topological soliton structures in chiral magnets, but is not directly relevant to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Gap Structure And Phase Diagram Of Twisted Bilayer Cuprates From A Microscopic Perspective
authors: Siddhant Panda, Andreas Kreisel, Laura Fanfarillo, And P. J. Hirschfeld
abstract:
Author(s): Siddhant Panda, Andreas Kreisel, Laura Fanfarillo, and P. J. Hirschfeld

Twisted cuprate Josephson junctions have been proposed as candidate platforms for superconducting states that break time-reversal symmetry. However, experiments report conflicting signatures. Here, the authors show that this variability can arise from microscopic parameters: the systematic exploration of the phase diagram reveals that twist angle θ, filling, and interlayer tunneling strength stabilize distinct competing superconducting states. The results clarify how differences between devices can determine whether time-reversal symmetry breaking appears.


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224523] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the gap structure and phase diagram of twisted bilayer cuprates, focusing on time-reversal symmetry breaking in Josephson junctions.
motivation: Experiments on twisted cuprate Josephson junctions show conflicting signatures of time-reversal symmetry breaking, motivating a microscopic understanding of the phase diagram.
method: The authors systematically explore the phase diagram as a function of twist angle, filling, and interlayer tunneling strength using a microscopic model.
result: They find that distinct competing superconducting states are stabilized depending on microscopic parameters, explaining device-to-device variability.
conclusion: The variability in experimental signatures of time-reversal symmetry breaking arises from differences in microscopic parameters, clarifying the conflicting observations.

title: Spin-orbit Coupling Induced Multigap Superconductivity In $β\text{−}{\mathrm{Bi}}_{2}\mathrm{Pd}$
authors: Sonu Prasad Keshri
abstract:
Author(s): Sonu Prasad Keshri

The superconductor [MATH] is well known for its inconsistent experimental indications of single versus multiple superconducting (SC) gaps, while simultaneously being considered a promising candidate for topological superconductivity. To clarify its SC behavior, we in…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224524] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the superconducting gap structure of β-Bi2Pd, finding evidence for multigap superconductivity induced by spin-orbit coupling.
motivation: β-Bi2Pd shows inconsistent experimental indications of single vs. multiple superconducting gaps and is a candidate for topological superconductivity, motivating a theoretical clarification.
method: The authors use first-principles density functional theory (DFT) and solve the Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) equations to study the electronic structure and superconducting gaps.
result: They find that spin-orbit coupling leads to multiple superconducting gaps on different Fermi surface sheets, resolving the experimental inconsistencies.
conclusion: The multigap nature of β-Bi2Pd is confirmed, supporting its candidacy for topological superconductivity.

title: Superconductivity And The Quasiparticle Mass Enhancement Near The Charge Density Wave Critical Point Using The Bethe-Salpeter Method: Application To Cuprates
authors: Youichi Yamakawa And Hiroshi Kontani
abstract:

In recent years, charge-channel order in strongly correlated metals has attracted much attention. Representative examples include electronic nematic order in cuprates and iron-based superconductors, and Star-of-David order in kagome metals. Critical phenomena and unconventional superconductivity ari…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235140] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies superconductivity and quasiparticle mass enhancement near a charge density wave critical point in cuprates using the Bethe-Salpeter method.
motivation: To understand the interplay between charge order and superconductivity in strongly correlated metals like cuprates.
method: The authors employ the Bethe-Salpeter method to analyze the self-energy and vertex corrections near the charge density wave critical point.
result: They find that the quasiparticle mass is enhanced near the critical point, and this enhancement is linked to the superconducting pairing mechanism.
conclusion: The charge density wave fluctuations play a key role in enhancing superconductivity in cuprates.

title: Altermagnetism In An Exactly Solvable Model: Two-dimensional Ising-Kondo Lattice Model With Alternating Next-nearest-neighbor Hopping
authors: Miaomiao Zhao, Wei-Wei Yang, And Yin Zhong
abstract:

The altermagnet (AM), a recently identified class of collinear magnet, has garnered significant attention due to its unique combination of zero net magnetization and spin-split energy bands, leading to a variety of novel physical phenomena. Using numerically exact lattice Monte Carlo simulations, we…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235144] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies altermagnetism in a 2D Ising-Kondo lattice model using Monte Carlo simulations, focusing on magnetic properties and band structure.
motivation: Altermagnets are a new class of collinear magnets with zero net magnetization but spin-split bands, promising novel phenomena. The authors aim to provide an exactly solvable model to understand their properties.
method: They use numerically exact lattice Monte Carlo simulations on a two-dimensional Ising-Kondo lattice model with alternating next-nearest-neighbor hopping.
result: The model exhibits altermagnetic order with spin-split bands and zero net magnetization, and the phase diagram is characterized.
conclusion: The work provides a clean theoretical platform for studying altermagnetism, but it is primarily a condensed matter physics result without direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Valley Order In Moiré Topological Insulators
authors: Bo Zou, Anzhuoer Li, And A. H. Macdonald

[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245141] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies valley order in moiré topological insulators, focusing on interaction-induced insulators and intervalley coherence.
motivation: To understand the possibility of intervalley coherence in moiré materials with opposite Chern numbers in time-reversal-partner valleys.
method: Theoretical analysis using mean-field or similar many-body techniques to explore interaction-driven phases.
result: Identifies conditions under which intervalley coherence can occur in moiré topological insulators.
conclusion: Intervalley coherence is possible in certain moiré materials, affecting their topological properties.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Organic Mixed Conductors: Phase Transitions In A Lattice Gas
authors: Lukas M. Bongartz
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Bongartz

Organic mixed conductors (OMCs) represent a promising class of materials for applications in bioelectronics, physical computing, and thermoelectrics. Rather unparalleled, OMCs feature dynamics spanning multiple length and timescales, involving an intricate coupling between electronic, ionic, and mas…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065424] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: A statistical mechanics model for phase transitions in organic mixed conductors, focusing on ionic and electronic coupling.
motivation: Organic mixed conductors have complex dynamics across scales; understanding phase transitions is key for applications in bioelectronics and thermoelectrics.
method: A lattice gas model is developed to capture the interplay between electronic and ionic degrees of freedom, analyzed using mean-field theory and Monte Carlo simulations.
result: The model predicts first-order phase transitions and critical points driven by ion concentration and electronic coupling.
conclusion: The lattice gas framework provides a foundation for understanding thermodynamic behavior in organic mixed conductors, but the paper is primarily a materials physics study.

title: Steady-state Equilibrium And Nonequilibrium Noisy Network Dynamics
authors: Pik-Yin Lai

The fluctuating dynamics of a network about its stable, noise-free steady state are theoretically investigated. Various causes of nonequilibrium dynamics are identified in terms of the properties and symmetry of the network connections and the noise covariance matrices. Several equivalent conditions…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064148] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies steady-state fluctuations in noisy networks, focusing on equilibrium and nonequilibrium dynamics from a classical stochastic perspective.
motivation: To understand how network connectivity and noise properties drive nonequilibrium dynamics in complex systems.
method: Theoretical analysis using Langevin equations and covariance matrices to characterize fluctuations around stable steady states.
result: Identifies conditions for equilibrium and nonequilibrium dynamics based on network symmetry and noise correlations.
conclusion: The framework provides a general classification of network dynamics but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Hydrodynamic Theory Of Wetting By Active Particles
authors: Noah Grodzinski, Michael E. Cates, And Robert L. Jack

The accumulation of self-propelled particles on repulsive barriers is a widely observed feature in active matter. Despite being implicated in a broad range of biological processes, from biofilm formation to cytoskeletal movement, wetting of surfaces by active particles remains poorly understood. In …

tldr: This paper develops a hydrodynamic theory for the wetting of surfaces by active particles, focusing on the accumulation of self-propelled particles on repulsive barriers.
motivation: Wetting by active particles is poorly understood despite its relevance to biological processes like biofilm formation and cytoskeletal movement.
method: The authors derive a hydrodynamic theory based on continuum equations for active particle density and orientation, incorporating boundary conditions at the substrate.
result: The theory predicts wetting transitions and contact angles that depend on activity, and shows that active particles can wet surfaces even when passive particles would not.
conclusion: Active wetting is qualitatively different from passive wetting, with activity enabling new wetting regimes that could be exploited in biological and technological contexts.

title: Collective Coordinate Descriptions Of A Kink In A Driven-damped ${ϕ}^{4}$ Model

tldr: This paper develops effective collective coordinate models for kink dynamics in a driven-damped φ^4 model, extending previous work on sine-Gordon kinks.
motivation: To provide a reduced description of kink motion in the φ^4 model under driving and damping, capturing position, width, and internal mode dynamics.
method: Three reduced models are proposed based on collective coordinates (position, width, internal mode) and compared with full partial differential equation simulations.
result: The reduced models reproduce key features of kink dynamics, including propagation and internal mode excitation, with varying accuracy depending on the model.
conclusion: Collective coordinate approaches offer efficient and reasonably accurate descriptions of kink dynamics in driven-damped φ^4 systems.

title: Relationship Between Heider Links And Ising Spins

We show that the Heider model with an external field is equivalent, in the limit of structural balance, to the Ising model with nearest-neighbor interactions without an external field. More precisely, we claim that the signs of the Heider relations that maintain structural equilibrium in the system …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, L062104] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes an equivalence between the Heider model of social balance and the Ising model in the limit of structural balance.
motivation: To connect sociological balance theory to statistical physics, specifically showing that Heider's social relations can be mapped to Ising spins.
method: Analytical derivation showing that the Heider model with an external field reduces to the Ising model without a field under structural balance conditions.
result: The signs of Heider relations maintaining structural equilibrium correspond to Ising spin configurations with nearest-neighbor interactions.
conclusion: The equivalence provides a physical interpretation of social balance and may allow transfer of methods between the two fields.

title: Discontinuous Wealth-gradient Transition Driving Cooperation
authors: Hyun Gyu Lee, Hyeong-Chai Jeong, And Deok-Sun Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Hyun Gyu Lee, Hyeong-Chai Jeong, and Deok-Sun Lee

The universal prevalence of cooperation is puzzling, as defection typically yields higher payoffs than cooperation, motivating searches for hidden pathways to cooperation. Here we study a game-theoretic model on a lattice structured population in which interaction payoffs are scaled by the minimum o…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064306] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies cooperation in a game-theoretic model on a lattice, focusing on wealth gradients and phase transitions.
motivation: Understanding the emergence of cooperation despite the payoff advantage of defection is a classic puzzle in evolutionary game theory.
method: The authors analyze a spatial game where interaction payoffs are scaled by the minimum of players' wealth, leading to a wealth-gradient driven transition.
result: They find a discontinuous transition to cooperation as the wealth gradient increases, with critical behavior characterized by scaling laws.
conclusion: Wealth inequality can promote cooperation in structured populations, offering a new mechanism for the evolution of cooperation.

title: Propagation Of Coherent Mechanical Waves In Stealth Hyperuniform Materials In The Transparent Regime
authors: Tony Valier-Brasier
abstract:
Author(s): Tony Valier-Brasier

Wave propagation in multiply scattering media is a fundamental and long-standing topic that has undergone renewed interest with the advent of metamaterials. In particular, disorder control is an efficient way to alter wave propagation. Stealth hyperuniform (SHU) media, characterized by the cancellat…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065505] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies coherent mechanical wave propagation in stealth hyperuniform materials, focusing on the transparent regime.
motivation: Understanding wave propagation in disordered media is fundamental and relevant for metamaterial design.
method: Theoretical analysis and numerical simulations of wave propagation in stealth hyperuniform elastic media.
result: Identifies conditions for transparency and coherent wave propagation in these materials.
conclusion: Stealth hyperuniform materials can support coherent wave propagation with suppressed scattering in certain regimes.

title: Universality And Ambiguity In Extremes Of Anomalous Diffusion
authors: Sean D. Lawley
abstract:
Author(s): Sean D. Lawley

Many biophysical processes begin when the fastest searcher finds a target out of many random searchers, which is called an extreme or fastest first passage time (fFPT). In some models (i) the fFPT vanishes logarithmically as the number of searchers grows and (ii) the fFPT can be faster for subdiffus…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064135] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the scaling of fastest first-passage times in anomalous diffusion processes, focusing on universality and ambiguity in extreme statistics.
motivation: Many biophysical processes depend on the fastest searcher among many; understanding how extreme first-passage times scale with the number of searchers is important for modeling such processes.
method: The author analyzes mathematical models of subdiffusion and superdiffusion, deriving asymptotic formulas for the fastest first-passage time as the number of searchers grows large.
result: The fastest first-passage time vanishes logarithmically for some models but can be faster for subdiffusive processes, revealing ambiguity in the extreme behavior depending on the diffusion model.
conclusion: The universality of extreme first-passage time scaling is not guaranteed across different anomalous diffusion models, which has implications for biophysical search processes.

title: Phase-space Topology And Spectral Flow In Screened Magnetized Plasmas
authors: Xianhao Rao, Adil Yolbarsop, Hong Li, And Wandong Liu
abstract:

Topological wave phenomena in continuous media are fundamentally challenged by unbounded spectra and the absence of a compact Brillouin zone, which obstruct conventional bulk-interface formulations. We develop a unified phase-space framework for screened magnetized plasma based on a pseudo-Hermitian…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023334] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a phase-space topological framework for screened magnetized plasmas, focusing on spectral flow and bulk-interface correspondence in continuous media.
motivation: Topological wave phenomena in continuous media are challenged by unbounded spectra and lack of a compact Brillouin zone, motivating a unified phase-space approach.
method: The authors construct a pseudo-Hermitian formalism in phase space to analyze topological invariants and spectral flow in screened magnetized plasmas.
result: They demonstrate bulk-interface correspondence and topological transitions in the plasma system, revealing spectral flow phenomena.
conclusion: The phase-space framework successfully extends topological concepts to continuous media with unbounded spectra, offering new insights into plasma wave dynamics.

title: Excited Eigenstates From A Two-species Random Walk
authors: Paul-Henry Glinel, Normand Beaudoin, And Alexandre Melanson

Macroscopically, the population density function of random walk models can satisfy self-contained dynamics and exhibit unexpected order. Here, we show how a two-species random walk model that includes diffusion, probabilistic absorption of walkers mediated by a potential function, cross-species anni…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023324] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: A two-species random walk model with diffusion, absorption, and cross-species annihilation is studied, showing emergent order in population densities.
motivation: To understand how macroscopic order can arise from simple stochastic microscopic rules in multi-species systems.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of a two-species random walk model with diffusion, potential-mediated absorption, and cross-species annihilation.
result: The population density functions exhibit self-contained dynamics and unexpected order, such as pattern formation or steady-state structures.
conclusion: The model demonstrates that complex macroscopic behavior can emerge from simple random walk interactions, relevant to statistical physics but not directly to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Theory Of High-harmonic Generation With Quantum Light
authors: Haoyu Liu, Hanxu Zhang, Xu Wang, And Jianmin Yuan

method: The authors develop a theoretical framework combining quantum optics and strong-field physics to describe HHG with bright squeezed vacuum light.
result: They elucidate the mechanism and predict observable signatures of quantum light in HHG spectra.
conclusion: The work opens up new possibilities for controlling HHG with quantum light and for probing quantum properties of light via strong-field processes.
