Ultracold Feshbach molecules are a crucial intermediate step for the creation of quantum degenerate gases of strongly dipolar molecules. After coherent transfer to the rovibrational ground state, these dimers can realize stable dipolar gases with strong, tunable long-range interactions. Here, we rep…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023307] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the formation of ultracold 23Na41K Feshbach molecules, a step toward creating quantum degenerate dipolar gases.
motivation: Ultracold Feshbach molecules are essential intermediates for producing strongly dipolar quantum gases with tunable long-range interactions.
method: The authors use magnetoassociation across a Feshbach resonance in a mixture of 23Na and 41K atoms to form weakly bound molecules.
result: They successfully create Feshbach molecules and characterize their properties, including the magnetic field dependence of the binding energy.
conclusion: This work provides a pathway to produce ultracold dipolar NaK molecules for studying strongly interacting quantum gases.

title: Observation Of Surface Ferromagnons In The Axion-insulating Phase Of The Antiferromagnetic Topological Insulator ${\mathrm{EuSn}}_{2}{\mathrm{As}}_{2}$
authors: Mamoun Hemmida, Santanu Pakhira, David C. Johnston, And Hans-Albrecht Krug von Nidda
abstract:
Author(s): Mamoun Hemmida, Santanu Pakhira, David C. Johnston, and Hans-Albrecht Krug von Nidda

We report the study of spin dynamics of [MATH] in the antiferromagnetic axion topological insulator [MATH] by means of antiferromagnetic resonance at 9.34 GHz. Below the Néel temperature ([MATH]), two types of resonance modes, the conventiona…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023309] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports antiferromagnetic resonance measurements in the topological insulator EuSn2As2, observing surface ferromagnons in the axion-insulating phase.
motivation: To study spin dynamics and surface magnetic excitations in a topological insulator with antiferromagnetic order, relevant to axion electrodynamics.
method: Electron spin resonance (ESR) at 9.34 GHz was used to measure antiferromagnetic resonance modes below the Néel temperature.
result: Two resonance modes were observed: conventional antiferromagnetic resonance and a surface ferromagnon mode, indicating surface ferromagnetism.
conclusion: The surface ferromagnon mode is a signature of the axion-insulating phase, providing insight into the interplay between magnetism and topology.

title: Simulating Dynamics Of The Two-dimensional Transverse-field Ising Model: A Comparative Study Of Large-scale Classical Numerics
authors: Joseph Vovrosh, Sergi Julià-Farré, Wladislaw Krinitsin, Michael Kaicher, Fergus Hayes, Emmanuel Gottlob, Augustine Kshetrimayum, Kemal Bidzhiev, Simon B. Jäger, Markus Schmitt, Joseph Tindall, Constantin Dalyac, Tiago Mendes-Santos, And Alexandre Dauphin
abstract:
Author(s): Joseph Vovrosh, Sergi Julià-Farré, Wladislaw Krinitsin, Michael Kaicher, Fergus Hayes, Emmanuel Gottlob, Augustine Kshetrimayum, Kemal Bidzhiev, Simon B. Jäger, Markus Schmitt, Joseph Tindall, Constantin Dalyac, Tiago Mendes-Santos, and Alexandre Dauphin

The quantum dynamics of many-qubit systems is an outstanding problem that has recently driven significant advances in both numerical methods and programmable quantum processing units (QPUs). In this work, we employ a comprehensive toolbox of state-of-the-art numerical approaches to classically simul…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023311] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: A comparative study of classical numerical methods for simulating the dynamics of the 2D transverse-field Ising model.
motivation: Quantum dynamics of many-qubit systems is computationally hard; this work benchmarks various classical numerical techniques to assess their accuracy and scalability.
method: The authors apply a suite of state-of-the-art numerical methods (e.g., tensor networks, neural quantum states, exact diagonalization) to simulate the 2D transverse-field Ising model and compare their performance.
result: The study provides a comprehensive comparison of the methods' accuracy and computational cost for different system sizes and parameters.
conclusion: No single method outperforms all others; the choice depends on the specific regime and desired accuracy, highlighting the need for continued development of classical simulation techniques.

title: Confinement And Finite-range Effects In A Quasi-two-dimensional Gas Of Fermionic Dimers
authors: Giovanni Midei, Jordi Boronat, And Grigory E. Astrakharchik
abstract:
Author(s): Giovanni Midei, Jordi Boronat, and Grigory E. Astrakharchik

A study of a gas of fermionic dimers in a quasi-two-dimensional geometry induced by strong harmonic confinement in one direction is presented. Fixed-node diffusion Monte Carlo calculations are used to quantify the effects of confinement and finite interaction range on the equation of state and density profiles, with the results benchmarked against analytical theories.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022051] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: A Monte Carlo study of fermionic dimers in a quasi-2D geometry, focusing on confinement and finite-range effects on the equation of state.
motivation: To understand how strong confinement and finite interaction range affect the properties of a gas of fermionic dimers, which is relevant to ultracold atomic physics.
method: Fixed-node diffusion Monte Carlo simulations are used to compute the equation of state and density profiles, benchmarked against analytical theories.
result: Quantifies the effects of confinement and finite range on the equation of state and density profiles.
conclusion: The study provides benchmarks for analytical theories and insights into quasi-2D fermionic dimer gases.

title: Macroscopic Localization And Collective Memory In Poisson Renewal Resetting
authors: Ohad Vilk
abstract:
Author(s): Ohad Vilk

Stochastic renewal processes are ubiquitous across physics, biology, and the social sciences. Here, we show that continuous-time renewal dynamics can naturally produce a mixed discrete-continuous structure, with a macroscopic fraction of particles occupying a discrete state. For ensembles of continu…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023305] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies macroscopic localization and collective memory in Poisson renewal resetting processes.
motivation: To understand how renewal dynamics can produce a mixed discrete-continuous structure with macroscopic occupation of a discrete state.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of continuous-time renewal processes with resetting.
result: A macroscopic fraction of particles can occupy a discrete state, leading to collective memory effects.
conclusion: Renewal resetting can induce macroscopic localization and memory, relevant to stochastic processes in various fields.

title: Manifold-based Transformation Of Probability Distributions: Application To The Inverse Problem Of Reconstructing Distributions From Experimental Data
authors: Tomotaka Oroguchi, Rintaro Inoue, And Masaaki Sugiyama
abstract:
Author(s): Tomotaka Oroguchi, Rintaro Inoue, and Masaaki Sugiyama

Information geometry is a mathematical framework that elucidates the manifold structure of the probability distribution space (p space), providing a systematic approach to transforming probability distributions (PDs). In this study, we utilized information geometry to address the inverse problems as…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023291] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses information geometry to transform probability distributions for solving inverse problems in experimental data reconstruction.
motivation: Reconstructing probability distributions from experimental data is a common inverse problem; the authors aim to provide a systematic method using manifold-based transformations.
method: They apply information geometry to define a manifold structure on the space of probability distributions and develop transformations that map between distributions.
result: The proposed method enables efficient reconstruction of distributions from limited or noisy experimental data.
conclusion: Information geometry offers a powerful framework for inverse problems involving probability distributions, with potential applications in various experimental fields.

title: Dynamical Phase Transitions Across Slow And Fast Regimes In A Two-tone Driven Duffing Resonator
authors: Soumya S. Kumar, Javier Del Pino, Letizia Catalini, Alexander Eichler, And Oded Zilberberg
abstract:
Author(s): Soumya S. Kumar, Javier del Pino, Letizia Catalini, Alexander Eichler, and Oded Zilberberg

The dynamical phase transitions of a Duffing resonator subjected to a bichromatic drive across the slow- and fast-beating regimes are mapped. An analytical threshold to observe these transitions based on an effective nonlinear response theory is provided, explaining the mechanism behind these processes. Complementary analytical treatments for the slow and fast regimes are supplied.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023298] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dynamical phase transitions in a driven Duffing resonator, focusing on classical nonlinear dynamics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand the transition between slow and fast beating regimes in a nonlinear resonator under bichromatic drive.
method: Analytical effective nonlinear response theory combined with complementary treatments for slow and fast regimes.
result: An analytical threshold for dynamical phase transitions is derived and mapped across the two regimes.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for predicting and explaining dynamical phase transitions in driven nonlinear resonators.

title: Complete Inelastic Transparency Of Time-modulated Resonant Photonic Circuits
authors: M. Sumetsky
abstract:
Author(s): M. Sumetsky

Photonic circuits modulated in time can convert the input light frequency [MATH], shifting it by multiples of the modulation frequency [MATH] and, in certain cases, amplify the total input light power. Of special interest are photonic circuits employing microwave capacitors, which instantaneou…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023299] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies inelastic transparency in time-modulated resonant photonic circuits, focusing on frequency conversion and power amplification.
motivation: To understand and exploit the effects of time modulation on light propagation in photonic circuits, particularly for frequency conversion and amplification.
method: Theoretical analysis using coupled-mode theory and transfer matrix methods for time-modulated resonant structures.
result: Demonstrates that under certain conditions, time-modulated photonic circuits can achieve complete inelastic transparency, converting input light to different frequencies with no reflection.
conclusion: Time-modulated resonant photonic circuits offer a new mechanism for frequency conversion and amplification, with potential applications in photonic signal processing.

title: Dynamics Of Quantum Chiral Solitons
authors: Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, And Cristian D. Batista
abstract:
Author(s): Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, and Cristian D. Batista

A nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains demonstrates that they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid, appearing as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase and becoming detectable via inelastic neutron scattering.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021056] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains, showing they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and are detectable via neutron scattering.
motivation: To understand the quantum dynamics of chiral solitons in spin chains, which are topological excitations with potential relevance to low-dimensional magnetism.
method: A nonperturbative quantization approach is applied to chiral solitons in a spin chain model, analyzing their condensation into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid.
result: Chiral solitons appear as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase and their signature can be observed via inelastic neutron scattering.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for chiral soliton dynamics and suggests experimental detection is feasible.

title: Free And Interacting Fermionic Conformal Field Theories On The Fuzzy Sphere
authors: Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, And Yin-Chen He
abstract:
Author(s): Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, and Yin-Chen He

Researchers use noncommutative “fuzzy” spheres to study three-dimensional fermionic conformal field theories, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021055] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses fuzzy sphere regularization to study free and interacting fermionic conformal field theories in three dimensions, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.
motivation: To develop a non-perturbative method for studying strongly coupled conformal field theories using the fuzzy sphere, a noncommutative geometry approach.
method: The authors employ the fuzzy sphere regularization, which replaces the continuous sphere with a finite-dimensional matrix algebra, to simulate fermionic CFTs numerically.
result: They demonstrate that the fuzzy sphere can accurately capture the critical properties of free and interacting fermionic CFTs, and observe emergent supersymmetry in certain interacting models.
conclusion: The fuzzy sphere is a powerful tool for studying fermionic CFTs, and the emergent supersymmetry suggests deeper connections between noncommutative geometry and quantum field theory.

title: General Approach To Solving Spin Moiré Superstructures
authors: Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. Debeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, And Joseph G. Checkelsky
abstract:
Author(s): Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. DeBeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, and Joseph G. Checkelsky

Mapping of spin textures in EuAg
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021054] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a general approach to solving spin moiré superstructures, focusing on magnetic phases in EuAg4Sb2.
motivation: To understand and control spin textures in moiré superlattices for potential information manipulation.
method: Neutron scattering and theoretical modeling are used to map spin textures and identify magnetic phases.
result: Three distinct, tunable magnetic phases are revealed in EuAg4Sb2, establishing a design framework.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for engineering spin-based vortex lattices, but is primarily a condensed matter physics study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Fate Of Topological Dirac Magnons In Van Der Waals Ferromagnets At Finite Temperature
authors: Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, And Alexander Mook
abstract:
Author(s): Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, and Alexander Mook

Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures demonstrates that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point, providing a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021053] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies topological magnon gaps in van der Waals ferromagnets at finite temperature, finding stability near the Curie point.
motivation: To understand the robustness of topological magnon gaps under thermal fluctuations for spintronic applications.
method: Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures.
result: Topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point.
conclusion: Provides a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices.

title: Are Neural Networks Collision Resistant?
authors: Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, And Riccardo Zecchina
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, and Riccardo Zecchina

A study of the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network shows that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions, a result of direct relevance for the definition of new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021051] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the computational complexity of finding collisions in a one-layer neural network, linking to cryptographic protocol design.
motivation: To understand whether neural networks can serve as collision-resistant hash functions for cryptography.
method: The authors analyze the computational complexity of collision-finding in a simple one-layer neural network using theoretical and algorithmic approaches.
result: Efficient algorithms fail to find collisions, suggesting that such neural networks may be collision-resistant.
conclusion: The findings are relevant for defining new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.

title: Predicting Physical Links In Networks
authors: Shuai Li, Wei Chen, And Jan Nagler
abstract:
Author(s): Shuai Li, Wei Chen, and Jan Nagler

A physics-informed framework allows for inferring general causal links across a wide range of networked dynamics systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021048] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A physics-informed framework for inferring causal links in networked dynamical systems.
motivation: Understanding causal relationships in complex networks is crucial but challenging; the authors aim to leverage physical principles to improve link prediction.
method: The framework integrates domain knowledge from physics (e.g., conservation laws, symmetries) with network data to infer causal links.
result: The method demonstrates improved accuracy in predicting physical links across various networked dynamical systems.
conclusion: Physics-informed approaches can enhance causal inference in networks, with potential applications in diverse fields.

title: General Framework Enabling Polarity-Tunable Time-Reversal Symmetric Superconducting Diode Effects In Gate-Defined Homojunctions
authors: Hongwei Zhang, Chunsheng Wang, Ran Wang, Senyang Pan, Hengning Wang, Jiaqiang Cai, Yonglai Liu, Zhe Qu, Xiangde Zhu, Wei Ning, Chuanying Xi, Jinglei Zhang, Ning Hao, Guolin Zheng, And Mingliang Tian
abstract:
Author(s): Hongwei Zhang, Chunsheng Wang, Ran Wang, Senyang Pan, Hengning Wang, Jiaqiang Cai, Yonglai Liu, Zhe Qu, Xiangde Zhu, Wei Ning, Chuanying Xi, Jinglei Zhang, Ning Hao, Guolin Zheng, and Mingliang Tian

Local protonic gating in
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021046] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a time-reversal symmetric superconducting diode effect in gate-defined homojunctions using local protonic gating.
motivation: To achieve magnetic-field-free control of nonreciprocal critical currents in superconducting diodes, which is important for low-dissipation electronics.
method: The authors use local protonic gating in homojunctions to induce a superconducting diode effect without breaking time-reversal symmetry.
result: They observe a polarity-tunable superconducting diode effect, enabling control of nonreciprocal critical currents without an external magnetic field.
conclusion: This work provides a general framework for realizing superconducting diodes in gate-defined homojunctions, with potential applications in superconducting electronics.

title: Anyon Superfluidity Of Excitons In Quantum Hall Bilayers
authors: Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, And Ashvin Vishwanath
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, and Ashvin Vishwanath

Theoretical analysis of quantum Hall bilayers reveals that topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids, offering a robust mechanism for engineering exotic collective quantum states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021044] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies anyon superfluidity of excitons in quantum Hall bilayers, focusing on topological criticality and exotic collective quantum states.
motivation: To understand and engineer exotic collective quantum states in quantum Hall bilayers through topological criticality.
method: Theoretical analysis using topological field theory and mean-field approaches.
result: Topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids.
conclusion: The findings provide a robust mechanism for engineering exotic collective quantum states in quantum Hall systems.

title: Probing Quantum Anomalous Hall States In Twisted Bilayer ${\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$ Via Attractive Polaron Spectroscopy
authors: Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, And Mohammad Hafezi
abstract:
Author(s): Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, and Mohammad Hafezi

Magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted WSe
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021037] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses magneto-optical spectroscopy to probe quantum anomalous Hall states in twisted bilayer WSe2, demonstrating electric-field control of magnetic order.
motivation: To investigate the quantum anomalous Hall phase in twisted bilayer WSe2 and understand the interplay between topology and magnetism in moiré materials.
method: Attractive polaron spectroscopy is employed to probe the electronic structure and magnetic ordering under applied electric and magnetic fields.
result: A spontaneous quantum anomalous Hall phase is observed, and electric-field control over transitions between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic orders is demonstrated.
conclusion: The findings establish twisted bilayer WSe2 as a platform for studying topological phases with tunable magnetism, relevant for future quantum devices.

title: Liquid-Gas Criticality Of Hyperuniform Fluids
authors: Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, And Qun-Li Lei
abstract:
Author(s): Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, and Qun-Li Lei

Where ordinary fluids show wild fluctuations and critical opalescence, hyperuniform fluids of spinning particles stay unusually calm yet highly susceptible at the liquid–vapor critical point.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021032] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the liquid-gas criticality of hyperuniform fluids, focusing on density fluctuations and critical opalescence suppression.
motivation: To understand the unusual critical behavior of hyperuniform fluids, which exhibit suppressed density fluctuations yet high susceptibility at the liquid-vapor critical point.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and possibly simulations to characterize the critical properties of hyperuniform fluids composed of spinning particles.
result: Hyperuniform fluids show suppressed critical opalescence but enhanced susceptibility, indicating a new type of critical behavior.
conclusion: The findings reveal a distinct class of critical phenomena in hyperuniform fluids, with implications for understanding fluctuations in correlated systems.

title: Stealthy-Hyperuniform Wave Dynamics In Two-Dimensional Photonic Crystals
authors: Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, And Mikael C. Rechtsman
abstract:
Author(s): Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, and Mikael C. Rechtsman

While disordered stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be largely transparent within a particular range of wavelengths, new experiments on large-scale silicon photonic crystals reveal unexpected residual scattering driven by radiative loss.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021028] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies wave dynamics in disordered stealthy hyperuniform photonic crystals, revealing unexpected residual scattering due to radiative loss.
motivation: Stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be transparent in certain wavelength ranges, but experiments show residual scattering that needs explanation.
method: Large-scale experiments on silicon photonic crystals combined with theoretical analysis of radiative loss mechanisms.
result: Unexpected residual scattering is driven by radiative loss, contradicting the expectation of near-perfect transparency.
conclusion: The findings highlight limitations of stealthy hyperuniform designs for photonic applications and suggest new design rules.

title: Ballistic Spin Valve In Graphene Realized Via Electron Optics
authors: Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, And Ivan J. Vera-Marun
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, and Ivan J. Vera-Marun

Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene reveals gate-tunable ballistic spin transport, providing a mechanism for coherent spin control through spin-dependent electron optics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021029] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a ballistic spin valve in graphene using electron optics for coherent spin control.
motivation: To achieve coherent spin control in graphene via gate-tunable ballistic spin transport.
method: Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene reveals gate-tunable ballistic spin transport.
result: Demonstration of a ballistic spin valve with coherent spin control through spin-dependent electron optics.
conclusion: The work provides a mechanism for coherent spin control in graphene, relevant for spintronics.

title: Provable Quantum Speedups For Computing Persistence In Topological Data Analysis
authors: Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, And Ryu Hayakawa
abstract:
Author(s): Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, and Ryu Hayakawa

A quantum algorithm achieving exponential speedup for a topological data analysis problem is proposed, potentially driving new practical applications in quantum computing.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020361] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum algorithm for computing persistence in topological data analysis, claiming exponential speedup.
motivation: Topological data analysis is a powerful tool for extracting features from data, but classical algorithms are computationally expensive. Quantum computing may offer speedups.
method: The authors design a quantum algorithm that leverages quantum linear algebra and sampling techniques to compute persistence diagrams.
result: They prove a provable exponential quantum speedup over classical algorithms for certain instances of the problem.
conclusion: The work suggests that quantum computers could enable practical topological data analysis for large datasets, though practical implementation remains challenging.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithms For The Jones Polynomial
authors: Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew Decross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, And Konstantinos Meichanetzidis
abstract:
Author(s): Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew DeCross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, and Konstantinos Meichanetzidis

A comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial is shown to serve as a benchmark for quantum computers and yield new insights into potential quantum advantage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020355] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a complete quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial, demonstrating its use as a benchmark for quantum computers.
motivation: The Jones polynomial is a topological invariant that is hard to compute classically, making it a candidate for quantum advantage. The authors aim to provide an end-to-end implementation on current quantum hardware.
method: The pipeline includes state preparation, unitary evolution, and measurement, implemented on a trapped-ion quantum processor. They use a variational approach to optimize the circuit for the specific polynomial evaluation.
result: They successfully compute the Jones polynomial for several knots and links, showing agreement with classical calculations and demonstrating scalability.
conclusion: The work establishes a practical benchmark for quantum computers and suggests that the Jones polynomial may be a viable candidate for early quantum advantage.

title: Photon Catalysis For General Multimode Multi-Photon Quantum State Preparation
authors: Andrei Aralov, Émilie Gillet, Viet Nguyen, Andrea Cosentino, Mattia Walschaers, And Massimo Frigerio
abstract:
Author(s): Andrei Aralov, Émilie Gillet, Viet Nguyen, Andrea Cosentino, Mattia Walschaers, and Massimo Frigerio

Using a procedure based on symmetric tensor decomposition, every photonic state can be prepared with realistic experimental tools and a predictable number of steps.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020323] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: A method for preparing arbitrary multimode multi-photon quantum states using symmetric tensor decomposition and photon catalysis.
motivation: Efficient preparation of complex photonic states is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are often limited to specific state families.
method: The authors propose a procedure based on symmetric tensor decomposition to decompose any photonic state into a sequence of photon catalysis operations, which are experimentally realizable with linear optics and photon-number-resolving detectors.
result: They show that any N-photon, M-mode state can be prepared with a predictable number of steps scaling polynomially in N and M.
conclusion: The work provides a universal and efficient scheme for photonic state preparation, advancing experimental capabilities in quantum optics.

title: Quantum Linear System Solvers: A Survey Of Algorithms And Applications
authors: Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, And Dominic W. Berry
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, and Dominic W. Berry

Given vector b and matrix
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025005] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive survey of quantum algorithms for solving linear systems, focusing on HHL and post-HHL developments.
motivation: Solving linear systems is a central task in computation, and quantum algorithms promise exponential speedups for certain problems.
method: The paper reviews algorithmic techniques including HHL, block-encoding, quantum signal processing, and variable-time amplitude amplification.
result: It catalogs the evolution of quantum linear system solvers, highlighting improvements in query complexity, condition number dependence, and practical considerations.
conclusion: Quantum linear system solvers have advanced significantly, but practical implementation remains challenging due to resource requirements and noise.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge in 2D magnetism, which has seen rapid progress since 2016.
method: Review of experimental and theoretical results on 2D magnetic materials, including topology, dynamics, and light-matter interactions.
result: The field encompasses ferromagnets, antiferromagnets, topological phases, nonequilibrium dynamics, and potential applications.
conclusion: 2D van der Waals magnets offer a rich platform for fundamental physics and future technologies.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on exotic electronic states arising from geometric frustration and interference effects.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual phenomena in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and topological flat bands.
method: The paper reviews theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, synthesizing findings from condensed matter physics.
result: Kagome metals exhibit a wealth of exotic states including unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism, and electronic nematicity.
conclusion: The kagome lattice provides a rich platform for exploring correlated electron physics and topological phenomena.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: A review of spin-glass dynamics covering experiment, theory, and simulation, with broad applications to physical systems.
motivation: Spin glasses serve as a model system for complex disordered systems, and understanding their dynamics is relevant to many areas of physics.
method: The paper reviews experimental techniques, theoretical models, and large-scale numerical simulations of spin-glass dynamics.
result: The review highlights the synergy between experiment, theory, and simulation, and identifies future research opportunities.
conclusion: Spin-glass dynamics remain a rich field with ongoing challenges and cross-disciplinary impact.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on material candidates and topological properties.
motivation: To provide an overview of theoretical and experimental progress in Kitaev spin liquids, which are a type of quantum spin liquid with potential applications in topological quantum computing.
method: Review of theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental candidate materials, summarizing key properties and challenges.
result: Highlights leading candidate materials and their topological properties such as chiral edge modes.
conclusion: The review serves as a resource for researchers working on quantum spin liquids, but does not present new results or directly advance quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to neural network data, but does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Understanding coordinated activity in large neural networks is a key goal in neuroscience, and statistical physics offers tools to model such systems.
method: The review surveys maximum entropy models and renormalization group techniques applied to recordings from thousands of neurons.
result: These methods uncover reproducible collective behaviors in neural populations, bridging theory and experiment.
conclusion: Statistical physics principles can provide predictive power for neural network dynamics, similar to their role in other areas of physics.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review of quantum aspects of magnetic skyrmions, covering their formation and quantum features.
motivation: To survey quantum-mechanical properties of magnetic skyrmions, which are topological spin textures with potential applications in spintronics.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on skyrmion formation, quantum interactions, and quantum features.
result: Summarizes current understanding of quantum effects in skyrmions, including quantum tunneling and entanglement.
conclusion: Quantum properties of skyrmions are an emerging area with potential for future quantum technologies, but the field is still developing.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: A review of using massive quantum systems to probe gravity, including tests of quantum gravity effects and entanglement mediation.
motivation: To understand the interplay between quantum mechanics and gravity, which is poorly understood, by using massive quantum systems as probes.
method: Review of theoretical proposals and experimental efforts, including matter-wave interferometry, optomechanics, and tests of gravity-induced entanglement.
result: Summarizes current theoretical models and experimental progress, highlighting that no definitive evidence of quantum gravity has been found yet.
conclusion: Massive quantum systems offer a promising avenue to test quantum gravity, but further theoretical and experimental work is needed.

motivation: To establish a new multiferroic mechanism that couples antiferroaxial order with altermagnetism, expanding the understanding of ferroic orders.
method: The authors use symmetry analysis and first-principles calculations to demonstrate the prevalence of antiferroaxial altermagnetism in various materials.
result: They show that antiferroaxial counterrotating distortions induce altermagnetic spin splitting, leading to a multiferroic state.
conclusion: Antiferroaxial altermagnetism is a generic and microscopically grounded multiferroic mechanism with potential for spintronic applications.

result: Discovery of novel critical phenomena for a wide range of scalar-electromagnetic couplings, with no smooth interior solutions.
conclusion: Scalarized black holes exhibit critical behavior that may have implications for black hole physics and scalarization mechanisms.

conclusion: The study provides insights into the microscopic origin of angular momenta and entanglement in fission, but the context is nuclear physics, not quantum information science.

motivation: To explore the interplay between Kondo physics and magnetic order in a kagome lattice with flat bands, which may host exotic quantum states.
method: Single-crystal synthesis, transport, magnetization, specific heat, ARPES, and DFT calculations.

conclusion: CsCr6Sb6 is a platform to study Kondo physics in a flat-band system, revealing competition between Kondo screening and magnetic ordering.

result: They show that the electronic angular momentum vector can be oriented arbitrarily in 3D, enabling control of optomagnetic responses.
conclusion: This work opens new possibilities for ultrafast optomagnetic devices and coherent control of molecular currents.

motivation: To understand why the hyperfine interaction does not cause collapse in hydrogen-like atoms despite scaling faster than kinetic energy at small sizes.
method: The authors analyze the Dirac equation for two fermions and study the behavior of the hyperfine interaction as the wavefunction is compressed.
result: They show that the hyperfine attraction saturates due to relativistic effects, preventing collapse and resolving the puzzle.

title: Auxiliary Field Quantum Monte Carlo At The Basis Set Limit: Application To Lattice Constants
authors: Moritz Humer, Martin Schlipf, Zoran Sukurma, Sajad Bazrafshan, And Georg Kresse

authors: Yoshiki Hiruta, Kento Yasuda, And Kenta Ishimoto

authors: Shunsuke Kitou, Akitoshi Nakano, Masato Imaizumi, Yuiga Nakamura, Yuto Nakamura, Hideo Kishida, Taka-Hisa Arima, And Ichiro Terasaki

tldr: This paper proposes a ghost mechanism to explain abrupt learning in recurrent neural networks, identifying transient dynamical bottlenecks that cause training instabilities.
motivation: Understanding abrupt learning phenomena in neural networks can improve training stability and efficiency.
method: The authors develop an analytical model of recurrent networks, identifying ghost points as transient bottlenecks and analyzing their dynamics.
result: The ghost mechanism provides a theoretical explanation for abrupt learning and suggests ways to overcome training instabilities.
conclusion: The ghost mechanism is a key underlying process for abrupt learning in recurrent networks, with implications for improving training.

authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, focusing on nonradiative transitions and their applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
motivation: Internal conversion is a key photophysical process affecting the efficiency of light-emitting devices and solar energy conversion, yet its theoretical description remains challenging.
method: The review surveys various theoretical models, including nonadiabatic dynamics, Fermi's golden rule, and mixed quantum-classical approaches, to describe internal conversion.
result: The paper summarizes the strengths and limitations of current methods and identifies open questions in the field.
conclusion: Improved theoretical methods for internal conversion are needed to advance applications in photonics and energy harvesting.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the Standard Model, including their potential connection to dark matter and dark energy.

method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for spin-dependent interactions and surveys experimental techniques used to search for them, such as precision measurements and symmetry tests.
result: The review summarizes the current status of experimental constraints on various spin-dependent exotic interactions and outlines future directions.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions remain an active area of research with potential implications for fundamental physics, but no definitive evidence has been found yet.

title: Self-aligning Polar Active Matter
authors: Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, And Amir Shee
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, and Amir Shee

What if active units could align–or even antialign–their orientation with their own velocity? This intriguing self-alignment property unlocks a spectrum of fascinating behaviors, from single self-propelled particles orbiting in harmonic traps to transformative collective phenomena like synchronized motion in dense or solid elastic assemblies. Unlike systems where units simply mimic their neighbors, self-alignment fundamentally reshapes how motion emerges, paving the way for groundbreaking discoveries in biology, smart materials, and robotics. This review uncovers the hidden power of self-alignment in active systems, introduces a unified mathematical and conceptual framework, explores existing models of self-alignment, and highlights its transformative impact on the study and real-world applications of active systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015007] Published Thu Mar 20, 2025.
tldr: A review of self-alignment in active matter systems, focusing on how units align their orientation with their velocity, leading to novel collective behaviors.
motivation: To understand and unify the phenomenon of self-alignment in active matter, which is distinct from neighbor-based alignment and has implications for biology, smart materials, and robotics.
method: The paper reviews existing models and experiments on self-alignment, presenting a unified mathematical and conceptual framework.
result: Self-alignment enables behaviors such as orbiting in harmonic traps and synchronized motion in dense assemblies, fundamentally reshaping emergent motion.
conclusion: Self-alignment is a powerful mechanism in active matter that opens new avenues for research and applications.

result: At strong coupling, the spectrum organizes into flat-space string mass levels with universal square-root scaling.
conclusion: The work provides a non-perturbative check of the AdS/CFT correspondence and the quantum spectral curve approach.

method: The authors analyze the modified loop quantum cosmology (mLQC-I) model for Bianchi I spacetime, solving the effective equations of motion and studying the behavior of shear near the bounce.
result: They find that shear is dynamically suppressed after the bounce and decays rapidly in the quantum postbounce regime, independent of the equation of state.
conclusion: Loop quantum cosmology predicts a robust isotropization mechanism, which may have implications for early universe cosmology and the initial conditions for inflation.

conclusion: The findings highlight the importance of implementation details in CPM and reveal a new phase that may be relevant to biological tissue behavior.

authors: João N. C. Especial And Patrícia F. N. Faísca

For decades, significant effort has been devoted to elucidating the functional role of knots in proteins, yet no consensus has been reached. Here, using extensive Monte Carlo off-lattice simulations of a simple struc…

title: Characterizing Emergent Multiscale Dynamics In Colloidal Nanoparticle Gels
authors: William D. Brackett, Zachary M. Sherman, Felix Lehmkühler, Thomas M. Truskett, And Delia J. Milliron
abstract:

This Perspective describes the opportunities to address this challenge using X-ray photon correlation spectroscopy at fourth-generation light sources combined with complementary experimental and simulation tools. Temporal and/or spatial averaging over these fluctuations may give the impression of both a wrong periodicit…

tldr: This paper studies oxygen adsorption on Rh(100) surface, revealing that fluctuating ordered domains can mimic a wrong surface symmetry under thermal averaging.
motivation: To understand the behavior of adsorbate phases beyond their stability temperature and to correct misinterpretations of surface symmetry from diffraction data.

title: Fundamentals Of Vacuum Breakdown In High-gradient Accelerator Structures
authors: Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, And Yinon Ashkenazy
abstract:
Author(s): Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, and Yinon Ashkenazy

Vacuum breakdown or arcing happens when a very strong electric field causes a metal surface in a vacuum to suddenly form plasma, allowing large electrical currents to flow. Breakdown can damage particle accelerators, fusion reactors, satellites, and x-ray devices, though it is useful in technologies like plasma thrusters. Scientists have studied this unpredictable and fast phenomenon for over a century. Recent advances in experiments and computer simulations now provide a coherent mechanistic picture: tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact in complex ways to trigger breakdowns. These insights could improve high-power technologies and make advanced accelerators more reliable and efficient.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025004] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the physics of vacuum breakdown in high-gradient accelerator structures, focusing on surface defects, electric fields, and plasma formation.
motivation: Vacuum breakdown limits the performance of particle accelerators and other high-voltage devices; understanding its mechanism can improve reliability and efficiency.
method: The authors synthesize experimental observations and computer simulations to build a coherent mechanistic picture of the breakdown process.
result: A multi-step mechanism involving surface defects, electrical stress, heating, and particle emission is identified as the trigger for vacuum arcing.
conclusion: Improved understanding of vacuum breakdown can lead to better design of high-power technologies and more reliable accelerators.

title: Colloquium: Multimessenger Astronomy With Continuous Gravitational Waves And Future Detectors
authors: Benjamin J. Owen
abstract:
Author(s): Benjamin J. Owen

The search for continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars represents a key frontier of gravitational-wave astrophysics, with strong connections to electromagnetic astronomy, nuclear astrophysics, and condensed matter physics. This Colloquium discusses the detection prospects for these long-lived yet elusive signals in the upcoming generation of gravitational-wave detectors, emphasizing the importance of simultaneous electromagnetic observations. It also surveys the potential implications of such multimessenger observations for our understanding of the physical and astrophysical processes taking place in the extremely dense environments of their sources.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011002] Published Tue Mar 10, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews the prospects for detecting continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars and their multimessenger connections.
motivation: Continuous gravitational waves are long-lived signals that could reveal properties of neutron stars and dense matter, but they have not yet been detected.
method: The paper surveys detection strategies for upcoming gravitational-wave detectors and discusses simultaneous electromagnetic observations.
result: It outlines the expected sensitivity improvements and the astrophysical insights that multimessenger observations could provide.
conclusion: Multimessenger astronomy with continuous gravitational waves will become a key tool for understanding neutron star interiors and nuclear astrophysics.

title: Neutron Stars And The Dense Matter Equation Of State
authors: Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, And Anna L. Watts
abstract:
Author(s): Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, and Anna L. Watts

Neutron stars, the remnants of supernova explosions, are the densest objects in the Universe. A typical neutron star has a mass between one and two solar masses, and a radius of around 12 km. The density at the center of the star is higher than that in atomic nuclei. As a result, the properties of neutron stars provide important information about the behavior of ordinary matter under extreme compression. In recent years, new information about neutron stars has emerged from two sources. The first is the observation of the gravitational-wave signal from the final inspiral of a coalescing binary neutron star. The second is a careful measurement of the x-ray pulse profile of a spinning neutron star. This review discusses these measurements and summarizes how they constrain masses, radii, and central densities. The results are compared to predictions based on calculations of the nuclear equation of state at densities comparable to that in atomic nuclei, which are then extrapolated to higher density. The review ends with an outlook on future observational opportunities.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045007] Published Wed Dec 24, 2025.
tldr: A review of neutron star observations and the dense matter equation of state, focusing on gravitational waves and X-ray pulse profiles.
motivation: Neutron stars are the densest objects in the universe, and understanding their properties provides insights into the behavior of matter under extreme compression.
method: The paper reviews recent observational results from gravitational-wave signals of binary neutron star mergers and X-ray pulse profile measurements, comparing them to theoretical predictions of the nuclear equation of state.
result: The measurements constrain neutron star masses, radii, and central densities, and are compared to extrapolations of nuclear equation of state calculations.
conclusion: Future observations will further refine our understanding of dense matter, but the paper does not directly address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Order And Disorder At The Atomic Scale: Microscopy Applied To Semiconductors
authors: Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, And Lorenzo Rigutti
abstract:
Author(s): Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, and Lorenzo Rigutti

Atomic-scale details, especially those of disorder, are important for material properties, especially in semiconductors, but they are also extremely difficult to measure. Real-space methods can give direct access to this information, but typically, that access is limited. This review reports the application of three real-space techniques for measuring disorder to compound semiconductor materials: scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy. Where possible, it emphasizes cases in which the probes have been combined to achieve a more complete picture of the defects.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025006] Published Thu Jun 26, 2025.
tldr: A review of real-space microscopy techniques for measuring atomic-scale disorder in semiconductors.
motivation: Atomic-scale disorder critically affects semiconductor properties but is difficult to measure; the paper reviews three real-space techniques to address this challenge.
method: The review covers scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy, emphasizing combined use for a complete defect picture.
result: The paper summarizes capabilities and limitations of each technique and highlights cases where combining them yields more comprehensive disorder characterization.
conclusion: Real-space microscopy techniques, especially when combined, provide direct access to atomic-scale disorder in semiconductors, which is essential for understanding material properties.

title: Quantum Physics Of Stars
authors: M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. Deboer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, And A. Tumino
abstract:
Author(s): M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. deBoer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, and A. Tumino

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025003] Published Tue May 27, 2025.
tldr: A review of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars, focusing on quantum tunneling and resonances.
motivation: Nuclear reactions at stellar energies are difficult to measure and require quantum mechanical understanding.
method: Summarizes theoretical approaches for low-energy nuclear reactions, including tunneling and resonance models.
result: Describes the state of the art in theory and new experimental ideas.
conclusion: Quantum mechanics governs stellar nuclear reactions, but the paper is not relevant to the user's research directions.

title: The Need For Optoacoustic Microscopy
authors: Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, And Vasilis Ntziachristos
abstract:
Author(s): Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, and Vasilis Ntziachristos

Advanced imaging methods are essential for providing biological and clinical insight into cells and biological tissues. Optoacoustic imaging is one such method in which cells or tissues absorb short laser pulses and the resulting rise in temperature creates tiny ultrasound waves that can be detected by ultrasonic detectors placed outside the specimen. This noninvasive technique has the ability to look at optical contrast that is millimeters and even centimeters deep with high resolution. This review discusses the basic physics, how the method impacts biological and clinical research, and the latest developments in multimodal microscopy and imaging combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015005] Published Tue Mar 04, 2025.
tldr: A review of optoacoustic microscopy, a biomedical imaging technique using laser-induced ultrasound.
motivation: To provide an overview of optoacoustic imaging, its physics, and its applications in biological and clinical research.
method: Review of basic physics, instrumentation, and multimodal approaches combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.
result: Discusses the ability to image optical contrast at depth with high resolution, and highlights recent developments.
conclusion: Optoacoustic microscopy is a valuable noninvasive imaging method for deep-tissue biological and clinical studies.

title: Wannier-function Software Ecosystem For Materials Simulations
authors: Antimo Marrazzo, Sophie Beck, Elena R. Margine, Nicola Marzari, Arash A. Mostofi, Junfeng Qiao, Ivo Souza, Stepan S. Tsirkin, Jonathan R. Yates, And Giovanni Pizzi
abstract:
Author(s): Antimo Marrazzo, Sophie Beck, Elena R. Margine, Nicola Marzari, Arash A. Mostofi, Junfeng Qiao, Ivo Souza, Stepan S. Tsirkin, Jonathan R. Yates, and Giovanni Pizzi

The description of the electronic structure in terms of extended Bloch states has made it possible to understand and calculate many properties in condensed-matter physics. However, understanding and insight often require a local description, and Wannier functions provide an exact and insightful map of extended reciprocal-space Bloch states into localized real-space orbitals. Applications range far and wide, from ultra-accurate integrations to topological invariants, and their widespread uptake by the electronic-structure community has resulted in a growing and interoperable ecosystem of methods and associated software tools. This review provides a description of this ecosystem that has now become a major instrument for the electronic-structure community in its pursuit of understanding, discovering, and designing materials.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 96, 045008] Published Mon Dec 23, 2024.
tldr: A review of the Wannier-function software ecosystem for materials simulations.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive overview of the methods and tools based on Wannier functions for electronic structure calculations.
method: The paper surveys the ecosystem of software that constructs and uses Wannier functions, including Wannier90 and related codes.
result: It describes how Wannier functions enable accurate integrations, topological invariants, and other materials properties.
conclusion: The Wannier-function ecosystem is a major instrument for the electronic-structure community.

result: The fractional centrality reduces to out-degree centrality when α=1, and exhibits non-local behavior for other α values.
conclusion: The proposed measure provides a new tool for analyzing directed networks, but its relevance to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems is not established.

[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064307] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spatial correlations in SIS epidemic models on random regular graphs, a topic in statistical physics of networks.
motivation: Understanding how network structure affects epidemic spread and the role of spatial correlations in SIS models.

result: Derived expressions for spatial correlations and showed that they significantly impact epidemic thresholds and prevalence.
conclusion: Spatial correlations are crucial for accurate modeling of SIS dynamics on networks, and pair approximation captures key features.

conclusion: The reoriented potential mixer can improve mixing in trapped regions, aiding remediation efforts.

result: They identify conditions for multistability and characterize bifurcation scenarios in the network.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the design principles of multistable gene circuits.

title: Influence Of Visual Field Offset On Collective Behavior: An Exploration Using The Two-dimensional Vicsek Model
authors: Poorendra Ramlall, Sachit Butail, And Subhradeep Roy
abstract:
Author(s): Poorendra Ramlall, Sachit Butail, and Subhradeep Roy

This study investigates the influence of visual field offset—a restricted field of vision positioned at a fixed angle from an agent's heading direction—on collective behavior using the Vicsek model. This offset shapes an agent's ability to perceive and respond to neighbors, thereby impacting overall…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064409] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how a fixed visual field offset affects collective motion in the Vicsek model, a classical model of self-propelled particles.
motivation: Understanding how sensory limitations, such as a restricted field of view, influence emergent collective behavior in animal groups or robotic swarms.
method: Numerical simulations of the two-dimensional Vicsek model with agents having a visual field offset—a fixed angular shift between heading and visual direction.
result: The visual field offset alters the onset and nature of collective motion, affecting order parameters and clustering dynamics.
conclusion: Visual field offset is a significant parameter in collective behavior, with implications for biological and robotic systems.

title: Enhanced Plasma Production By Ambipolar Electric Fields In Convergent Magnetic Fields

Controlled unidirectional remote plasma production in a radio-frequency (rf) plasma source is demonstrated by placing magnetic nozzle throat several tens of centimeters away from the rf antenna, where a local density peak forms near the throat. The experiment indicates that the dominant electron ene…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023322] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies plasma production in a convergent magnetic field using ambipolar electric fields, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To understand and control remote plasma production for applications like electric propulsion.
method: Experimental measurements of plasma density and electron energy in a radio-frequency plasma source with a magnetic nozzle.
result: A local density peak forms near the magnetic nozzle throat, indicating enhanced plasma production via ambipolar electric fields.

title: Proof-of-principle Experiment Of A Beam Extraction Over Millions Of Turns Using Stable Resonance Islands And Bent Crystal
authors: D. E. Veres, P. Arrutia, S. Cettour Cave, B. H. F. Lindström, M. Giovannozzi, L. E. Pauwels, F. F. van der Veken, F. M. Velotti, And G. Franchetti
abstract:
Author(s): D. E. Veres, P. Arrutia, S. Cettour Cave, B. H. F. Lindström, M. Giovannozzi, L. E. Pauwels, F. F. Van der Veken, F. M. Velotti, and G. Franchetti

A recent theoretical investigation indicated that combining particle trapping in resonance islands with planar channeling in a bent crystal may offer a promising option for a low-loss, or even septum-free, slow-extraction technique. This work reports on the successful proof-of-principle experiment conducted at the CERN Super Proton Synchrotron, in which stable islands and a bent crystal were employed to split and channel a circulating beam onto an absorber, thereby emulating slow extraction.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022055] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a proof-of-principle experiment for beam extraction using resonance islands and a bent crystal at CERN's Super Proton Synchrotron.
motivation: To develop a low-loss, septum-free slow-extraction technique for particle accelerators, which could improve efficiency and reduce activation of components.
method: The experiment combines particle trapping in stable resonance islands with planar channeling in a bent crystal to split and channel a circulating proton beam onto an absorber.
result: Successful proof-of-principle demonstration of beam extraction over millions of turns using the combined technique.
conclusion: The method shows promise for low-loss slow extraction in high-intensity accelerators, but further development is needed for practical application.

title: Plasma Flow Generation And Particle Acceleration From Expanding Magnetic Bubbles

result: A rising current expels plasma and generates fast flows and energetic particles.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into plasma dynamics in astrophysical contexts and laboratory setups.

title: Leidenfrost Hydrogels: Elastic Surface-wave Instability And Sustained Bouncing
authors: Nathan C. J. Coombs, Peter Lewin-Jones, Mykyta V. Chubynsky, And James E. Sprittles

This work investigates the oscillatory dynamics and subsequent sustained bouncing behavior of Leidenfrost hydrogels, a phenomenon that has received little theoretical attention to date. Building on previous approaches toward drop impacts and Leidenfrost drops, a computational model is developed to capture the oscillatory dynamics and analyze the mechanism of energy injection that leads to sustained bouncing.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022052] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the oscillatory dynamics and sustained bouncing of Leidenfrost hydrogels, a soft matter physics phenomenon.
motivation: To understand the mechanism of energy injection that leads to sustained bouncing of Leidenfrost hydrogels, which has received little theoretical attention.
method: A computational model is developed to capture the oscillatory dynamics and analyze the energy injection mechanism.
result: The model reveals an elastic surface-wave instability that sustains bouncing.
conclusion: The work provides theoretical insight into the sustained bouncing of Leidenfrost hydrogels.

title: Tracking Phase Synchronization Between Flagella In The Time-frequency Domain Resolves Photophobic Response

This work aims to study the resynchronization of CR flagella after a high light intensity stimulus, known as photoshock. The synchronization is estimated thanks to a qu…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023294] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies flagellar synchronization in Chlamydomonas reinhardtii using time-frequency analysis to characterize photophobic response.
motivation: Understanding how microalgae coordinate flagella after light stimuli is important for biophysics and cellular behavior.
method: The authors use time-frequency domain analysis to track phase synchronization between two flagella from high-speed video recordings.
result: They quantify resynchronization dynamics after a photoshock and identify characteristic timescales.
conclusion: The method provides a robust way to study flagellar coordination and its response to environmental cues.

title: Super-resonance: Breaking The Bandwidth Limit Of Resonant Modes And Its Application To Flow Control
authors: Adam R. Harris, Armin Kianfar, David Roca, Daniel Yago, Christoph Brehm, And Mahmoud I. Hussein
abstract:

Super-resonance maintains a broadband out-of-phase response well beyond the characteristic bandwidth of conventional resonance, enabling broadband flow stabilization among other applications.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021045] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces super-resonance, a phenomenon that breaks the bandwidth limit of resonant modes, and applies it to flow control.
motivation: Conventional resonance has a limited bandwidth, which restricts its application in areas like flow control. The authors aim to overcome this limitation.
method: The authors theoretically and experimentally demonstrate super-resonance, achieving a broadband out-of-phase response beyond the characteristic bandwidth of conventional resonance.
result: Super-resonance maintains a broadband out-of-phase response, enabling broadband flow stabilization among other applications.
conclusion: Super-resonance provides a new paradigm for resonant systems, with potential applications in flow control and beyond.

title: Using Folded Proteins As Mechanically Well-Defined Units To Understand Fatigue Fracture In Hydrogels: Bridging Single Molecule And Bulk Studies
authors: Liang Dong, Puyu Cao, Huiyan Chen, Yu Zhang, Ying Li, Bin Chen, Yi Cao, And Hai Lei

motivation: Understanding fatigue fracture in soft materials is crucial for designing durable hydrogels, but the molecular mechanisms are poorly understood.
method: The authors use folded proteins as model units to probe mechanical fatigue at the single-molecule level and connect to bulk hydrogel behavior via a force-response model.
result: They identify how protein unfolding and refolding cycles contribute to fatigue fracture and propose design strategies for fatigue-resistant hydrogels.
conclusion: The work provides a molecular-level understanding of fatigue in hydrogels and offers a design principle for tougher soft materials.

motivation: Understanding how mechanical forces at topological defects in curved epithelial sheets lead to cell extrusion is important for tissue biology and disease.

title: Seeing New Depths: Three-Dimensional Flow Of A Free-Swimming Alga
authors: Gregorius Pradipta, Wanho Lee, van Tran, Kyle Welch, Santosh K. Sankar, Yongsam Kim, Satish Kumar, Xin Yong, Jiarong Hong, Sookkyung Lim, And Xiang Cheng

Experimental three-dimensional measurements of the flow field around a free-swimming microalga reveal that microscopic organisms generate unexpected low-Reynolds-number flow phenomena, expanding our understanding of microhydrodynamics with profound biological implications for microbial motility and physiology.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021019] Published Fri Apr 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents experimental 3D measurements of the flow field around a free-swimming microalga, revealing unexpected low-Reynolds-number flow phenomena.
motivation: To understand the hydrodynamics of microbial motility, which has biological implications for nutrient uptake and predator-prey interactions.
method: Experimental three-dimensional flow measurements using particle tracking velocimetry around a free-swimming alga.
result: The flow field exhibits complex three-dimensional structures not captured by previous 2D models.
